adventure.title: The Bell Beneath Harrowgate
adventure.synopsis: Three nights running, the Deep Bell has sounded beneath Harrowgate with no rope and no ringer. Dust rises before each toll. Wells climb their walls. People above wake holding memories lost by people below. The Ember Company descended under a secret, conditional recovery contract; Factor Orren Saye then trusted an abridged royal sequence and cut the chain carrying the Crown's live load. The buried house is now passing strain among water, ward-light, memory, command, and counterweight systems. The adventurers must rescue the scattered expedition, learn whom each system has been spending, and choose an ending: repair the old burden, replace it, divide it, collapse it, free the Crown, or bargain with the listener beneath the fault. Every answer needs a bearer and a route.
adventure.premise: The Deep Bell is drawing breath for a fourth toll, and each broken cycle closes faster. Two descents remain open. Survivors are scattered below. Every repair shifts danger into another system. Enter the buried house, learn what its safety has cost, and decide which burdens Harrowgate will carry in public.
adventure.explanation:
The Deep Bell is a pressure engine built around Queen Avarra's coerced surrender. Her Crown of Measure became clapper, counterweight, and legal authority: one person made the junction between mountain strain and public command. Later custodians diverted part of every toll's mnemonic cost into the labor community now called the Low Choir.

Five days ago, Lady Merrow Vey's trust hired the Ember Company to verify the Crown and recover it only after the buried house was made safe. Her chief factor, Halren Coss, secretly accepted Councilor Samet Rhun's possession rider: take the Crown before Harrowgate could assert custody, and Rhun would supplement the fee from town debts pledged against it. Rhun also supplied an abridged extraction schedule. It called the Crown Drum's outer chain a release restraint and omitted the three operations that would have exposed its live load. Orren Saye knew he was racing public notice. Captain Maelin Rook saw all three drums under strain and refused the cut. Their struggle severed the chain, reversed the Water Drum, and left the Memory Drum half-braked.

The first toll passed for quarry settlement. After the second, Harrowgate closed wells and signaled both entrances. The third collapsed a tenement. At dawn, a dying porter named Orren's order and Rook's refusal. Only then did the council know the cause and possess a public mandate for another descent. Tarrow expects the shortening cycle to close again before midnight.

The broken house now shifts strain among water, light, memory, command, and weight. Lady Vey can repudiate the rider and chain cut, but not the secret expedition that enabled them. No ending restores safety and justice together. Rescue, route preparation, preserved evidence, and voluntary obligations determine what can be saved—and who may still refuse the settlement.

references.title: The Salt Wardens
references.summary: Salt-preserved officers divided over whether to continue, replace, or end the Deep Bell's inherited burden.
references.content:
## Personhood and maintenance

A Salt Warden is a maintained person whose continuity depends on a preserved shell, a salt memory tablet, and witnesses who recognize the relation between them. A shell can obey without weighing exceptions; a tablet can recite records without deciding what its remembered feelings mean. Repair may preserve uncertainty, but theft, forced transfer, or missing witnesses makes identity and authority disputed.

## Present division

The Continuance faction, represented by Sister Vesra Quill, would repair people and machine before any release. Prior Dalca's Release faction argues that the old sentence has expired and that repair must not renew captivity. Literal-order Wardens obey the last command they recognize. Prefect Ardel Quoin's missing command tablet and sealed shell leave all three positions without an undisputed commander.

## Command, bargains, and refusal

Wardens recognize declared burden, witnessed duty, valid command tablets, and bounded orders. They can supply disciplined labor, Wells crews, route seals, command keys, tablet repair, and testimony. They require every new duty to identify its scope and remedy; an alliance that merely restores obedience without resolving consent repeats the buried house's original failure.

references.title: Lady Merrow Vey
references.summary: The last acknowledged royal descendant: lawful sponsor of the secret recovery expedition, holder of a genuine but bounded Crown claim, and principal able to bind House Vey but not Harrowgate or the buried communities.
references.content:
## Claim and complicity

Lady Merrow Vey is the last acknowledged descendant of Harrowgate's buried kings and the principal of the recovery trust that hired the Ember Company. Her written contract authorized a quiet survey and Crown recovery only after the buried house was made safe, with witnessed transfer and no damage to the Bell. She did not authorize Councilor Rhun's possession rider, Halren Coss's second payment schedule, or Orren Saye's chain cut. Her secrecy, money, seals, and chosen agents nevertheless created the opportunity for all three.

## What she wants

Vey wants Harrowgate stabilized and the Crown of Measure returned to House Vey afterward. She treats the Crown as stolen dynastic property, but the surviving genealogies give her a genuine custody claim rather than exclusive authority over Avarra, the Bell, or every burden attached to them. She may repudiate the concealed rider and Orren's method without becoming innocent of the expedition.

## What her seal can bind

Vey may bind House Vey's grain stores, retainers, genealogy archive, money, warrants, and claim. She may lend genealogy seals, delegate an agent, support evacuation or maintenance, and accept divided or supervised custody. She cannot bind Harrowgate's elected officers, the Salt Wardens, Low Choir households, Queen Avarra's retained will, or another blood line. Her present concessions, resources committed, and final Crown position remain matters for play.

references.title: Captain Maelin Rook
references.summary: The Ember Company captain who refused Orren's loaded chain cut, keeps rescue and stabilization ahead of possession, and can command surviving Company hands without deciding their public judgment.
references.content:
## Command and the Company split

Captain Maelin Rook commanded the Ember Company's descent. At the Ropeworks she saw live strain on the Crown, Water, and Memory drums and refused Orren Saye's order to cut the outer royal chain. Orren proceeded under the abridged sequence, and the expedition divided around the refusal. Rook's counter-orders, field signs, restrained demolition work, and care for the wounded preserve a second Company account of the failure.

## Priorities and manner

Rook puts rescue and stabilization before Crown possession. She wants the concealed rider, incomplete sequence, and divided responsibility entered into the public record. She is practical about dangerous work and unsentimental about command, but she will not let surface patrons or buried authorities use the emergency to discard her people before their conduct is heard.

## Orders she will give

Rook may command Ember personnel who still recognize her, coordinate rigging and rescue labor, authenticate Company field practice, and negotiate a disciplined withdrawal or renewed operation. She cannot bind Lady Vey, Harrowgate, the Salt Wardens, or Company members who have deserted or chosen Orren. Her survival, location, available crew, injuries, and disposition remain encounter and play-state questions.

references.title: Factor Orren Saye
references.summary: The Ember factor who knowingly used a concealed possession rider and abridged sequence to order the loaded royal chain cut, yet remains a negotiable source of evidence, routes, labor, and dangerous leverage.
references.content:
## Office and decision

Factor Orren Saye led the Ember Company's Crown party under Lady Vey's base contract and Chief Factor Halren Coss's concealed payment schedule. He knew Councilor Rhun's possession rider required physical custody before public notice and accepted an extraction sequence missing the Crown Drum's unload and synchronization operations. When Captain Maelin Rook refused the cut, Orren ordered the loaded outer chain severed anyway.

## Position

Orren believes Harrowgate's authorities, the buried custodians, and the royal house all use records selectively, and that possession of the Crown is the only leverage none can quietly erase. He is controlled, exact, and willing to bargain. He points correctly to concealed history and divided responsibility while refusing to let those truths excuse his own decision.

## Leverage without title

Orren may offer the rider, payment schedule, royal sequence plate, Company testimony, route knowledge, loyalist labor, and ordinary salvage. He may seek temporary claimant recognition or negotiate Crown custody. He cannot bind Lady Vey, Chief Factor Coss, Harrowgate, the Salt Wardens, or Queen Avarra, and possession alone does not settle title or repair the Bell. His location, allies, custody, survival, and later bargains remain matters for play.

references.title: Engineer Pell Varo
references.summary: The Ember field engineer who reads the buried house as linked load systems and can coordinate major repairs without pretending that engineering removes their human or political cost.
references.content:
## Trade and knowledge

Engineer Pell Varo is the Ember Company's principal field engineer below Harrowgate. He reads the three Ropeworks drums as one burden-transfer system, understands the Counterweight Wells' separate questions of mass, path, and timing, and marked the brake windows that govern a toll. His surviving notes connect routes, load lines, and repair operations across the buried house.

## Priorities

Pell wants survivors extracted and enough of the machinery stabilized to prevent a catastrophic toll. He is furious that Orren treated an incomplete sequence as permission to move a live load. He has no independent claim to the Crown and does not pretend that an engineering operation can decide who ought to bear its political or mnemonic cost.

## Repairs he can answer for

Pell may diagnose machinery, explain displaced burdens, coordinate a complex movement, and perform major field work when supplied with tools, access, protection, and supporting crews. He cannot make a burden disappear or promise that one repair leaves every other system safe. His injuries, availability, completed jobs, remaining capacity, and chosen route remain encounter and play-state questions.

references.title: Queen Avarra
aliases: Avarra of the Crown of Measure
references.summary: The conquered sovereign whose coerced Crown became the Deep Bell's command and load junction; her divided faculties can measure, refuse, and witness but cannot rule the present or choose justice for others.
references.content:
## Sovereign and sentence

Queen Avarra ruled before Aldren Harrow's conquest. During the siege she mistook the fault's response to royal cadence for obedience. Her later surrender was limited, witnessed, and coerced; the Crown of Measure was then made clapper, counterweight, and command authority within the Deep Bell. The indefinite hereditary sentence and the transfer of mnemonic cost to the Low Choir were later additions, not terms she granted.

## Retained faculties

Avarra does not survive as one complete person waiting inside the Crown. Measure, Refusal, and Witness persist across the Crown, Iron Choir, surrender records, and inherited testimony. Reconstructed together, they can compare burdens, reject commands made through her Crown, and testify to the original limits. They know later history only through memories fed into the machine.

## Terms she will not leave implicit

Avarra wants her sentence ended without coercing another person into her place. She may aid a replacement, distributed settlement, controlled collapse, royal unbinding, or a bounded emergency continuance with a real end and remedy. Her retained will can influence old mechanisms and the Mouth's learned cadence, but it cannot rule present Harrowgate, erase other claims, or certify that efficiency is justice. Whether her faculties are reconstructed, separated, carried, freed, suppressed, or lost remains a matter for play.

references.title: Chief Factor Halren Coss
references.summary: The Ember Company chief factor who converted Lady Vey's conditional recovery into a concealed race for possession and issued the second payment schedule used below Harrowgate.
references.content:
## Office and concealed escalation

Chief Factor Halren Coss is the senior Ember Company officer behind the Harrowgate expedition. Lady Merrow Vey's written contract authorized survey and recovery only after the buried house was stabilized. Coss privately accepted Councilor Samet Rhun's accelerated-possession rider, used Vey's seal to issue a second payment schedule, and rewarded physical custody before public notice.

## Evidence and responsibility

The waxed contract case, Company testimony, and complete extraction plates can establish that Coss exceeded the authority in Vey's copy. They do not by themselves establish what Vey knew before the disaster. Coss's concealed schedule explains Orren Saye's incentives without excusing Orren's loaded chain cut or making the wider Company equally culpable.

## Accounts that bind him

Coss can answer for Company accounts, deputies, schedules, and institutional liability. His office may offer records, money, personnel, or a settlement if he later enters play. It cannot turn possession into title, bind House Vey or Harrowgate, validate Rhun's debt claim, or erase Captain Rook's counter-order. His knowledge, later response, and willingness to repair the harm remain open.

references.title: Councilor Samet Rhun
references.summary: A Harrowgate councilor and creditor who supplied the debt rider and abridged royal sequence meant to turn rapid Crown possession into security for town obligations.
references.content:
## Creditor and councilor

Councilor Samet Rhun is a Harrowgate creditor with civic standing but no independent royal or custodial title. He proposed treating physical possession of the Crown of Measure as security for town debt, supplied an accelerated-possession rider, and required custody before public notice.

## The abridged sequence

Rhun also supplied the royal extraction copy used by Orren Saye. It labels the outer Crown chain as a release restraint while omitting the unload and synchronization operations that reveal live burden on the Crown Drum. The complete Ropeworks and Scriptorium records expose the omissions; they do not prove that every person who handled the copy understood them.

## A creditor claim without custody

Rhun may advance a creditor claim, answer for his rider, and influence Harrowgate politics. He cannot pledge the whole town without lawful public authority, bind Lady Vey or the Ember Company beyond accepted agreements, convert the Crown into ordinary collateral, or decide which buried community bears the debt. His later political position and accountability remain open.

references.title: Prefect Ardel Quoin
references.summary: The last undisputed Salt Warden commander, whose voluntary tablet removal preserved evidence of a lawful release clause while leaving command and personal continuity incomplete.
references.content:
## Inquiry and removal

Prefect Ardel Quoin was the last undisputed commander of the Salt Wardens. He opened an inquiry into whether their inherited sentence had reached its end condition. After learning that the original compact permitted release when an accepted replacement burden existed, Quoin asked a Garden keeper to remove his command tablet before literal-order officers could suppress the finding.

## Incomplete continuity

Quoin's shell remains sealed beneath the Barracks command chair while his cracked tablet is rooted in the Garden's Bitter Bed. The tablet remembers the inquiry, the release clause, and consent to removal, but not the keeper's face, the final vote, or several surrounding years. It may be read, repaired, restored, or kept as an independent witness without making any option a perfect recovery.

## Command after interruption

A sufficiently witnessed restoration can support temporary joint command, a final muster, and bounded stabilization or replacement orders. Quoin will not compel Wardens to dissolve or surrender the Crown to a private claimant. His damaged testimony cannot prove which present faction deserves command, and his current shell, tablet, witnesses, repair, and chosen form of continuity remain matters for play.

references.title: Keeper Odran Greve
references.summary: The last living-born keeper of the Chain Scriptorium, carrying more than a century of returned working memory and guarding the context that makes buried records intelligible.
references.content:
## Keeper of burden records

Odran Greve is the last living-born Keeper of the Chain Scriptorium. He survives inside its rotating index cage after the archive returned more than a century of working memories to him. He speaks as if each sentence needs a hook and shelf because several offices still press their unfinished duties through his memory.

## Knowledge and custody

Odran can trace water, royal, memory, execution, maintenance, personhood, Menagerie, and emergency-descent records by the burdens they governed. He knows the Crown's coerced repurposing, the later transfer of mnemonic cost to the Low Choir, the accepted-burden precedent, and the relationship among the three genealogies. He can expose omissions in Orren's sequence and open several record-defined routes.

## What stays on the chains

Odran may interpret plates, authenticate their physical order, lend a bounded record set, and provide maintenance testimony. He will not surrender the whole archive at once: removing records without their hanging context can make theft look like proof and can physically destroy the index. His survival, evacuation, plates removed, routes opened, and memories retained remain encounter and play-state questions.

references.title: Tavia Hest
references.summary: A blinded Ember Company scout whose touch-reading of route chalk, dark-route discipline, and testimony about the overlapping contract remain useful beyond her rescue.
references.content:
## Scout and witness

Tavia Hest is an Ember Company scout who survived the Lantern Cistern by tying herself to a valve standard after a flare burned her eyes. She can identify Company route chalk by touch and testify that Orren ordered Corven Braid to carry a second contract sealed by Chief Factor Halren Coss.

## Priorities and capabilities

Tavia wants Corven recovered, the lower ward marks denied to Orren, and wounded Company members treated as people rather than discarded accomplices. Once her face is washed and the burned cloth is changed, her sight returns gradually. Even before then she can guide dark routes, find the Reliquary water lift, range ahead without losing direction, and assist survivor extraction.

## Sight, testimony, and dependence

Tavia's testimony establishes a second contract and Company route practice; it does not prove every term, Vey's prior knowledge, or Orren's final location. Her injuries, treatment, mobility, confidence, current route, and willingness to continue remain changing state.

references.title: Rhea Colm
references.summary: An Ember Company surgeon and trained witness whose triage, mnemonic diagnosis, and contract testimony connect the Reliquary rescue to later survivor care and public evidence.
references.content:
## Surgeon in Returning Breath

Rhea Colm is an Ember Company surgeon trapped with a crushed leg inside the Saint of Returning Breath. She used the shared air manifold to preserve another wounded person's name and can distinguish ordinary shock from imposed or contaminated memory. She speaks in triage order: who is breathing, who can be moved, and which testimony will worsen if delayed.

## Knowledge and aims

Rhea knows that Orren's loyalists took the royal niche route, Captain Rook followed rather than abandoning the wounded, and a dead clerk carried papers under a second Vey seal that did not match the main contract. She wants the Common Measure preserved and Orren returned alive if possible. Her recurring question is practical: what takes the weight when the gold is removed?

## Breath, triage, and proof

If rescued, Rhea can stabilize survivors, identify drowned bodies, diagnose mnemonic contamination, read medical and recognition protocols, and provide a careful account of the Company split. She does not authenticate every contract term or settle responsibility by herself. Her remaining air, injury, rescue, later location, patients, and willingness to aid the expedition remain changing state.

references.title: Nara-of-the-Seventh-Name
references.summary: A Low Choir compact advocate who carries seven names without treating inherited duty as ownership of the bearer.
references.content:
## Seven names, one bearer

Nara Vale was born with one name and now carries six names lost during earlier tolls: Mere, Hama, Voss, Rill, Tett, and Orra. She does not claim to be those people. She keeps their names alive so unfinished kinship, contracts, debts, and testimony still have a living address. Her title places her own name seventh and warns against mistaking inherited duty for ownership of the bearer.

## The Kept Chain

Nara speaks for the Kept Chain households within the Low Choir. They preserve cups, duty weights, surface correspondence, witnesses, and the practical labor needed to fit a replacement burden. She tests every proposal by operators, gate hours, food, inspection, signatures, stop conditions, and remedies. She accepts bounded emergency continuance when it buys time for rescue and a real transition; she rejects an indefinite promise to reform after Harrowgate is safe.

## What one advocate can bind

Nara is a principal compact advocate, not the Low Choir's queen. The Warm Table, Open Cup, Kept Chain, and Narrow Line overlap without surrendering their separate consent. She can offer her households' witnesses, three voluntary weights, liturgy, records, and labor. She cannot bind every buried household, certify a coerced Common Measure, or waive another claimant's route, memory, Crown, or maintenance interest. Her location, current support, delegated representative, and final settlement remain live play state.

references.title: The Ember Company
references.summary: The contracted expeditionary company divided between Captain Rook's rescue-first counter-order and Factor Orren's concealed race for Crown possession.
references.content:
## Contracted expedition

The Ember Company is a survey, salvage, engineering, and recovery outfit hired through Lady Merrow Vey's recovery trust. Its main crew entered under a conditional contract requiring stabilization and witnessed transfer before Crown recovery. Chief Factor Halren Coss's concealed payment schedule and Councilor Rhun's rider created a second incentive that not every Company member saw.

## The split below Harrowgate

At the Ropeworks, Captain Maelin Rook refused to cut a loaded royal chain. Factor Orren Saye proceeded under the abridged sequence, and the expedition divided. Company chalk, route ledgers, rigging, tools, testimony, and surviving crews preserve both the possession party and Rook's rescue-first counter-account. Membership does not make every survivor equally informed or culpable.

## Officers, contracts, and liability

Recognized officers may direct Company personnel who still accept their command, authenticate field practice, supply labor and tools, and negotiate withdrawal, repair, or liability. The Company cannot bind Lady Vey, Harrowgate, the Salt Wardens, the Low Choir, or Queen Avarra, and its contract does not create title by possession. Current survivors, injuries, loyalties, custody, equipment, and reconciliation remain play state.

references.title: The Low Choir
references.summary: The living descendant community beneath Harrowgate whose names, memories, labor, and households have borne the Deep Bell's hidden mnemonic cost for generations.
references.content:
## A living community, not a mechanism

The Low Choir descends from workers, prisoners, petitioners, and households kept below the old royal machine. Later custodians redirected the Deep Bell's mnemonic cost into their names and memories. The community preserves people through households, memory cups, inherited names, work, witness, and chosen obligation; it is not identical with the Iron Choir apparatus that stores and speaks extracted voices.

## Households and positions

Low Choir households disagree about refuge, passage, continued maintenance, Crown custody, public return, and the meaning of inherited names. The Feast of Empty Chairs makes four broad positions visible, but no caucus or speaker owns every household. Their compact practice asks who witnesses, who may pass, what is provided, who maintains it, where the limit lies, and what remedy follows failure.

## Households bind themselves

Households can bind their own stores, routes, witnesses, memories, labor, and continuing duties. Named representatives can negotiate only within the standing they actually hold. No single speaker can surrender every memory, accept a new hereditary burden for all, or make Harrowgate's promises true by reciting them. Current household positions, rescued names, cups, casualties, routes, and final compact remain matters for play.

references.title: The Chain Scriptorium
references.summary: A burden-indexed brass archive whose moving chains preserve maintenance law, dynastic claims, condemned promises, and the context needed to distinguish evidence from extraction.
references.content:
## Archive by burden

The Chain Scriptorium stores plans, judgments, repair orders, successions, and condemned promises on hanging brass plates. Records are indexed by the burdens and offices they governed rather than by ordinary geography. At its reading post, a declared purpose brings forward the records historically used by people claiming the same duty.

## Chains, routes, and proof

Water records hang low, royal plates high, and memory records warm on silvered links. Chain families connect the Ropeworks, Barracks, Reliquary, Feast, Chapel, King's Narrow Grave, Iron Choir, and controlled-collapse routes. The three genealogies distinguish blood custody, maintained obligation, and Avarra's retained surrender terms.

## What removal costs

The Scriptorium can expose omitted operations, open record-defined routes, supply maintenance plates, and preserve evidence of alternatives and abuses. It does not answer questions without the duty implied by them. Removing plates changes what can later be proved, and stripping a chain family destroys the physical index that gives a record meaning. Its current damage, plates removed, routes opened, and keeper remain changing state.

references.title: The Feast of Empty Chairs
references.summary: The Low Choir's inhabited refuge and negotiating hall, where empty places, memory cups, inherited names, and six compact weights make obligation visible.
references.content:
## Refuge and table

The Feast of Empty Chairs is a living Low Choir hall rather than a memorial ruin. Occupied tables feed households and workers; empty chairs hold places for people absent, forgotten, endangered, or still claimed by duty. The hall tests visitors through whom they return, whom they name, and which absence they are willing to acknowledge.

## Cups, names, and compact

Memory cups allow listening, witnessed stabilization, voluntary carrying, return, redirection, and toll shielding. Inherited names are chosen standings and duties, not ownership of the bearer. Negotiation uses six compact weights: witness, passage, provision, maintenance, limit, and remedy. Different households may accept different combinations.

## What the hall can promise

The Feast can provide refuge, food, guides, witnesses, memory practice, household commitments, and maintainers for a future settlement. No table or representative binds every household, and no dramatic promise substitutes for a named limit and remedy. Current chairs, cups, positions, stores, guests, promises, and hostility remain changing state.

references.title: The King's Narrow Grave
references.summary: A narrowing royal claim chamber and treasury where three incompatible genealogies, the retained king's voice, and material Crown assets divide custody from command.
references.content:
## Three successions

The King's Narrow Grave protects three valid genealogies with different jurisdictions. The Golden Branch supports blood custody through House Vey. The Burden Chain tracks succession through maintained obligation. The Ash Witness preserves limits on Queen Avarra's surrender and later royal alterations. None grants complete ownership of the Crown, the Bell, or the people below.

## Voice, defenses, and treasury

Aldren Harrow's retained command voice tests claimants through narrowing walls, gilt mourners, indivisible commands, and a coffin knight. The treasury contains crown-bars, a royal brake sequence, chain-splice material, maintenance and resettlement funds, ceremonial goods, and records of debt. These assets can become proof, repair material, counterweight mass, public remedy, or private treasure.

## What each claim can open

The Grave can recognize limited standing, release specific resources, and expose the difference among custody, maintenance, surrender, and creditor claims. It grants no throne and does not settle Harrowgate's future by opening. Current defenders, Orren's position, damaged genealogies, bars removed, treasury custody, and routes remain changing state.

references.title: The Counterweight Wells
references.summary: Three linked shaft-and-brake systems that force every proposed Bell solution to separate mass, load path, and timing before anyone calls it balanced.
references.content:
## Three different requirements

The Counterweight Wells are three vertical load systems joined to the buried house. The Royal Well governs Crown mass and dynastic mechanisms. The Civic Well governs streets, foundations, and public works. The Funerary Well governs mnemonic and mortuary paths. A correct mass in the wrong Well or at the wrong time remains a failure.

## Operations and irreversible choices

Crews can brace a Well, exchange load, install an accepted burden, remove Crown load, conduct a temporary human hold, or drop one Well permanently. Royal, Civic, and Funerary drops send force into different routes and create different physical, political, and mnemonic losses. The Wells reveal rather than erase where a proposed solution sends its cost.

## What every transfer spends

The Wells can provide mass, path, timing, brake access, and a test of whether an operation closes its physical account. They cannot create consent, maintenance, memory justice, or replacement material. Their current strain, crews, plates, brake houses, suspended loads, dropped shafts, and available routes remain authoritative in the operating ledger and play state.

references.title: The Deep Bell
references.summary: The buried sovereign machine that converts mountain strain into water, counterweight, command, and mnemonic burdens through a four-phase toll.
references.content:
## What the Bell does

The Deep Bell is a vertical pressure machine built around the Crown of Measure. Its cycle takes breath, draws load from connected systems, lowers the Crown as clapper and command junction, and sounds into Harrowgate. Later alterations made the Low Choir the nearest open mnemonic path, turning repeated stabilization into inherited human cost.

## Four phases and connected systems

Taking Breath gathers pressure. Drawing Load pulls through water, roots, foundations, Wells, and memory. Crown Descent brings physical mass and recognized authority into the bell cage. Sounding releases what the previous phases assigned. Ropeworks drums, ward-light, the Reliquary, Garden, Chapel, Wells, Iron Choir, Black Rain, and the Mouth all change what the cycle receives and where it returns force.

## Repairs, endings, and named costs

The Bell can be held, repaired, supplied with a replacement burden, distributed among visible systems, broken through prepared collapse, stripped of the Crown, or subordinated to a Mouth settlement. No architecture removes cost; each requires named bearers, casualties, authority, maintenance, and remedy. Current phase, pressure, damage, crews, Crown condition, active paths, and final settlement remain changing state.

references.title: The Mouth Below
references.summary: A fault, resonant cavity, and learning phenomenon beneath the Bell that answers repeated exchanges more readily than spoken intention.
references.content:
## Fault and listener

The Mouth Below is the old records' name for a place where geological fault, resonant cavity, and intelligence cannot be separated. It consumes patterned vibration and returns altered pressure, matter, and memory. The Long Listener is the conversational shape it forms from black water and fault glass, not proof of a human mind beneath the mountain.

## Recurrence and settlement

The Mouth learns repeated exchanges. A stable settlement needs an enacted offering, a concrete boundary, and a recurring return. Names, memories, royal cadence, civic machinery, opened landscape, heat, minerals, labor, or controlled vibration can all become patterns, but only if Harrowgate can actually maintain them. Repetition can become law before anyone intends it.

## What an answer cannot settle

The Mouth may reduce pressure, restore or alter memory, close royal command paths, return useful materials, or learn a safer venting cadence. It does not understand justice through abstraction, promise a human friendship, or make an unmaintainable bargain safe. Whether it is entered, what it has learned, offerings made, boundaries established, returns received, and any settlement remain matters for play.

references.title: The Crown of Measure
references.summary: A gold-black command and burden instrument whose custody, load, and retained royal faculties remain disputed.
references.content:
## A burden instrument

The Crown of Measure is a gold-black circlet built on the scale of a city wall: six arches close around a central measuring tongue inside the Deep Bell's clapper cage. It is not merely regalia. The Crown couples royal command, legal recognition, memory cadence, and a substantial share of the Bell's physical load.

## What the Crown carries

Queen Avarra's retained faculties pass between Crown and Iron Choir as Measure, Refusal, and Witness. The Crown can help compare burdens, reject a coerced acceptance, preserve surrender terms, open royal mechanisms, and complete certain command cadences. It cannot choose a just bearer, create consent, erase displaced strain, or make one genealogy exclusive.

## Custody is not settlement

The Golden Branch can recognize descent and open custody mechanisms. The Burden Chain recognizes communities and offices that maintained the machine. The Ash Witness preserves Avarra's conditions and release testimony. Possession may confer leverage and physical access without conferring lawful command. The Crown's condition, current custodian, attached load, available faculties, and final disposition remain live state; freeing it requires transferring or spending what it carries.

references.title: The Common Measure
references.summary: A rejected but workable distributed-burden design that replaces singular royal authority with voluntary weights, witnessed acceptance, bounded duration, and continuing maintenance.
references.content:
## Design and surviving parts

The Common Measure was rejected politically rather than mechanically. Its surviving design uses seventy-two inscribed civic handweights, voluntary or sworn substitutes, a copper acceptance collar, and the Pilgrim's Yoke as proof that a burden can be transferred without making one bearer permanent. Design plates and trial segments preserve the geometry.

## Recognition and operation

A usable Measure requires an intact or reconstructed collar, sufficient voluntary weight, Inverted Chapel recognition, Counterweight Wells balancing, and identified maintainers after the crisis. Acceptance must name authority, consent, duration, and remedy. Refusal must remain able to halt a transfer whose stated limit disappears.

## What the frame still needs

The Common Measure can distribute obligation and make later transfer accountable. It is not a perfect answer, a sovereign person, or proof that every represented community consented. It cannot supply its own mass, operators, maintenance, or political legitimacy. Components recovered, copies made, weights pledged, bearers chosen, Chapel status, Wells fit, duration, and post-crisis use remain changing state.

encounters.title: The Cracked Chapterhouse
encounters.summary: Harrowgate argues beneath rising dust while two sealed descents wait for the word rescue.
encounters.opening_view: The dust rises before the Bell sounds. It lifts from the altar crack in one pale sheet, and every argument in the chapterhouse stops with it. Public seals bar the old processional stair; across the floor, Tarrow’s survey stakes lean toward the quarry wound. Only when the dust begins to settle does Warden Marr finish the word he had been trying to say: “Rescue.”
encounters.content:
## Situation

Harrowgate has used the old chapterhouse as storehouse, plague ward, election hall, and now command post. Each use left its own lock, chalk mark, and grievance. A crack runs from the sealed processional stair to the outer wall. Warm air rises through it with lamp soot, wet stone, and the iron taste of blood. Dust comes first when the Bell draws breath; the council has learned to stop speaking.

The bell beneath Harrowgate has sounded three times without rope or ringer, each earlier in the damaged cycle than the one before. The first toll cracked chimneys and was blamed on quarry settling. After the second emptied the north well in a column of black rain, the council closed the affected streets and sent signals down both old entrances. No answer came. The third toll, before dawn today, dropped a tenement wall and left nine townspeople unable to remember the names of their oldest children. Tarrow's gauges are already returning to their pre-toll positions. If nothing below changes, he expects the fourth before midnight.

The Ember Company entered the buried complex five days ago and spent its first two days surveying in silence. One Ember porter brought two injured workers out before the Crown party reached the Ropeworks. That porter had seen a preparatory order to open the Queen's chain, but not the cut itself, and reported it only to Ember's surface clerk. A wounded porter returned through the quarry at dawn after the third toll. He reported that the company reached the old Ropeworks, that Factor Orren Saye executed the order, and that Captain Maelin Rook tried to stop him. He died before naming who survived. The earlier survivor then gave Warden Marr the copied order. A player character may be that survivor; otherwise the porter briefs the commission, offers to guide the first descent, and remains available for surface rescue. Until the dying porter's testimony, Harrowgate knew the Bell had failed; it did not know a living expedition had broken it.

## The commission

**Warden Elian Marr**, Harrowgate's elected civil officer, asks the party to descend, find any living members of the Ember Company, and prevent another uncontrolled toll. He can promise town funds, salvage rights to ordinary treasure, and public authority to requisition labor or close streets. He cannot grant ownership of the royal crown said to hang inside the bell.

**Lady Merrow Vey**, the last acknowledged descendant of Harrowgate's buried kings, has arrived with six retainers and a sealed genealogy. The third toll has made secrecy useless, so she admits that a Vey recovery trust funded the Ember Company's survey and authorized recovery only after the buried house was made safe. She denies authorizing a chain cut or any race against Harrowgate's custody. Her copy of the contract contains no second payment schedule. She offers a much larger reward for the Crown of Measure and insists that her ancestor's crown was stolen by rebels and made into the bell's clapper. She will accept a repaired bell only if the crown is returned to her after Harrowgate is safe.

**Master Iven Tarrow**, the town's quarry engineer, cares less about dynastic law. His survey stakes show that each toll transfers strain from the buried complex into the inhabited ridge. He believes the dungeon contains a deliberate pressure-release system, but he cannot tell whether repairing, silencing, or destroying it is safest without seeing its lower works.

The three patrons agree on rescue and immediate stabilization. They disagree about everything that follows.

## What the party knows at the outset

Give the players these facts without requiring investigation:

- the bell is physically beneath Harrowgate;
- the abandoned cloister stair and the quarry cleft are both open routes below;
- the Ember Company entered two days before the first toll, and a dying porter says Orren ordered one royal chain cut over Captain Rook's refusal;
- the old complex used water, lamps, and immense counterweights as one machine;
- the Crown of Measure is believed to hang within the Deep Bell; and
- another uncontrolled toll is likely before midnight.

Do not hide these premises. Exploration reveals how the systems work, who remains alive, and which endings the party can still afford.

## Two entrances

### The processional stair

The blocked stair descends from the chapterhouse crypt to the Hall of Bent Knees. Clearing it is slow but controlled. It allows a stretcher team, ordinary lanterns, and a retreat line. The first obstruction is a stone door whose petition slot still moves.

### The quarry cleft

A fresh collapse has exposed a maintenance shaft in Harrowgate's working quarry. It is faster and reaches the Lantern Cistern side of the upper dungeon, but the descent crosses broken hoists, unstable shelves, and the hunting path of something that has learned to follow lamplight.

Divide the expedition, choose one descent, or establish both. The stair favors negotiation and orderly retreat; the cleft favors speed, surprise, and early access to the water system.

## The fourth-toll clock

Begin at **Tremor 1: unsettled**. Advance the clock when the party takes a full rest in unsafe ground, makes a major failed attempt against the bell machinery, abandons a large noisy conflict, or deliberately spends hours on excavation or salvage.

1. **Unsettled:** dust falls; small mechanisms slip; creatures move toward warmer chambers.
2. **Shifting:** one previously easy vertical route becomes difficult until braced or counterweighted.
3. **Black rain:** water reverses through one open conduit; change the state of a cistern or flooded room.
4. **The fourth toll:** Harrowgate suffers a major collapse, every unprotected creature in the dungeon experiences memory bleed, and the Deep Bell's hanging structure loses another degree of stability.

Treat midnight as Tarrow's best projection, not a stopwatch. Failed operations and major delay close the cycle; bracing, venting, crews, shortcuts, and safe camps buy time. Telegraph every advance before it lands.

## Useful preparations

The council can provide rope, quarry spikes, timber shores, oil, stretchers, chalk, canvas, and six disciplined volunteers. Specialized requests create choices:

- Tarrow can spare a compact brake winch or a set of four wall shores, not both.
- Lady Vey can lend the genealogy seals or two heavily armed retainers, not both.
- Marr can send the town surgeon below or keep her ready for the next surface collapse.

None is mandatory. Each solves a class of problem while leaving another exposed.

## Immediate complications

Use one before descent if the opening needs pressure:

- a child recognizes a returned Ember Company pack and claims its owner is still alive;
- Chief Factor Halren Coss's deputy attempts to insert a private instruction into the party's commission;
- the blocked stair exhales a human voice reciting names no one in the chapterhouse remembers;
- a quarry horn reports movement beneath the new cleft; or
- the floor crack widens enough to reveal a brass chain plate carrying a partial dungeon plan.

## Results and return

The chapterhouse remains the safest surface base until a fourth toll breaks it. Bring rescued delvers, recovered records, faction envoys, and disputed treasure here. Everything carried across this floor becomes public: Crown custody, protected prisoners, evacuation orders, and promises made below in Harrowgate's name.

reference_links.context: Vey offers House resources and a genuine but bounded Crown claim while answering for the secret recovery contract.
The dying porter's testimony establishes Rook's refusal and the expedition's split.
Public testimony identifies Orren's loaded chain cut while leaving the concealed sponsor chain to later evidence.
Coss's deputy and the public commission expose the difference between the written recovery contract and private Company instructions.
Returned equipment and testimony make the private expedition a public rescue and accountability crisis.
The shortening toll clock and surface damage make the hidden machine a public emergency.
The disputed royal instrument is the commission's promised prize, but neither reward nor descent settles its load or custody.

encounters.title: The Quarry Cleft
encounters.summary: A fresh quarry wound offers speed, a stranded porter, and a hunter that follows open light.
encounters.opening_view: The rope has been cut carefully. Its lower knots are gone, but enough remains for a rescuer and not enough for a hurried pursuit. Below, a quarry cage hangs crooked on one rail. Someone coughs in the dark beneath it. The moment a lamp shutter opens, something pale turns its smooth head toward the light.
encounters.content:
## Situation

The eastern quarry has bitten through the buried house. A night collapse exposed bronze rungs, broken ceramic lines, and shelves narrow enough for one careful worker. The Ember Company used the cleft after retreating from the processional stair. Its rope still hangs, but someone cut the lower knots from beneath: pursuit delayed, rescue still possible.

Three hazards stand between the lip and the Lantern Cistern or Garden of Teeth.

## The descent

**The broken hoist.** A quarry cage hangs twenty feet below the lip, caught on one bent rail. Its brake can be restored, sacrificed as a falling platform, or ignored. Ember Company packs inside contain food, lamp oil, a field surgeon's roll, and a ledger identifying six members who entered by this route.

**The breathing shelf.** Warm air pushes through a horizontal crack in a slow rhythm. Crossing during the exhalation is easy. Crossing against it risks a fall or losing loose equipment into the dark. The rhythm matches, but does not perfectly predict, the Deep Bell's strain cycle.

**The lamp hunter.** A pale, six-limbed quarry predator clings to the shaft below. It has no eyes. It follows heat and lamp smoke, attacking the brightest descending target before withdrawing through maintenance slots. Darkness, cold light, baited oil, noise from another shelf, or direct violence can all answer it. Killing it is useful but not required; driving it toward the Menagerie changes that optional region later.

## The stranded porter

**Jessa Noll**, an Ember Company porter, is wedged in a service niche behind the breathing shelf. Her ankle is broken and her memories arrive out of order. She can still report three reliable facts:

- Captain Maelin Rook opposed cutting the chain;
- Factor Orren Saye took four delvers toward the royal grave after the first uncontrolled movement; and
- engineer Pell Varo descended toward the Ropeworks with tools and two wounded companions.

Jessa has a brass tally stamped with the Ropeworks load sequence. She will surrender it freely if promised extraction. Carrying her up costs time and hands; stabilizing the cleft lets the town volunteers retrieve her later.

## Routes

At the bottom, three ways open:

- an oil-slick service walk enters the Lantern Cistern;
- a root-choked crack descends into the Garden of Teeth; and
- a cage-transfer tunnel leads toward the Menagerie of Quiet Beasts.

The processional side can also be reached by following a narrow inspection ledge toward the Hall of Bent Knees, creating the first upper-dungeon loop.

## Treasure and salvage

The broken cage holds climbing gear, compact rations, three flasks of high-grade ward oil, silver wire, a surgeon's roll, and the Ember Company's sealed base contract with Lady Vey's recovery trust. It authorizes survey and Crown recovery only after the buried house is made safe, requires witnessed transfer, and does not authorize damage to the Bell. It contains no accelerated-possession rider or second payment schedule.

## Consequences

- **Cleft braced:** volunteers can evacuate wounded and carry modest salvage without advancing the tremor clock.
- **Hoist restored:** later travel between surface and cistern is fast, but the mechanism's noise draws attention.
- **Lamp hunter loose:** it may appear in any unlit upper encounter or return to the Menagerie.
- **Jessa abandoned:** the next tremor worsens her condition and damages trust with surviving delvers.
- **Base contract exposed:** Lady Vey must answer for the secret expedition, while the missing rider and second schedule narrow the later escalation to Coss, Rhun, Orren, or evidence still below.

reference_links.context: The recovered base contract establishes Vey's conditional authority and the absence of the later possession rider.
Jessa preserves Rook's counter-order and traces her pursuit after Orren.
Jessa traces Orren and four delvers toward the royal route after the first failure.
Jessa traces Varo, his tools, and wounded companions toward the Ropeworks.
Company route marks, wounded survivors, and the split trail establish the descent's practical history.

encounters.title: The Hall of Bent Knees
encounters.summary: Two hundred stone petitioners make every entrant declare the burden they will carry.
encounters.opening_view: The ceiling makes you bow before the petitioners do. Two hundred stone figures kneel in ordered rows, their faces worn away, their burdens still exact: bread, blade, broken wheel, dead child, sealed mouth. The far door offers no latch. Beside it, a bronze scale holds one empty pan and room enough for a name, a burden, and whatever makes the two belong together.
encounters.content:
## Situation

The processional stair ends in a hall designed to make pride physically inconvenient. Two hundred statues kneel in ordered rows, each carrying a different petition: loaf, sword, dead child, broken wheel, water jar, sealed mouth. Mineral dust has erased their faces but not their burdens. The far door has no handle. Beside it, a bronze scale waits for an entrant to make weight and meaning agree.

The hall was once the lawful public entrance to the buried house. Its machinery still distinguishes petitioners, officers, prisoners, and thieves. It enforces declared purpose and recorded burden, whether the purpose is merciful or wicked.

## The petition scale

To open the inner door, someone must place one of four things on the scale:

- a written name accepted as the entrant's own;
- an object the entrant is honestly willing to leave behind;
- a burden taken from another person in the hall; or
- blood sufficient to mark the petition plate.

Nothing placed on the scale must be lost forever. Entrants can retrieve an object from the inner return channel, share a burden, present a true alias, use an Ember Company tally, or dismantle the mechanism. The scale establishes the house's grammar: declared purpose moves machinery, and every movement transfers weight.

False declarations do not trigger a trap. They open the wrong door. A petitioner claiming to be a prisoner reaches holding cells; a thief reaches the tally cage; an officer reaches the inspection gallery. Each route is usable and each shows different clues.

## The first Salt Wardens

**Sister Vesra Quill** and three salt-preserved wardens occupy the inspection gallery. Their skin is gray-white and cracked around old stitching. They are neither mindless dead nor living people in ordinary need of food. Their memories are held in salt tablets fitted behind the sternum.

Vesra opens with three questions:

1. Who bears responsibility for the broken Queen's chain?
2. Does the party intend to restore the bell, remove the crown, or merely survive?
3. What burden will Harrowgate accept if its safety depends on people buried below it?

She knows the party cannot answer all three yet. Honest uncertainty earns a temporary passage mark. A claim of absolute right—royal, civic, religious, or martial—causes her to demand a formal petition and collateral.

Vesra belongs to the **Continuance** faction among the Wardens. She believes the bell must be stabilized and rung under control until a lawful replacement for the crown exists. She admits that the old settlement harms the Low Choir, but she considers an uncontrolled collapse worse.

## Opposition

The hall's active threats depend on how the party enters:

- forcing the far door animates burden-bearer statues that grapple, pin, and redistribute carried equipment rather than simply dealing damage;
- presenting stolen royal seals opens the officer route but wakes a bronze examiner that attempts to confiscate them;
- spilling blood in excess wakes the tally cage and marks the donor for recognition by deeper ward mechanisms; and
- attacking Vesra causes the inspection gallery to seal while a warning travels to the Salt Barracks.

Use the kneeling rows as narrow lanes, low sightlines, and stone barriers waiting to be toppled.

## Routes and discoveries

The main petition door reaches the Ropeworks. The officer gallery reaches the Chain Scriptorium. The prisoner route descends toward the Salt Barracks. A maintenance crawl behind the statue carrying a broken wheel returns to the Quarry Cleft.

The hall also contains the first complete statement of the three burdens:

> Water carries the weight. Light remembers the way. The chain decides who pays.

## Negotiated passage

Vesra can grant:

- a salt mark recognized by lesser wardens;
- safe directions to the Ropeworks and Barracks;
- the name of Prior Dalca, leader of the Warden faction that favors ending the bell's sentence; and
- a promise to delay one hostile response if the party rescues trapped wardens or recovers missing salt tablets.

She cannot grant ownership of the crown and will not permit the Deep Bell to be destroyed without hearing a credible evacuation plan for Harrowgate.

## Outcomes

- **Petition accepted:** the party gains orderly access and understands burden transfer.
- **Alternative door used:** the party gains a different route and leaves a recorded declaration that deeper mechanisms may invoke.
- **Wardens allied:** the Salt Barracks begins watchful rather than hostile.
- **Wardens opposed:** later barriers close, but the party can still proceed through machinery, hidden routes, or the Low Choir.
- **Scale broken:** immediate access is easy; later return channels and lawful shortcuts fail until repaired.

reference_links.context: Sister Vesra Quill introduces Warden petition grammar and the Continuance position.
Petitions and Warden grammar expose the buried community's suppressed standing before the party reaches its households.

encounters.title: The Ropeworks of Three Burdens
encounters.summary: Three burden drums turn the upper house; each repaired route strains another system.
encounters.opening_view: A drum moves. A hand’s breadth only. It is enough. Black water climbs a service channel; silver memory lines draw taut and begin to sing; the Crown chain jerks above a bridge crowded with survivors. Three instructions shine on the drum housing where Orren’s copied schedule left blank metal. Then the bridge drops another inch.
encounters.content:
## Situation

Here the buried house admits that it is a machine. Three immense drums govern lifts, water, bridges, memory lines, and the Deep Bell's frame. No burden moves invisibly; every transfer appears as motion, slack, or strain on the other two drums.

The Ember Company reached this chamber intact. Factor Orren Saye used a royal seal and an abridged extraction schedule to access the Crown Drum. His copy called the outer chain a release restraint. The complete sequence, still cut into the drum housing, requires operators to unload the Crown Drum, set the Water Drum forward, and arrest the Memory Drum before that chain is opened. Orren's copy omits those three lines.

Captain Maelin Rook saw live strain on all three drums and refused the cut. Orren ordered it anyway, arguing that delay would let Harrowgate seize the Crown. The struggle left the outer chain severed, the Water Drum in reverse, and the Memory Drum half-braked. The first uncontrolled toll followed within the hour.

## The three drums

### The Crown Drum

Black rope and bronze chain descend toward the Counterweight Wells and Deep Bell. One of three royal chains is severed. The drum now slips whenever the mountain flexes. Bracing it reduces immediate movement but prevents the main royal lift from descending.

### The Water Drum

Ceramic-jacketed ropes operate sluices between the Lantern Cistern, Reliquary Under Water, and Black Rain Cistern. It currently runs in reverse, sending warm lower water upward in pulses. Correcting it can drain one region only by flooding another unless secondary gates are opened locally.

### The Memory Drum

Silver-gray cords connect ward lamps, speaking tubes, and the Choir of Iron Tongues. Its brake stores the impressions taken during each toll. Releasing it restores fragments of memory to nearby sufferers but extinguishes ward-light and alerts the Low Choir.

For every operation, name what moves, what stops, and where the displaced burden lands.

## Survivors on the hanging bridge

Engineer **Pell Varo**, shield-bearer **Dain Cor**, and two wounded porters are trapped on a bridge between the Water and Crown drums. A snapped lift cage blocks their retreat. Pell can explain the immediate machinery and repair one major component if given tools and protection. He is furious with Orren but does not know whether Captain Rook survived.

Rescuing them can be handled through climbing, rotating a drum, counterweighting the bridge, using the quarry winch, crossing from the Scriptorium gallery, or reaching the bridge's lower anchor from the Salt Barracks.

## Active threats

**Load ghosts** appear as translucent workers whenever a drum moves without a declared operator. They repeat the last fatal labor performed at that station: hauling, cutting, catching, or being dragged into a brake. They can be fought, but naming a responsible operator and accepting the drum's visible mark makes them stand down.

**The slipping Crown Drum** advances toward failure during prolonged conflict. Telegraph each slip with a hard metallic report and a corresponding lurch in the shaft.

**Ember Company deserters** may occupy the upper control booth. They want the surviving porters rescued but fear Captain Rook will execute them for siding with Orren. They can offer crossbows, route knowledge, and false testimony.

## Courses of action

### Stabilize first

Shore the Crown Drum, lock the Water Drum, and leave Memory untouched. This creates the safest upper hub but closes the royal lift and leaves lower flooding unresolved.

### Restore transit

Repair the lift controls and accept continued strain on the Crown Drum. Travel becomes fast, wounded can be evacuated, and the Counterweight Wells are easier to reach. A later tremor may drop the lift if the crown chain remains unrepaired.

### Reverse the water

Send the Water Drum forward. The Reliquary begins draining while the Black Rain Cistern rises. This opens treasure and a route to the Inverted Chapel but worsens the deepest pressure hazard.

### Release stored memory

Ease the Memory brake. Nearby victims recover names, maps, and moments. Ward lamps dim across the dungeon, and creatures kept quiet by light begin to move. The Low Choir immediately knows someone has touched its stolen memories.

### Cut another burden free

The party can deliberately sever a drum and localize the disaster: drop a lift to lock the shaft, break a sluice line to isolate water, or cut memory cords to end the bell's reach in one region. Each creates a permanent route change and a named cost.

## Routes

- upper galleries reach the Hall of Bent Knees and Chain Scriptorium;
- a service bridge reaches the Salt Barracks;
- the water lift descends toward the Reliquary Under Water;
- the royal lift descends toward the Counterweight Wells; and
- rope ladders behind the Water Drum reach the Lantern Cistern.

A party that controls the Ropeworks can traverse much of the dungeon quickly. A party that destroys it can still proceed through regional loops but loses easy extraction.

## What Pell Varo can do

Given time, tools, and one secure work site, Pell can complete one major repair before the fourth toll:

- restore the royal lift;
- fit a temporary crown-chain splice;
- synchronize the upper water gates;
- create a controlled Memory Drum release; or
- prepare demolition that will drop the Ropeworks without propagating upward.

A second task requires a recovered maintenance plate from the Chain Scriptorium or assistance from the Salt Wardens.

## Outcomes

Record all three drums, the survivors, and whether the hub remains traversable. Control here shortens rescue and extraction; destruction leaves regional loops but makes every later operation slower and harder.

reference_links.context: Rook recognized live load on all three drums and refused the abridged chain-cut sequence.
The complete drum sequence shows what Orren's copy omitted when he ordered the outer chain cut.
Varo can read the three drums, explain displaced burden, and coordinate a major repair if rescued and supplied.
The complete drum sequence reveals the unload and synchronization steps omitted from Rhun's copy.
Rook's refusal and Orren's loaded cut divide the Company around command, rescue, and possession.
Scriptorium plates preserve the complete load sequence and connect the three drums to later maintenance law.
The Ropeworks identifies the loads that must later be assigned to compatible Wells paths and timings.
The three drums expose the Bell's connected Crown, Water, and Memory loads.

encounters.title: The Chain Scriptorium
encounters.summary: A hanging archive files truth by duty and exposes the claimant behind every question.
encounters.opening_view: Keeper Odran Greve bars the threshold with one open hand. “Not what do you want,” he says. “Under what duty do you ask?” When someone answers, brass records begin travelling through the dark: water low, royal claims high, memory plates warm between them. A genealogy descends one link, stops, and sways. Odran watches the stopped link rather than the speaker.
encounters.content:
## Situation

The buried house hangs plans, judgments, repair orders, and dynastic claims by the burden they governed. Water records hang low and green, royal plates high, and silvered memory plates warm between them.

At the central post, state a purpose and accept the records it implies. The chains answer with prior uses of the same duty: evacuation routes and casualty rolls for rescue, confiscation inventories and hidden returns for theft, succession law and execution orders for sovereignty.

## Navigating the archive

Search by:

- declaring a purpose and accepting the records it implies;
- physically following chain families from one mechanism to another;
- using genealogy seals to access royal plates;
- releasing the brake that keeps condemned records above the floor; or
- asking a Salt Warden or Low Choir guide to read old burden notation.

On a failed search, bring forward a dangerous or inconvenient truth. Never return nothing.

## Keeper Odran Greve

**Odran Greve** turns within the rotating index cage, frail beneath a century of returned working memory. Each sentence arrives as if it needs a hook and shelf. “A room that remembers what an office forgot,” he calls the Scriptorium; several such offices still speak through him.

Odran knows:

- Queen Avarra's limited surrender permitted her Crown to stabilize the fault, though the surrender itself was coerced;
- the bell's regular toll transferred mountain strain into the Black Rain Cistern;
- later wardens redirected the toll's mnemonic cost onto the labor community now called the Low Choir;
- the crown can be replaced by another accepted burden of equal declared authority; and
- a controlled collapse can save most of Harrowgate if the quarry vents and black-water channels are opened first.

Odran will not hand over every plate at once. “A record can be stolen by removing it,” he says, “or by removing everything that tells you where it hung.” Too much extraction destroys the physical index and sends whole chain families sliding into lower shafts.

## The chained genealogy

Lady Vey's descent is genuine but incomplete. The high royal plates divide three jurisdictions:

- the Golden Branch traces blood custody through House Vey and collateral lines;
- the Burden Chain traces operating standing through offices, households, guilds, Wardens, and crews that maintained the machine; and
- the Ash Witness preserves Avarra's surrender limits through living and inherited testimony.

None grants simple ownership. Together they separate custody, maintained obligation, and release testimony. The King's Narrow Grave can be found by aligning all three instead of privileging one.

## Dangers

**Index shear.** Sudden movement turns the hanging rows into cutting pendulums. The party can drop, brace, ride, or deliberately redirect the chain wave.

**Condemned records.** Plates lifted out of the lower dark carry executed promises. Reading one may impose a temporary compulsion, reveal a hidden route, or summon a load ghost that insists the old sentence be completed.

**Orren's search party.** Factor Orren Saye or his agents may arrive seeking the royal chain sequence. They prefer bargaining, theft, and hostage leverage to a fair fight. Orren believes the town will confiscate the crown unless he reaches it first. Odran can compare Orren's copied schedule with the complete hanging plate: the copy preserves the release command and removes the three prerequisite operations that would have shown the Crown Drum was still carrying live load.

## Routes and useful plates

The archive can identify or directly open routes to:

- the Ropeworks inspection gallery;
- the Salt Barracks through a muster-record door;
- the Reliquary Under Water by its salvage register;
- the Feast of Empty Chairs through ration chains;
- the Inverted Chapel through execution records;
- the King's Narrow Grave through the three genealogies; and
- the Choir of Iron Tongues through maintenance concordances.

Recovering a maintenance plate lets Pell Varo or another skilled operator perform an additional major repair.

## Hard choices

- Taking the royal genealogy strengthens Lady Vey's claim but removes evidence of the other two successions unless copied.
- Releasing Low Choir memory plates restores names at the cost of extinguishing one family of ward lamps.
- Giving Odran safe passage deprives the archive of its keeper; leaving him preserves navigation but risks his death in the fourth toll.
- Destroying condemned plates prevents old compulsions from returning and also erases proof of crimes committed by the buried kings.

## Outcomes

Before the party leaves, give them one route, one operating truth, and one disputed claim. They need not exhaust the archive; every plate removed changes what can later be proved.

reference_links.context: Three successions confirm Vey's blood descent while dividing custody, maintenance authority, and surrender standing.
Odran can compare Orren's copied schedule with the complete plate and expose the missing prerequisites.
A recovered maintenance plate expands the safe work available to Varo or another skilled operator.
Surrender plates and the Ash Witness line preserve Avarra's limited terms rather than a complete royal command.
Burden-indexed records let the party compare Rhun's abridged schedule with the complete royal plate.
Odran governs searches by declared duty, preserves plate context, and can expose the omissions in Orren's copy.
The burden-indexed archive, Odran's custody, chain hazards, and disputed records are encountered directly.
The Scriptorium's three genealogy lines align the route and preserve the Grave's divided jurisdictions.
Duty records separate royal command, maintenance standing, and surrender terms attached to the Crown.

encounters.title: The Lantern Cistern
encounters.summary: Four lamp boughs divide safety, memory, and scarce oil above black water full of pale hands.
encounters.opening_view: The fourth lamp bough is dark. Beneath it, the dead scout under the oil-black water walks the same three steps, turns, sinks, and rises to begin again. Pale hands keep pace below him. Tavia Hest, bound to a valve standard with cloth over her burned eyes, hears your gear and says, “Tell me you brought rope before you tell me you brought fire.”
encounters.content:
## Situation

The Lantern Cistern is a round chamber built around a basin of warm black water. A copper mast divides above it into four lamp boughs, each carrying hundreds of shallow cups on silver wire. Ward-oil lies across the basin in a skin thin enough to mirror flame and thick enough to conceal the pale things feeding beneath it. Every branch lights a route; every silver wick carries something else away.

The basin was designed to separate oil from the warm water pumped up from the Black Rain Cistern. The lamp-tree then sends both light and mnemonic discharge through silver-wick lines into the rest of the buried house. Since the Water Drum reversed, black water enters in pulses. Each pulse lifts the oil skin, rocks the hanging cups, and threatens to carry fire into the service galleries.

Treat the cistern as a distribution station. A lit bough quiets its routes and carries future toll-memory toward the Choir. A dark bough releases what its wicks hold, frees scavengers along that route, and yields oil for elsewhere.

## First view and immediate pressure

The party arrives while three lamp boughs burn and the fourth gutters. On the outer service ring, **Tavia Hest**, an Ember Company scout, has tied herself to a valve standard. Her eyes are wrapped in oil-soaked cloth after a flare burned them. She extinguished the Mourning Bough to escape a creature that followed the light reflected in her polished buckles. She now believes, incorrectly, that every lamp attracts the things below.

At the center of the basin, a dead scout named **Corven Braid** drifts face-down beneath the oil skin. The lamplighter key is clipped to his belt. Each black-water pulse makes his body stand, walk several steps along the submerged grate, and sink again. A pale shape follows beneath him.

Put five decisions in view:

- recover the lamplighter key or bypass its keyed valves;
- keep Tavia alive through the next water pulse;
- decide whether to relight the Mourning Bough;
- prevent a lamp cascade if the oil skin reaches the lowest cups; and
- choose how much light and oil to preserve for later regions.

## Lamplighter Senn

**Lamplighter Senn** is a Salt Warden dried translucent around a lattice of silver wick. Turn the key—or speak three lamp names in order—and he steps from the mast. He names each branch for the workers, prisoners, petitioners, and Low Choir children whose memories passed through it. His speech is arithmetic: “Processional keeps twelve routes. Mourning keeps Rhea breathing. Deep keeps the gauges honest.” He has kept the account accurately enough to make the word unbearable.

Senn's first obligation is to prevent a basin fire. His second is to keep at least one safe route to every occupied district. His third is to preserve the memory carried by the wicks. Those duties now conflict. He will cooperate with anyone who names what they are willing to leave dark and who will bear responsibility for the people on that route.

Senn knows:

- the four lamp boughs and every region each protects;
- how to release stored memory without setting the oil alight;
- that the silver wick is carrying Low Choir memory toward the Iron Tongues;
- that the Reliquary's copper saints share an air manifold with the cistern bells;
- that the Deep Bough was dimmed before the Ember Company arrived; and
- that one branch can be kept lit for a full tremor interval with one portable measure of ward-oil.

He does not know why the Deep Bough was dimmed. That order came from the Salt Barracks, not the lamplighters.

## The four lamp boughs

Track each bough as one regional state; ignore individual cups unless a scene makes one matter.

### The Processional Bough

Feeds the Hall of Bent Knees, Ropeworks, and Chain Scriptorium. While lit, load ghosts in those regions remain slow and ceremonial, and the main upper routes are easy to read. Darkening it yields one portable oil measure and releases memories of petitioners, condemned workers, and the Ember Company's first passage.

### The Ossuary Bough

Feeds the Salt Barracks, Garden of Teeth, and Menagerie handling ways. While lit, the Garden's bone moths remain in their beds and Warden recognition marks remain visible. In darkness, root routes become easier to follow by sound, but purpose-bred scavengers leave their stalls. Darkening it yields one portable oil measure.

### The Mourning Bough

Feeds the Reliquary Under Water, Feast of Empty Chairs, and Inverted Chapel. It begins extinguished. While lit, copper saint mouths glow beneath the water and Low Choir mourning stairs remain protected. Relighting it suppresses drowned load ghosts but resumes carrying memories from the inhabited Feast Hall toward the Iron Tongues.

### The Deep Bough

Feeds the Counterweight Wells, Choir of Iron Tongues, Black Rain Cistern, and the upper control walks of the Deep Bell. It begins lit only at half strength. Full light makes deep mechanisms legible and suppresses fault-born scavengers. Darkness conceals movement from the Iron Choir and prevents new memory from reaching it, but the lower routes become substantially more dangerous. Bringing it to full strength costs one portable oil measure; darkening it yields one.

## Ward-oil economy

There are four portable oil measures available when the room is first secured:

- one in Senn's emergency cabinet;
- one in Corven Braid's sealed survey can;
- one trapped in the gutter beneath the Processional Bough; and
- one recoverable by skimming the basin without contaminating it with black water.

In addition, darkening the Processional, Ossuary, or Deep Bough yields one measure. The extinguished Mourning Bough has already been drained by Tavia.

One measure can:

- keep one bough operating through the next tremor-clock advance;
- light a portable ward lamp for one expedition interval;
- make two weapons or shields repellent to pale scavengers for one encounter;
- establish a safe camp in a defensible room, provided smoke can escape; or
- prime one Reliquary saint, Chapel station, or Iron Tongue mechanism that has lost its local supply.

Oil mixed with black water burns hot and almost smokeless for a few breaths, then produces silver vapor carrying involuntary memories. It is an effective barrier or emergency purge, but anyone breathing the vapor experiences a memory that belongs to someone below. Record whose memory was taken and whether it is later returned.

## The pale scavengers

The shapes beneath the oil are **wick-eaters**, soft white creatures with lampblack mouths and hands like drowned paper. They feed on the memory residue that condenses around active silver wick. Direct ward-light pins them below the water, but reflected or portable light draws their attention through dark spaces.

Move them toward whatever the party's light plan makes newly edible.

- In full light, they remain beneath the grates and can be observed or trapped.
- Under selective light, they migrate toward the boundary between lit and dark routes.
- In complete darkness, they climb out and seek warm memories: names spoken repeatedly, written journals, ancestral relics, and people recently affected by a toll.
- Released memory can distract, feed, or even briefly communicate through them.
- Black-water fire destroys them locally but risks a lamp cascade.

A wick-eater's first wound is mnemonic: it takes why the victim came. Continued contact strips names, loyalties, and practiced routes.

## Operating the cistern

### Recover the key

Corven's body can be reached by swimming under the oil skin, hooking him from the service ring, lowering a Ropeworks line, walking the submerged grate between pulses, or luring the following wick-eater away with released memory. Cutting the key free without recovering the body is faster. Bringing Corven out gives Tavia a reason to cooperate and provides an intact route ledger in his boot.

### Bypass the key

The valves can be forced, picked through the mast, commanded by a recognized Warden, or operated from the Ropeworks Water Drum. A bypass risks opening two bough feeds at once, causing a flare cascade unless someone controls the cup chains.

### Restore full light

Relight the Mourning Bough and strengthen the Deep Bough. This costs two portable oil measures. Upper and middle routes become safer, drowned load ghosts recede, and the Iron Tongues receive every new mnemonic discharge. Senn prefers this until confronted with what the Low Choir pays.

### Establish selective light

Choose which boughs remain lit. Selective light gains oil and route control while concentrating wick-eaters at lit-dark boundaries. Mark both lit routes and newly dark routes.

### Release stored memory

Senn can pinch a bough's feed, cool its cups, and draw the silver wicks through a ceramic comb. The bough goes dark, and everyone nearby hears names, work songs, arguments, and final thoughts. People whose memories are present recover them if they are close enough or later receive the combed wick. The released memories can expose routes, Ember Company actions, or Low Choir identities. The operation takes time and attracts wick-eaters without causing a fire.

### Burn the basin clean

Opening the black-water pulse while dropping selected cups creates a brief sheet of silver flame. It destroys wick-eaters, sterilizes contaminated oil, and can deny pursuit through one gallery. It also consumes two oil measures, fills adjacent rooms with memory vapor, and risks setting an entire bough beyond control.

### Reverse or isolate the separator
