The local separator can be locked against the global water state, allowing the Reliquary to change level without immediately flooding the cistern. This requires the key, Senn, or coordinated work from the Ropeworks. A rough repair holds until the next tremor advance; a proper repair by Pell or a Warden crew is durable.

## Tavia Hest

Tavia is observant, ashamed, and still useful. Her sight returns gradually if the burned cloth is changed and her face washed with clean water. She can identify Ember route chalk by touch, guide the party to the Reliquary water lift, and testify that Orren ordered Corven to carry a second contract sealed by Chief Factor Halren Coss.

She wants Corven recovered and the Deep Bough darkened so Orren cannot use the lower ward marks. She will not knowingly condemn the wounded company members in the Ropeworks. If rescued and treated honestly, she can range ahead through dark routes without losing direction and later help extract survivors.

## Routes

- a rung ladder behind the Processional feed reaches the Ropeworks;
- the quarry service tunnel enters above the emergency cabinet;
- a petitioner's oil pipe reaches the Hall of Bent Knees;
- the Ossuary drain passes into the Garden of Teeth;
- the Mourning conduit and bell line descend to the Reliquary Under Water; and
- a narrow maintenance throat follows the Deep Bough toward the Black Rain Cistern.

The Black Rain throat is passable only when the separator is isolated or the party accepts a hot-water surge. It is an early deep route, not a safe shortcut.

## Clues and useful discoveries

Searches, operations, and conversations here can reveal:

- the bell's systems exchange water, light, memory, and burden rather than operating independently;
- ward-light suppresses scavengers while carrying stolen memory into the Iron Choir;
- the Reliquary can be entered and ventilated through its saint manifold;
- the Garden drain remains usable even when its upper door is barred;
- the Deep Bough was deliberately weakened on Warden orders; and
- Corven's ledger marks a fault-line maintenance route into the Black Rain Cistern.

## Outcomes

Record:

- which boughs are lit, dark, failing, or burning;
- how many portable oil measures remain;
- whether stored memories were released and to whom;
- whether Senn remains at his post, joins the party, or is destroyed;
- the fate and disposition of Tavia Hest;
- whether Corven's body, key, ledger, and second contract were recovered;
- whether the local separator is synchronized, isolated, or ruptured; and
- where the wick-eaters migrate.

Light here always has a recipient and a payer. Make both visible before the party carries its oil deeper.

encounters.title: The Reliquary Under Water
encounters.summary: Six copper saints trade breath and water around a trapped surgeon and a rejected civic burden.
encounters.opening_view: On every third breath, the copper saint speaks with a woman’s voice. “Do not drain it.” Black water stands at the saints’ ribs. A many-armed pallbearer is drawing a drowned burden toward the figure with closed eyes, while the Open Palm keeps oil, seals, and pressure cloth lifted above the flood. The saint breathes twice more. On the third, Rhea Colm says, “Replace what you take.”
encounters.content:
## Situation

The Reliquary is a shrine built as a breathing machine. Six copper saints stand in two rows on a gridded floor, their mouths, hands, and hollow bodies joined into one air-and-water manifold. At balance, black water reaches their ribs. At every other level, some rescue, route, or truth rises while another disappears.

The Reliquary keeps practical sacred things: tools, seals, trial burdens, and emergency fittings the old house promised never to use casually. Nearly every one is claimed.

The reversed Water Drum has made the level rise and fall in pulses. During the last rise, an Ember Company salvage team opened the central saint and triggered the reliquary's pallbearer construct. One survivor remains sealed inside the statue. Several dead workers have returned as load ghosts, endlessly moving weights between niches whose labels they can no longer read.

## The six copper saints

Each statue is a station in the shared manifold. A party can understand them from inscriptions, experimentation, Senn's guidance, Ropeworks records, or the rhythm of air moving through their mouths.

### The Saint of Returning Breath

Its open mouth draws air from the Lantern Cistern bell line. **Rhea Colm**, the Ember Company's field surgeon, is sealed inside its chest with a crushed lower leg. She has enough air for roughly one tremor interval if the Mourning Bough remains dark, longer if the bell line is primed with ward-oil or manually pumped.

### The Saint of the Open Palm

Its hands contain waxed pressure cloth, silvered oil flasks, ceramic valve wedges, and two emergency seals. Removing the right-hand cache lowers a local floodgate unless its weight is replaced.

### The Saint of Many Hands

Six hinged arms surround a rack of seventy-two bronze handweights. Each weight bears a different civic office, trade, household, or public duty. Together they form the surviving core of the **Common Measure**, a rejected design for replacing the Crown of Measure with many voluntary obligations held in one accepted frame.

### The Saint Beneath the Yoke

Its shoulders support a portable transfer frame called the **Pilgrim's Yoke**. The yoke can carry one declared burden between mechanisms for a short time. A willing bearer can use it to hold a gate, quiet load ghosts, or substitute for a missing counterweight. Each use leaves a visible gray line across the bearer's shoulders and transfers a memory or obligation with the load.

### The Saint of Closed Eyes

Its head faces the sealed royal niche. Flooding the statue to eye level opens the niche; draining below its knees closes it. The niche leads toward the King's Narrow Grave and holds one of the three genealogy seals. The mechanism reads water pressure, not blood.

### The Saint Who Kneels

Its body controls the lower culvert to the Black Rain Cistern. Forcing it upright drains the room rapidly downward. Leaving it kneeling holds the lower pressure. A half-raised position permits controlled drainage but requires continuous bracing or a counterweight from another saint.

## Water levels

Track one of four local states. The room may differ from the global water state if the Lantern separator or local saint manifold has been secured.

### High water

Water reaches the saints' shoulders and most floor salvage is submerged. The water lift, upper bell line, and Black Rain culvert are usable. The royal niche is open. Swimming is difficult but load ghosts are weak and the pallbearer moves slowly along the walls. Air pockets in the saints are generous.

### Middle water

Water reaches the saints' waists. This is the intended service level and the best state for rescuing Rhea or moving large objects. All six stations can be operated. The dry ledge toward the Inverted Chapel is reachable by a short climb. The pallbearer can move freely.

### Low water

The gridded floor, trial burdens, and bodies are exposed. Salvage is easiest and the Chapel ledge becomes a broad route. The Black Rain culvert becomes a dangerous open drop. Load ghosts regain full strength because their drowned work is visible. Rhea's air pocket collapses unless her statue is opened or externally pumped.

### Ruptured

The lower gate or floor has failed. Water, loose relics, bodies, and perhaps Rhea are being dragged toward Black Rain. The royal niche closes. The room becomes a rescue-and-extraction sequence, and the deeper cistern worsens permanently. A ruptured Reliquary can still be crossed on saint shoulders and hanging bell lines, but it cannot be restored without a major repair.

## Rhea Colm's rescue

Rhea speaks through the Saint of Returning Breath in breath-length reports: Orren's loyalists took the royal-niche route; Captain Maelin Rook followed rather than abandon the wounded; one dead salvager carried papers under a second Vey seal that did not match the crew's contract.

Credible rescue methods include:

- open the chest plate while maintaining middle or high water;
- raise the water so Rhea floats clear when the lower hatch opens;
- prime the bell line with ward-oil and cut her free from inside the statue;
- command the pallbearer to brace and open the saint;
- use the Pilgrim's Yoke to carry the statue's pressure burden; or
- drain the room and continuously pump air from the Lantern Cistern.

Simply smashing the statue works, but collapses the shared air manifold, removes the safest trapped-air route, and may kill Rhea if no one supports her leg and the internal valve cage.

Once free, Rhea works in triage order: breathing, movement, testimony that will worsen if delayed. She can stabilize survivors and identify the drowned. She asks that the Common Measure be preserved and Orren returned alive if possible. About the Crown she asks only, “What takes the weight when you take the gold?”

## The pallbearer

The reliquary's construct resembles a broad copper crab assembled from bier handles, censers, and jointed devotional arms. Its formal designation is **Bearer of Things Not Yet Relinquished**. Ember survivors call it the pallbearer.

It enforces declared custody:

- a rescuer who names a trapped person may handle tools needed for rescue;
- an operator who names a repair may move fittings and trial burdens;
- a claimant who names an inheritance may inspect, but not remove, disputed relics;
- a thief or vague scavenger is treated as an unbalanced load and pinned beneath a copper limb.

The pallbearer can be fought, trapped by water level, blinded by darkness, commanded with Senn's key, persuaded through exact declarations, or given a new custodial order by a recognized Salt Warden. Once cooperative, it can tow heavy burdens, brace the Kneeling Saint, carry Rhea, or transport one major salvage object through the water lift.

Destroying it yields valuable devotional copper and six articulated load joints. Those joints are excellent counterweight fittings, but the Reliquary loses its strongest local operator.

## Drowned load ghosts

The load ghosts are the workers killed during earlier replacement trials. They do not defend holiness. They insist that each weight have a named destination and a bearer who accepts it.

They can be:

- dispersed by ward-light;
- directed by reading the labels they can no longer see;
- quieted by moving one burden to its intended niche;
- enlisted by declaring a new trial of the Common Measure; or
- angered by stripping copper, erasing names, or dumping weights into Black Rain.

If enlisted, they can complete one coordinated lift or hold one failing gate through the next tremor. If attacked and destroyed, their burdens fall physically onto the room: gates shift, statues settle, and loose relics slide toward the culvert.

## The Common Measure

Nothing in the apparatus failed mechanically. The rejection marks treat distributed consent as insufficient royal authority. The surviving field kit is:

- seventy-two inscribed handweights in the Saint of Many Hands;
- the Pilgrim's Yoke, which proves a burden can be transferred voluntarily;
- a copper acceptance collar folded beneath the central floor grate; and
- design plates sealed inside the Saint of Returning Breath beside Rhea.

The surviving parts still require five operations before they can replace the Crown:

1. preserve or reconstruct the acceptance collar;
2. obtain enough voluntary weights or sworn substitutes to represent Harrowgate and the people below;
3. have the Inverted Chapel accept the assembled burden;
4. balance it in the Counterweight Wells; and
5. establish who maintains the obligations after the crisis.

The handweights need not all be carried. A careful party can copy their measures and manufacture substitutes, recruit actual officeholders, or combine them with royal and Warden metal. Taking the original rack provides the strongest proof and fastest finale route but strips the Reliquary of its public record.

## Other salvage

### Emergency seals

Two ceramic-and-wax seals can close a ruptured pipe, saint, or minor black-water gate. Each is single-use unless recovered before pressure sets.

### Silvered oil flasks

Three flasks carry ward-oil through black water without contamination. Ordinary bottles work only briefly and may ignite or leak memory vapor.

### The drowned contract satchel

A dead Company clerk carries three documents in one waxed case: Lady Vey's conditional survey-and-recovery contract, a concealed bonus schedule issued by Chief Factor Halren Coss for physical possession before public notice, and Councilor Samet Rhun's debt rider pledging town obligations against the Crown. The base contract requires safe detachment and a witnessed transfer. The later papers omit those conditions and pay for speed. They prove that Vey funded the expedition and that Coss exceeded the written authority in her copy; they do not by themselves prove whether she knew of the rider. Removing them without preserving the case destroys the order of seals and some signatures.

### Trial crown segments

Several copper-and-iron arcs were built to test replacement geometry. They are valuable, can repair the acceptance collar, and serve as excellent crown-chain splice material. Taking all of them makes later reconstruction easier and deprives Harrowgate of evidence that alternatives were deliberately rejected.

## Operating the manifold

### Stabilize at middle water

Balance the Open Palm cache, set the Kneeling Saint halfway, and pulse the Returning Breath bell. This is the safest general state. It requires either two operators, the pallbearer, or a temporary counterweight.

### Flood deliberately

Close the lower culvert and accept water from the Ropeworks. High water weakens load ghosts, opens the royal niche, and creates generous trapped-air routes. It also carries loose oil, bodies, and relics upward toward the Lantern Cistern if the separator is not isolated.

### Drain deliberately

Raise the Kneeling Saint or reverse the Water Drum. Low water exposes salvage and the Chapel ledge but strengthens load ghosts, threatens Rhea's air, and increases Black Rain pressure. A controlled drain is useful. A full drain without a lower plan sends the danger downhill.

### Seal the room

Use emergency fittings and the saint manifold to isolate the Reliquary from both upper and lower water. This creates a possible safe camp and preserves the room as an operating base. It consumes one seal or requires a durable repair.

### Rupture the lower gate

The party may choose speed, deny pursuit, or deliberately send water toward a controlled-collapse plan. This permanently worsens Black Rain, closes the royal niche, and may sweep useful burdens out of reach. It also opens a fast but perilous descent.

## Routes by water state

- **Water lift to the Ropeworks:** usable at high or middle water; at low water the cage hangs above the floor and requires climbing or counterweighting.
- **Mourning conduit to the Lantern Cistern:** usable as an air line at any state; physically passable only at high water or after removing grates.
- **Dry ledge to the Inverted Chapel:** narrow at middle water, broad at low water, submerged at high water.
- **Royal niche toward the King's Narrow Grave:** open only at high water or when the Closed-Eyes Saint is manually pressurized.
- **Lower culvert to Black Rain:** swimmable at high water, controlled at middle water, a hot vertical drop at low water, and a torrent when ruptured.

Keep at least one route open in every water state. The level changes what is easy, what is exposed, and who is endangered.

## Hard choices

- Rescue Rhea immediately, or spend her remaining air stabilizing a more favorable water state.
- Take the Common Measure rack for the strongest replacement route, or leave its public record intact and copy it under pressure.
- Preserve the pallbearer as an operator, or break it for fittings needed elsewhere.
- Drain for salvage and accept greater danger below, or flood for rescue and risk contaminating the Lantern Cistern.
- Open the royal niche for a fast route after Orren, or hold the room at the level best suited to the wounded and the Common Measure.
- Return named relics to Low Choir households, place them under Warden custody, honor Lady Vey's legal claim, or treat them as Harrowgate's emergency repair stock.

## Clues and useful discoveries

Searches, declarations, and successful operations can reveal:

- the copper saints can preserve air and control local water without dumping the whole room into Black Rain;
- the Common Measure failed politically rather than mechanically;
- a replacement burden requires voluntary weights, an accepted frame, Chapel recognition, and Wells balancing;
- Orren's loyalists used the royal niche route, followed by Captain Rook;
- Chief Factor Halren Coss issued a concealed accelerated-possession schedule beyond the base contract;
- the lower culvert touches the mountain fault; and
- the Chapel pivot station can be reached across the dry ledge.

## Outcomes

Record:

- the water level and whether it is stable, locally isolated, or ruptured;
- Rhea Colm's fate, testimony, and willingness to aid the party;
- whether the pallbearer is cooperative, hostile, destroyed, or reassigned;
- the disposition of the Common Measure, Pilgrim's Yoke, acceptance collar, seals, flasks, and trial crown segments;
- which claims were acknowledged and which evidence was preserved;
- whether the royal niche, Chapel ledge, and Black Rain culvert are open;
- whether the load ghosts were enlisted, quieted, or destroyed; and
- what additional pressure was sent upward or downward.

A visit can succeed without stripping the room. Leave with one rescued person or strong operator, one replacement-burden asset, and one water decision that follows the party deeper.

encounters.title: The Salt Barracks
encounters.summary: Twenty-three Wardens dispute command while two empty shells patrol and their buried prefect taps below.
encounters.opening_view: One tap comes from beneath the empty command chair. A pause. Two taps. The white-armored sentinels do not turn toward it. “Name. Burden. Authority,” they say to you instead. On the stone bunks behind them, twenty-three preserved Wardens sit in three ranks, each rank watching the others for the first sign of obedience.
encounters.content:
## Situation

The Salt Barracks is a white vault arranged around an empty command chair. Twenty-three Wardens retain judgment here; twenty follow one of three command positions, while Heth Brine and two attendants keep the salt room. Two more shells patrol without judgment, repeating the last route written before their tablets vanished. Most of the others sit still until duty, alarm, or contradiction gives them reason to wake.

The Wardens are not ghosts wearing armor. Each is a maintained person assembled from three continuities:

- a **salt-cured shell**, which preserves bodily habit, sensation, and emotional reflex;
- a **memory tablet** fitted behind the breastbone, which carries a name, sworn duties, selected memories, and the language by which the buried house recognizes an operator; and
- a **muster of witnesses**, living or preserved people who can say that the shell and tablet still belong to the same continuing person.

A Warden remains whole only while shell, tablet, and witnesses still agree. A shell can march and fight but cannot weigh exceptions. A tablet in brine recites records but cannot decide what its remembered feelings mean. A transferred Warden may function without witnesses, yet the command chains mark that person disputed. The safeguard against theft also gives every faction a different way to deny personhood.

The current crisis began before the Ember Company arrived. **Prefect Ardel Quoin**, last undisputed commander of the garrison, ordered an inquiry into whether the Wardens’ sentence had ended. During that inquiry his command tablet disappeared, his shell was sealed beneath the empty chair, and three incompatible duty boards appeared. Each faction accuses another of removing him. In truth, Garden keepers hid the tablet at Quoin’s own request after he learned that the Deep Bell’s continuance order included a lawful release clause. The Garden has since grown through the cracked tablet, obscuring several years of memory and making its testimony incomplete.

Orren Saye exploited the dispute. He passed the Barracks under a royal claimant’s inspection mark, promised the literal-order Wardens that the Crown of Measure would be restored to a lawful line, and sent one sealed order deeper. The inner gate is therefore open to his party, closed against most others, and prepared to report any new command claim to the Wells and Iron Choir.

## First contact

Entrances from the Hall, Ropeworks, and Garden display different credentials. Reception depends on what the party carries.

- A recognized petition mark from the Hall earns formal speech and one hearing before weapons are drawn.
- A Warden law mark, a recovered salt tablet, or Odran Greve’s maintenance testimony earns technical standing.
- Low Choir guides are treated as protected workers by Continuance, emancipated citizens by Release, and assigned dependents by the literal-order faction.
- Lady Vey’s seal, Orren’s contract, or a visible crown component causes the literalists to form ranks around the command chair.
- An openly damaged Warden tablet causes every faction to stop the scene and demand custody.

Without recognized standing, two blank sentinels approach. They ask three questions in the old order: **Name. Burden. Authority.** They accept literal answers, but they cannot interpret jokes, aliases, changed obligations, or divided authority. A party can answer, retreat, bypass them through the bunks, or let another Warden interrupt. Violence awakens the room one rank at a time rather than producing an immediate mass battle.

## The chamber

### The four ranks

Each rank once served a different part of the machine.

- **Gate Rank** holds petition shields, hooked spears, and route seals for the Hall and Feast service hall.
- **Balance Rank** carries short winches, plumb weights, and muster harnesses used in the Counterweight Wells.
- **Mourning Rank** keeps salt veils and memory bowls for toll casualties. Several of its bunks are empty because those Wardens accepted dissolution during earlier crises.
- **Deep Rank** bears blackened armor and tongue-shaped command keys for the Iron Choir. Three have obeyed Orren’s sealed order and already gone below.

Searching a bunk is not ordinary looting. The equipment is inventoried to the person sleeping beside it. A Warden ally can loan tools, grant salvage from an empty rank, or witness lawful requisition. Taking gear secretly marks the bearer as a grave robber to Barracks mechanisms and to any Warden who later recognizes the item.

### The empty command chair

The chair is carved from one block of salt-veined granite. A narrow cavity beneath it contains Quoin’s shell, still capable of reflex and feeling but unable to identify itself. The shell taps three rhythms against the stone: muster, dissent, and Garden water. Anyone who listens without treating the tapping as an attack can learn that Quoin consented to the tablet’s removal.

The chair recognizes command through three independent forms rather than one magic token:

1. a command tablet or lawful temporary tablet;
2. the witnessed assent of at least one functioning Warden from two ranks; and
3. acceptance of a defined duty that the buried house can test.

A claimant with all three can issue durable orders. Two are enough for a local emergency command lasting until the next toll. One permits speech through the chair but no obedience. This allows proof, coalition, personal sacrifice, or force to matter without making Quoin’s damaged tablet the only path forward.

### The salt room

Behind the Mourning Rank lies a workshop of brine troughs, blank tablets, spare salt ribs, and three unfinished relief shells. **Quartermaster Heth Brine**, whose left arm belongs to a former Gate Warden, tends the room. Heth is not neutral, but refuses to let factional advantage determine whether a damaged person receives care.

Heth can teach or perform the principal tablet operations:

- **Read:** place a tablet in cool brine and let it speak surviving inscriptions. This reveals records but leaves the shell insensible.
- **Rejoin:** return an intact tablet to its recognized shell before witnesses. A hurried rejoining may scramble recent sequence but normally restores judgment.
- **Repair:** grow salt across a crack using filtered Garden brine, one recovered memory, and witness testimony. Repair cannot create certainty where no evidence survives. The repaired Warden chooses whether an unknown interval remains blank or is marked with other people’s accounts.
- **Transfer:** fit a tablet into a relief shell. The Warden retains duty and selected memory but gains unfamiliar reflexes and may reject the new body. A living bearer can accept a tablet temporarily, but the command pressure intrudes on sleep, speech, and personal priorities until removed.
- **Release:** dissolve a tablet in clean water after the Warden states a name and relinquishes duty before witnesses. The shell dies. Its memories enter the water and may be returned to families, the Garden, or the Iron Choir.

Heth will not perform transfer or release without the Warden’s consent unless the tablet cannot answer and recognized witnesses agree that an emergency duty was already chosen. That standard is inconvenient in a crisis and intentionally so.

## The three positions

### Sister Vesra and Continuance

**Sister Vesra of the Balance Rank** keeps one hand on a hanging plumb weight and speaks in conditions: if the Crown moves, then this chain takes it; if that chain fails, then these streets fall. Nine Wardens support her, though two are wavering. She believes the first duty is to prevent Harrowgate’s destruction. She will repair, replace, or redistribute the burden, but will not consent to Crown removal while the nearest consequence remains unnamed.

Vesra’s tablet lacks six years. During that interval the first Low Choir petitions were suppressed, and she cannot remember whether she participated. She does not deny the possibility. She insists that guilt she cannot prove should not be used as a convenient reason to abandon people now alive. Returning one of her missing memories may harden her, break her position, or let her offer a more honest compact.

Vesra offers disciplined guides, a Wells crew, law marks, and temporary control of the inner gate. Her price is a declared stabilization plan and a promise not to remove the Crown while the bell remains physically dependent on it.

### Prior Dalca and Release

**Prior Dalca of the Mourning Rank** loses a little salt whenever he closes his hands. Six Wardens support him. He quotes the ending clauses of old orders and leaves the beginnings unstated. The Wardens’ duty, he argues, was a sentence with an end condition, not an eternal identity. Avarra’s burden, the Low Choir’s inherited harm, and the garrison’s preservation have all outlived the authority that imposed them.

Dalca favors the Common Measure, distributed stabilization, or controlled collapse. He will also accept evacuation followed by the machine’s destruction. He refuses any repair that simply restores the old sentence. His personal urgency is real: his tablet is sound, but his shell cannot survive many more tolls, and he wants the right to choose release before duty makes the decision for him.

Dalca offers Garden contacts, the Mourning routes, witnesses for voluntary burden, and Wardens willing to dissolve their tablets into a replacement memory medium. His price is a credible end to inherited service and recognition that release is not desertion.

### Sergeant Cleth Varn and literal obedience

**Sergeant Cleth Varn of the Gate Rank** commands five Wardens in the Barracks and claims the two blank sentinels whenever no higher order is recognized. Three Deep Rank supporters have already gone below under Orren’s seal. Cleth speaks in imperative verbs and refuses consolation. He does not call the old orders just. He asks what preserved soldiers become if they revoke their own authority while keeping their weapons. His board says: hold the gate, protect the chain, surrender command to a lawful royal line.

Orren showed Cleth Lady Vey’s sealed genealogy and base recovery contract without revealing the accelerated-possession rider or the missing safety lines in his extraction copy. Cleth therefore believes Orren’s party is conducting an ugly but lawful restoration. Proof of the rider and abridged sequence weakens this position but does not answer who now possesses authority.

Cleth offers immediate gate discipline, Deep Rank command keys, and a direct pursuit route after Orren. His price is recognition of a lawful commander—Lady Vey, Quoin restored, a valid emergency marshal, or another claimant the chair accepts. If defeated without such a replacement, Cleth’s sealed orders continue traveling below.

## Resolving the command crisis

Secure passage, manageable opposition, and a command relationship the party understands; unanimity is unnecessary. Several settlements work.

### Restore Prefect Quoin

Recover the tablet from the Garden, repair or acknowledge its missing intervals, rejoin it to the shell, and provide two witnesses. Quoin remembers the lawful release clause but not who removed the tablet. Quoin’s first order is a temporary joint command: stabilize immediate danger, permit Crown replacement if accepted, and convene a final muster after the crisis. This is broad but not morally clean. Quoin will not command Wardens to dissolve or surrender the Crown to a private claimant.

### Recognize a faction commander

Vesra or Dalca can take the chair if the party secures assent from another rank and helps define a testable duty. Vesra’s command is strongest for controlled repair and Wells operations. Dalca’s is strongest for replacement, evacuation, and release. Cleth can command if shown a valid royal authority, but his orders privilege Crown restoration and may place Low Choir routes under military control.

### Establish joint command

Two faction leaders can share emergency authority by dividing duties: one responsible for Harrowgate’s physical survival, one for release and affected people. The chair accepts this only if each leader states what the other may forbid. Joint command gains more personnel but requires the party to carry disagreements into the finale rather than settling them here.

### Appoint a guest marshal

A living character may accept a blank temporary tablet and a defined emergency duty before two ranks. This grants local command and access to the lower muster stair. Until released, the character hears every unresolved Barracks order as a physical tug and cannot honestly claim ignorance of Warden casualties. A self-serving or vague duty causes the tablet to crack.

### Conduct a barracks coup

The old muster law permits a nonlethal command challenge in the rectangle between bunks. The challenger must hold the command plumb while opponents try to take it, force a knee, or prove the declared duty contradictory. The room’s machinery shifts shields, opens brine channels, and changes footing according to which rank supports whom. Victory compels local obedience but does not erase dissent. Killing a Warden during the challenge breaks the muster and turns the remaining factions into independent armed groups.

### Break or bypass the gate

The inner gate can be forced with Ropeworks power, cut through after local water isolation, or bypassed through the Garden root door. Progress remains possible. The costs are explicit: warning tongues sound below, hostile Wardens follow on disciplined intervals, and no Barracks crew operates the Wells unless later reconciled. Rejecting the faction scene never blocks progress.

## Missing tablets and blank sentinels

The two blank sentinels are **Ora Pell** and **Maston Grey**. Their tablets lie in the Garden beside Quoin’s. Ora removed hers voluntarily after refusing an order to seize Low Choir children; Maston’s was taken by Cleth’s predecessor to erase testimony. Their shells now execute the same patrol, one by choice and one by theft, and the difference cannot be learned from the shells alone.

Recovering the tablets creates distinct decisions:

- Ora’s tablet asks not to be rejoined. She will testify in brine and then choose release or archival transfer.
- Maston’s tablet demands rejoining and a formal accusation against the old command chain.
- Rejoining either without hearing the tablet gives the party a useful soldier while repeating the Barracks’ central abuse.
- Leaving the shells blank preserves an immediate hazard and an unresolved person.

## Conflict and pressure

If fighting begins, Wardens operate the room rather than merely exchanging attacks.

- Gate Rank closes exits and separates intruders with petition shields.
- Balance Rank changes floor tension and uses harnesses to redistribute carried weight.
- Mourning Rank throws dry salt that draws active memories into visible shapes.
- Deep Rank sounds command tongues that awaken or redirect distant mechanisms.
- Blank sentinels repeat the last successful tactic until someone changes their order, route, or tablet state.

At Shifting or worse, a cracked brine pipe begins dissolving tablets stored in the salt room. At Black Rain, Garden water enters warm and starts unwanted repair growth. At the fourth toll, every Warden loses one recent memory unless protected by ward-light, clean brine, or living witnesses who immediately restate it.

## Resources and routes

A cooperative Barracks can provide:

- up to two disciplined Warden crews for specific operations;
- law marks that open service doors and identify carried equipment as requisitioned;
- three compact muster winches and a counterweight harness;
- Deep Rank command tongues for the Iron Choir;
- salt veils that protect a named memory through one toll;
- blank tablets for emergency command or voluntary transfer; and
- reliable routes to the Feast hall, Garden, Counterweight Wells, and Iron Choir approach.

The lower muster stair descends directly to the Counterweight Wells. The Feast service hall runs behind the Gate Rank. The Garden door opens into the Bitter Bed, where the missing tablets are rooted. A narrow command chase follows speaking tubes toward the Iron Choir; it is fast, exposed, and already marked by Orren’s people.

## Carry-forward states

Record more than “allied” or “hostile.”

- **Command:** Quoin restored, Vesra, Dalca, Cleth, joint command, guest marshal, disputed, or broken.
- **Duty:** continuance, release, royal restoration, divided, or a newly defined emergency duty.
- **Personnel:** crews assigned, dissolved, transferred, damaged, or pursuing the party.
- **Tablets:** Quoin, Ora, Maston, Vesra’s missing years, and any blank temporary tablets.
- **Gate:** cooperative, controlled, forced, bypassed, or alarming the deep works.
- **Promises:** stabilization limits, release rights, recognition of Low Choir standing, Crown custody, and post-crisis muster.

Every command settlement eases one later operation and sharpens one later dispute. Record who reaches the finale able to command, refuse, and remember why.

encounters.title: The Garden of Teeth
encounters.summary: An ossuary garden feeds the living, filters black water, catches names, and hides Harrowgate's pressure vents.
encounters.opening_view: The Garden says your names one heartbeat too early. White caps rise from ordered jawbones in three black beds, speaking in voices that nearly belong to people you know. Warm water enters carrying oil, ash, and scraps of memory. Beyond the silver roots, someone whispers, “Do not answer.” Along the outer wall, numbered shutters wait beneath costs cut too deeply to weather away.
encounters.content:
## Situation

The Garden grew where ossuary, filter house, and burial kitchen ceased to be separate institutions. Jawbones stand upright in black loam. White caps rise from the teeth, and silver roots weave beneath the beds, catching oil, ash, and memory from passing water. The Low Choir eats here, drinks here, remembers here, and can save the town here by destroying some part of all four.

Cool water makes the caps murmur scraps without ownership: a work song, the shape of a door, the smell of a mother's sleeve. Warm black water drives every tooth toward a complete name. Answering gives the Garden a pattern to grow toward. It may take recognition rather than fact: companions know the person is present but forget how they are related, which promises belong to them, or why the absence would matter.

The Garden is working infrastructure with four necessary jobs.

1. It filters black water before that water reaches the Lantern Cistern and Low Choir dwellings.
2. It grows toothcaps, root meal, and salt greens that feed the people below.
3. It catches mnemonic discharge that would otherwise enter surface wells or the Iron Choir in uncontrolled bursts.
4. Its dry root ways and pressure sluices cross the buried house laterally, including a route to the quarry vents.

Destroying the Garden buys immediate relief and creates water, food, memory, and pressure crises. Preserving it unchanged leaves the Low Choir dependent on ancestral remains and exposed to every toll. Show both truths in play.

## Arrival and visible choices

Five routes expose different parts of the ecology: Quarry, Lantern, Barracks, Feast, and Menagerie.

- The **quarry route** reaches the dry upper roots and the vent shutters. It is easiest for bypassing the beds and best for preparing controlled collapse.
- The **Lantern conduit** enters beside the first filter bed. Water, oil, or wick-eaters displaced above arrive here.
- The **Barracks door** opens directly into the Bitter Bed where missing salt tablets are hidden.
- The **Feast stair** reaches the tended beds, food stores, and Garden keepers.
- The **Menagerie tunnel** crosses refuse pens and can release maintenance beasts if opened carelessly.

No route requires a living name as payment. The Garden keepers know work names, salt mouthpieces, water rhythms, and covered walkways that permit safe crossing. A desperate traveler can feed the Garden a name to grow an instant bridge or reveal a path, but this is an exploit of the system, not the intended solution.

## The keepers

**Edda-of-the-Warm-Stone** is the senior keeper present. She is a broad, elderly Low Choir woman with toothcap flour on both arms and a copper cup tied over her mouth. Edda speaks through gesture, written slate, and short work names while in the beds. Outside the warm mist she is direct and impatient with anyone who calls the Garden merely a graveyard or merely a farm.

Edda’s priorities are practical:

- preserve enough food for the next month;
- stop contaminated water from reaching the Feast hall;
- recover the Warden tablets without surrendering them to the faction that caused their removal;
- keep the quarry vents available for Harrowgate’s evacuation plan; and
- prevent the Wardens or surface claimants from taking the silver root mesh as treasure.

Her apprentice, **Kell Nine-Spoons**, is a teenager who knows every dry route and has recently begun losing the reason behind several household names. Kell can guide the party quickly, but warm mist causes him to answer voices he recognizes. Protecting Kell is not required for passage. It makes later Low Choir negotiations personal and preserves an expert route guide.

Three other keepers work deeper beds and can be introduced as a group unless the scene needs individuals. They do not fight to the death for the Garden. They shut sluices, release spores, hide in root hollows, and bargain with access to food and clean water.

## The three filter beds

### The Jaw Catch

The first bed is built from ordinary burial bone and coarse salt loam. It catches grit, metal filings, blood, and the heavy black flakes that rise from the fault water. The white toothcaps here are edible if cut before they begin speaking. A careful harvest supplies a week of trail rations for a party or one day of food for the Low Choir.

The Jaw Catch is currently overloaded by Reliquary pulses. Clearing it requires shoveling hot black sediment, redirecting water, using the pallbearer or a maintenance beast, or sacrificing one section of root mat. Failure sends oily contamination toward Lantern and wakes the caps into a grasping carpet.

### The Silver Root

The middle bed is a woven mesh of pale roots threaded with old memory wire. It catches names, duties, and relational impressions. The material resembles valuable silver but cannot be removed in quantity without collapsing the filter. Small cuttings serve as mnemonic sutures, Warden-tablet repair fiber, or components for the Common Measure’s witness frame.

Memories caught here can be recovered by cooling a root, naming the intended recipient, and drawing the impression into a cup, salt veil, or living witness. Pulling without a recipient gives the nearest creature an intrusive relationship: it may remember itself as someone’s parent, debtor, murderer, or promised guide until the memory is placed elsewhere.

At the center of the mesh grows a tight black knot called **the Widow Root**. It contains decades of unreturned names from toll victims. Cutting it would release a powerful wave of memory, perhaps restoring many Low Choir records or overwhelming everyone nearby. Leaving it preserves filtration but keeps those memories inaccessible.

### The Quiet Loam

The final bed is deep dark soil mixed with dissolved salt tablets, cremation ash, and the remains of exhausted toothcaps. It removes the last mnemonic heat from the water and grows salt greens along its edges. Properly filtered water leaves here gray, cool, and safe enough for cooking.

The Quiet Loam also remembers commands. Old Warden phrases spoken nearby cause roots to form temporary straight lines, opening or closing service passages. This is how Orren’s party crossed toward the Feast route without dealing with the keepers. The command pattern remains and can be followed, erased, or turned into an ambush.

## The name hazard

Escalate the name hazard through signs; do not reduce it to one roll that deletes a character.

### Exposure signs

1. Teeth whisper work names or titles the party has used.
2. A character hears a true name spoken in the voice of someone trusted.
3. The Garden repeats a relationship: “my captain,” “her brother,” “their debtor.”
4. Another character briefly forgets why the exposed person matters.
5. The Garden grows a pale likeness or route shaped by the offered identity.

Interruption, cooling water, salt over the mouth, strong ward-light, or another person deliberately restating the relationship can stop escalation. If the Garden takes a name, record one lost recognition. Recover it through the grown cap, a returned memory, a salt veil, or reenactment of the relationship beyond the Garden's hearing.

### Safe methods

- Wear copper or waxed-cloth mouth covers and communicate by sign.
- Use temporary work names that describe the present task without claiming identity.
- Keep the nearest water cool and moving.
- Carry a lit Ossuary lamp; this suppresses speaking caps but directs caught memory toward the Iron Choir.
- Follow a keeper who taps route rhythm on jawbone rails.
- Spread dry salt across a narrow bed, accepting damage to that harvest.
- Move through the upper roots without entering the mist, if the route has not shifted.

### Dangerous leverage

A living name can be used intentionally to make the Garden act. Offering one may:

- grow a bridge across a broken filter;
- identify a route associated with that person’s duty or ancestry;
- lure a name-eating swarm away from someone else;
- awaken memory in a Warden tablet; or
- open a root gate that no current keeper knows.

The cost should match the leverage. The Garden takes a relationship, legal recognition, or remembered obligation connected to the offered name. The party can later recover it, but not by pretending no cost occurred.

## The Bitter Bed and the missing tablets

The Barracks ossuary door opens beside a bed whose caps taste of mineral bitterness and speak in clipped military cadence. Three salt tablets are rooted here.

### Prefect Ardel Quoin

Quoin’s command tablet is split diagonally and wrapped in silver root. It remembers ordering an inquiry, learning that the original Warden compact permitted release when an accepted replacement burden existed, and asking a Garden keeper to remove it before the literal-order faction could suppress the finding. It does not remember the keeper’s face, the final vote, or the years immediately before removal.

The tablet can be:

- read in place, where the Garden fills gaps with nearby memories and may create false confidence;
- cut free carefully, preserving the root as repair fiber;
- torn free quickly, losing one surviving memory but avoiding a long exposure;
- repaired in the Garden using caught Low Choir memories, which risks confusing command with the people harmed by it; or
- left as an independent witness rather than returned to Quoin’s shell.

Quoin’s recovery changes Barracks command but does not produce a perfect ruling. The damaged record proves that a release clause exists and that Quoin consented to removal. It cannot prove which current faction deserves command.

### Ora Pell

Ora’s tablet lies under a cap shaped like a closed hand. It records her refusal to seize Low Choir children during a food riot and her voluntary separation from her shell so that the literal command could not operate through her body. Ora will speak from cool brine. She asks not to be rejoined without a new freely chosen duty.

### Maston Grey

Maston’s tablet has been nailed beneath a jaw plate and nearly overgrown. It records that a former commander removed it after Maston witnessed falsification of the Low Choir ration count. Maston wants rejoining, formal testimony, and command accountability. He is furious that his blank shell has been used as evidence that tablet removal was always voluntary.

Recovering all three is valuable but not mandatory. Each tablet asks a different question about continuity, consent, and useful service.

## Food, water, and harvest

The Garden can provide concrete resources.

- **Toothcap cakes:** compact rations that remain edible for weeks if kept dry. Eating one near active ward-light may produce a harmless borrowed memory.
- **Salt greens:** bitter leaves that reduce mnemonic intrusion and help a person distinguish personal memory from transferred impressions.
- **Gray water:** filtered water safe for drinking and for Warden-tablet release.
- **Silver-root cuttings:** limited repair and memory-transfer material.
- **Name brine:** concentrated fluid that can awaken a tablet, power an Iron Tongue, or dangerously imitate authority.
- **Bone loam:** heavy, stable mass suitable for temporary counterweight fill.

The party may harvest a modest expedition supply without harming the Low Choir. Large extraction, sale, or use as replacement mass creates a claim that must be negotiated. Edda can state exactly how many household-days each proposed load represents.

## The pressure sluices

Three root-lined shutters connect the Garden to quarry cracks and sacrificial bone beds.

- **Upper Jaw** sends a modest pulse into abandoned quarry galleries. It can relieve local water pressure or buy time on the tremor clock if the surface vent is open.
- **Widow’s Run** spreads a larger surge through the Silver Root and releases caught memory into Harrowgate’s lower streets. It protects stonework but risks a surface memory event.
- **Last Teeth** opens the entire Garden as a crush and heat sink. It is a prerequisite for the safest controlled-collapse sequence, but it destroys most food beds, ancestral remains, and dry routes.

The shutters require force at two separated handles or a substitute crew, beast, harness, or Warden mechanism. They can be prepared now and opened later through Ropeworks or Iron Choir controls if the linkage remains intact.

Preparation need not sacrifice the Garden. Brace routes, evacuate stores, move tablets, warn surface crews, and decide which beds are expendable. Controlled collapse then carries visible human and material costs.

## Crossing and operating the Garden

### Guided passage

Earn Edda’s cooperation, protect a keeper, repair the Jaw Catch, return a memory, or acknowledge the Garden’s food claim. A guided group can reach any active exit without name loss unless the state changes violently.

### Silent upper crossing

Climb the silver-root ribs above the mist. This avoids the name hazard and most keepers but risks collapse, wick-eaters at lit-dark boundaries, and a long fall into speaking caps. It is the fastest route between Quarry and Barracks.

### Water crossing

Raise the local channel and float across on saint pallets, coffins, or improvised boards. This suppresses spores and exposes submerged valves. It also moves contamination and may carry loose tablets toward Lantern or Feast.

### Burn a lane

Ward-oil or ordinary fire clears a direct route. A narrow controlled burn costs one bed and releases recoverable memories in silver smoke. An uncontrolled fire can destroy the filter, spread through dried root ways, and produce a cloud in which everyone remembers incompatible versions of the dead.

### Feed the Garden

Offer bone, memory, command brine, or a living name to grow a temporary route. Bone is slow, memory is unpredictable, command brine creates obedient but brittle geometry, and a living name is fast with personal cost.

### Force the root gates

A Gate Warden crew, Ropeworks tension line, Menagerie burrower, or determined party can break through. This preserves forward movement but damages routes and may leave the Garden unable to isolate water later.

## Encounters and moving pressure

Let the Garden’s threats arise from its current state.

- **Speaking carpet:** caps knit across a path and repeat increasingly intimate names. Cutting it opens a route; cooling, feeding, or redirecting it may preserve the bed.
- **Name-eating bloom:** a cloud of pale spores pursues the strongest unspoken relationship in the group. It can be trapped in a memory cup or led into ward-light.
- **Wick-eater migration:** creatures driven from Lantern nest along the edge of the lit Ossuary bough and carry stolen reasons into the caps.
- **Blank sentinel patrol:** Ora and Maston’s shells enter from the Barracks, asking Name, Burden, Authority while the Garden speaks answers around them.
- **Black-water reversal:** one bed floods from below, exposing a safe high route and threatening food stores or tablets.
- **Keeper resistance:** Edda’s crew closes sluices and uses hooked harvest poles, sleep spores, and route knowledge to stop destructive extraction.
- **Lamp hunter:** if not dealt with in the Quarry, it stalks the upper roots, extinguishing guide lamps and forcing a choice between darkness and pursuit.

Violence changes the Garden's state; the room never resets for a later visit.

## Garden states

Track the Garden as one of several broad states, with local exceptions if useful.

### Tended

Food, filtration, and guidance function. The name hazard is controlled. Keepers can move memory and operate vents. This requires cooperation or at least restraint.

### Overgrown

Warm water or unattended memory causes rapid growth. Routes change, food becomes hazardous, and the Garden can produce powerful but unreliable bridges and visions. Cutting back takes time or a displaced cost.

### Flooded

Speaking caps submerge and most spores settle. Water routes improve, dry routes close, and tablets or silver root may tear loose. The Feast hall and Lantern Cistern receive whatever the party does not isolate.

### Harvested

The party or Low Choir removes significant food, root, loam, or memory. This supplies resources now. Record the household-days, filtration loss, and political claim rather than treating it as free treasure.

### Burned

Name hazards and many creatures die. Stored memories release in smoke, filtration fails, and Low Choir food security collapses. Some routes become clear while others cave as roots shrink.

### Vented

One or more pressure sluices are prepared or opened. The Garden becomes part of the surface survival plan. Each opened shutter has a separate cost; only Last Teeth destroys the whole system.

## Routes and carry-forward effects

- **Quarry Cleft:** upper roots and pressure shutters; best controlled-collapse preparation.
- **Lantern Cistern:** filter inlet, oil contamination, and wick-eater migration.
- **Salt Barracks:** Bitter Bed, missing tablets, and a bypass around the inner gate.
- **Feast of Empty Chairs:** food stair, gray-water outlet, and Low Choir households.
- **Menagerie of Quiet Beasts:** refuse tunnel and access to creatures that can dig, filter, or carry dangerous memory.

Record:

- state of each filter bed;
- food and clean-water security;
- Quoin, Ora, and Maston tablet locations and wishes;
- names or relationships taken, returned, or stored;
- silver-root and name-brine extraction;
- keeper disposition and Kell’s condition;
- each pressure shutter as closed, prepared, opened, broken, or inaccessible;
- route states; and
- where displaced water, memory, spores, and wick-eaters went.

The Garden pays in household-days. Before the party leaves, name what each taken resource was already doing and who must now do without it.

encounters.title: The Feast of Empty Chairs
encounters.summary: The Low Choir feeds its living and absent at one table, then asks what Harrowgate will owe.
encounters.opening_view: The bread is hot, and no one seems surprised that you have come. Fewer than half the chairs are occupied, but every empty place has been served: a clay cup, a small duty weight, a name carved by another hand. A child slides an unclaimed bowl toward you. “Who above would notice,” they ask, “if your name did not come home?”
encounters.content:
## Situation

The Feast fills an old ration hall and the dwellings cut around it. Brick ovens warm the chamber; laundry crosses the upper galleries; cooking tile repairs the royal mosaics. Every king has been covered. The laborers remain visible. At the tables, absence is given a chair, a cup, and enough ordinary hospitality to keep it from becoming an abstraction.

The hall itself holds one hundred ninety-two chairs. Fewer than half are used by living diners. At every empty place rests a clay cup, a small duty weight, and a name incised in a different hand from the one before it. The cups do not contain ghosts. They hold witnessed memories drawn out of the ward-light or caught by the Garden's silver roots: a mother's way of testing bread with one knuckle, the order of a quarry song, the smell of rain on a street that no longer exists, the reason one person forgave another. The Low Choir sets food before these places because remembrance without ordinary hospitality becomes an archive, and an archive can be closed.

The **Low Choir** lives in the hall and its cut-stone dwellings. Shared recollection becomes harmony in the Bell's channels: one voice can be dismissed as error; several independent voices speaking the same name become a record the machine must recognize.

The third toll took seventeen names from the Feast district. Three have been recovered in the Garden. Four more survive in cups whose living owners no longer know why they weep when they touch them. If the fourth toll sounds while the Mourning Bough remains fully lit, every unshielded household here will lose another anchor memory.

## First reception

The Low Choir neither attacks strangers on a known route nor mistakes them for rescuers. A child or elder asks each visitor three practical questions:

1. **Whom did you leave above who would notice if your name vanished?**
2. **What have you carried into this hall that belongs to someone else?**
3. **Which promise made in Harrowgate are you actually empowered to keep?**

Answers may be plain. Refusal closes the household passages but leaves the public hall open. An obvious lie earns no magical punishment and no later trust. Showing a public commission, a Warden recognition mark, rescued Company testimony, food, clean water, a recovered cup, or a person the Choir feared dead changes the opening disposition immediately.

Respect household boundaries and the Feast can support a safe camp, surgery, and ordinary conversation. A full rest costs one household-day of food and clean water per two guests unless the party supplies its own or repairs a local system. A toll during the rest may still strike memory unless the party prepares cups, dims the Mourning Bough, or accepts another protection cost.

## Nara-of-the-Seventh-Name

**Nara Vale** introduces herself as **Nara-of-the-Seventh-Name**, then speaks the six names she carries: Mere, Hama, Voss, Rill, Tett, and Orra. They keep unfinished contracts, kinship, debts, and testimony addressable. The seventh name is her own, spoken last whenever someone mistakes inherited duty for ownership of its bearer.

Nara wants an enforceable compact with Harrowgate before the old arrangement continues for another season. She will accept temporary stabilization if it buys time for rescue, surface preparation, and a replacement burden. She will not accept an indefinite promise to discuss reform after the town is safe. Her preferred outcome is a Common Measure whose obligations are public, bounded, and carried by several communities rather than by one crown or one buried people.

Nara speaks in household measures: sacks of grain, gate hours, signatures, inspection dates, beds for the displaced, names of people empowered to stop the work. “Destiny does not take the night watch,” she says. Bring Nara a generous principle without an operator, route, or remedy; she answers with broth, a chair, and no endorsement.

## The four household positions

The Low Choir is not unanimous. Its households share routes, food, and memory craft, but they disagree about which danger is tolerable.

### The Warm Table

**Bera Loam**, an oven keeper with two burned hands, speaks for households dependent on Garden food, gray water, and ward-light. The Warm Table fears an immediate shutdown that leaves children hungry, invalids in darkness, and the lower dwellings flooded before Harrowgate opens surface housing.

Bera will support controlled continuance for a defined term if the party secures food, water, passage, and a stop condition. She offers cooks, stretcher bearers, Garden labor, and a safe camp. She opposes burning the Garden, extinguishing all four lamp boughs, or releasing the crown before the Wells are ready.

### The Open Cup

**Tern-of-One-Name** refuses inherited names and argues that no survival service justifies another involuntary toll. His households have prepared packs, ash shrouds, and a route toward the Quarry Cleft. They want the Mourning Bough severed and the Deep Bell silenced even if the Feast must evacuate.

Tern can provide black-water masks, guides through dark routes, and volunteers for controlled collapse. He will not consent to a replacement burden that can quietly become permanent. He can be persuaded by a short, testable emergency term with an automatic release clause; he cannot be bought with treasure or royal recognition.

### The Kept Chain

Nara's households maintain records, cups, duty weights, and surface correspondences. They seek legal recognition, regular passage, shared maintenance, and remedies that do not depend on future goodwill. They are the strongest supporters of the Common Measure, but only if the affected bearers speak for themselves at the Chapel.

The Kept Chain can supply three voluntary household weights, trained witnesses, an acceptance liturgy, and the labor needed to carry the frame. Its members will expose any attempt to use a royal seal as a substitute for consent.

### The Narrow Line

**Illa Crownless**, a genealogy keeper, descends from Avarra's household through a line excluded from House Vey's surface register. She does not claim that blood alone makes her queen. She argues that Lady Vey cannot call the crown private inheritance while ignoring the buried line that maintained its sentence.

The Narrow Line wants access to the King's Narrow Grave, public comparison of the three genealogies, and a voice in the crown's disposition. It may support return to Lady Vey, shared custody, destruction, or a civic trust depending on what the records show. Illa offers a servants' passage, mortuary signs, and one living line of the chained genealogy. She withholds them from anyone promising the crown before hearing the buried claim.

These positions overlap. A household may feed with the Warm Table, entrust records to the Kept Chain, and still plan evacuation with the Open Cup. The party does not need unanimous support. It needs to know whose labor, consent, testimony, and routes each settlement actually uses.

## Memory cups

A memory cup is a vessel for witnessed recall, not a cure-all and not a portable soul. Each cup bears a name, an anchor mark, and at least two witness strokes. A cup without a living witness becomes increasingly ambiguous. A living witness without a vessel can preserve testimony, but the next toll may shear away the sensory and emotional detail that makes it usable by the machine.

### Listening

A person may warm a cup between both hands and receive a brief sensory impression. This reveals what kind of memory it holds without transferring it. Listening is safe unless the cup is cracked, contaminated with black water, or opened during a toll.

### Witnessing

Two people who independently knew the memory may speak its name, place, and consequence over the cup. This stabilizes the vessel and lets it serve as proof at the Scriptorium, Chapel, Iron Choir, or a Warden continuity hearing. One true witness plus corroborating material evidence can suffice, but the machine marks the record as repaired rather than complete.

### Carrying

A willing creature may drink from a prepared cup and carry the memory temporarily. The carrier can recall the stored event as if present, use a forgotten route rhythm, recognize a person, or speak an acceptance line the original witness knew. Until the memory is returned, the carrier gives up one comparably vivid personal recollection. It is not destroyed, but it becomes inaccessible and may bleed into the borrowed memory under stress.

No one can be made a stable carrier merely by forcing liquid down their throat. Coercive transfer produces confusion, false familiarity, and an unreliable record. The Chapel and Iron Tongues can distinguish voluntary carrying from imposed occupancy.

### Returning and redirecting

A carried memory can be returned to its cup, poured into a compatible Iron Tongue, rooted in the Garden, or transferred to another willing carrier in the presence of witnesses. Returning the memory restores the carrier's displaced recollection. Breaking the cup releases the memory into nearby ward-light or water, where it may reach an unintended recipient.

### Shielding a toll

Four prepared cups and four willing donors can shield one household cluster, safe camp, or operating crew from the next mnemonic discharge. Each donor places a chosen memory in a cup before the toll. The memories can later be returned if the vessels survive. This is a practical defense, not an invitation to demand sacrifice from the same people already bearing the bell.

The Low Choir has twenty-three sound empty cups, eleven cracked vessels suitable only for immediate listening, and seven cups currently holding memories needed by living people. Nara will not release the last category as general-purpose tools without the owners' consent.

## Inherited names

An inherited name preserves a social address when the original bearer has been erased from living recognition. It can carry:

- a debt or obligation that someone freely accepts;
- standing to testify about a household record;
- access to a route, cup, or maintenance office keyed to that name;
- kinship continuity for children whose parent has been forgotten; and
- a claim to be heard where the old machine would otherwise treat the person as never having existed.

It does **not** transfer the original person's body, marriage, property, guilt, or authority wholesale. The bearer must state which duties they accept and which they refuse. A household must witness the inheritance. The name can later be laid down when records and relationships have another secure home.

This distinction matters at the King's Grave and Inverted Chapel. A chained genealogy can establish standing without proving exclusive ownership. A duty name can authorize maintenance without surrendering the bearer's life to the mechanism. Nara will demonstrate by speaking Mere's unfinished grain promise, Hama's route witness, and then her own refusal to inherit Voss's punishment.

## The six compact weights

The Low Choir has translated generations of grievance into six obligations that can be fitted to the Common Measure. Each is represented by one or more small duty weights. None works as symbolic apology alone; each names a continuing practice and a remedy.

1. **Witness:** Harrowgate keeps a public register of the Low Choir, recovered names, toll losses, and maintenance decisions. Records remain accessible above and below.
2. **Passage:** the people below may travel, settle, trade, and seek aid on the surface without royal or Warden leave.
3. **Provision:** Harrowgate supplies grain, clean water, medicine, and temporary housing while the Garden and cistern systems are repaired or replaced.
4. **Maintenance:** surface crews, Warden operators, and Low Choir keepers share scheduled work. No community can be assigned the whole machine by default.
5. **Limit:** every emergency burden has a stated term, inspection interval, and maximum tolerated toll cost.
6. **Remedy:** breach triggers a real response—automatic shutdown, evacuation, release of the crown, transfer of authority, or another action the affected bearers can invoke.

The weights do not need to be accepted exactly as Nara presents them. The Chapel can recognize another compact if it names equivalent authority, consent, duration, and remedy. Removing an obligation lowers the frame's legal stability and usually shifts material load onto another component. For example, refusing Provision requires faster evacuation or more Garden capacity. Refusing Remedy makes the frame resemble Avarra's coerced sentence and gives the Chapel's execution machinery leverage over it.

### What Harrowgate can presently promise

The party's public commission covers rescue, requisition, ordinary salvage, and immediate stabilization. It does not by itself authorize permanent settlement, crown disposition, taxation, or hereditary recognition.

Useful surface commitments may come from several sources:

- Warden Marr can promise emergency passage, temporary housing, public records, and a council hearing.
- Master Tarrow can commit quarry crews and maintenance schedules if the town survives.
- Lady Vey can bind House Vey's grain stores, genealogy archive, retainers, and claim to the crown, but not the elected town.
- a recognized Warden commander can bind buried-house operators and access routes;
- Low Choir households can bind their own labor, weights, and consent; and
- rescued witnesses can expose later repudiation even when they cannot legislate.

A coalition of bounded promises is therefore more credible than one grand signature. The Common Measure is designed to hold several such obligations side by side.

## Social and operating scenes

### The place that should not be empty

One chair is newly set for a living person the party has met: Tavia Hest, Rhea Colm, Jessa Noll, Pell Varo, or another endangered delver. The cup at the place contains a memory caught during the third toll. Returning the person, carrying the memory to them, or admitting that the party left them behind changes the Feast's disposition more than abstract persuasion.

### The disputed child

Two households remember raising **Soli**, a ten-year-old cup keeper. Soli remembers both homes and refuses to choose which memory is false. A recovered Garden name shows that the households were once one extended family divided by an earlier toll. The scene demonstrates that restoration can complicate identity rather than simply repair it.

### The last bowl

The Warm Table has enough toothcap and salt greens for three household-days after the current meal. Feeding rescued outsiders, preparing an evacuation, and supporting a deep operating crew all draw from the same stock. The party can bring supplies, improve the Garden, shorten its stay, or knowingly spend someone else's margin.

### The surface voice

If the party can reach the Chapterhouse by runner, chain message, or released memory, the Low Choir asks for one surface authority to hear and answer the six obligations before the fourth toll. Marr, Tarrow, Lady Vey, or a delegated party member each creates a different compact. Delay is permissible, but temporary continuance then requires explicit limits.

### A cup that implicates an ally

One recovered memory shows a respected Warden, royal officer, or Ember Company member choosing to redirect a past toll into the Low Choir. The memory is partial but genuine. The party can preserve it, confront the implicated faction, use it as leverage, or suppress it. Nara cares less about punishment than whether the new settlement prevents the same private decision.

## Routes

- **Garden food stair:** the broadest route, normally controlled by keepers. It supports stretchers and supplies but closes if the Quiet Loam floods or the Feast is attacked.
- **Barracks service hall:** a salt door admits recognized Warden crews, household envoys, or anyone carrying a valid duty tablet. Forcing it alarms the Barracks.
- **Scriptorium ration chains:** narrow hanging baskets and maintenance ledges reach the archive. They can move cups, documents, or one careful climber at a time.
- **Reliquary mourning ledge:** available at low or middle water. It enters through a wash room where cups can be cooled and decontaminated.
- **Inverted Chapel mourning stair:** a steep stair ends at the Chapel's Mourning Brake. It is the safest route for witnesses and the Common Measure, provided the Chapel has not dropped.
- **King's Grave servants' passage:** hidden behind the Narrow Line's genealogy wall. It opens only with buried-line signs, a Scriptorium concordance, or physical excavation.
- **Black-water crawl:** Tern's evacuation route reaches lower conduits toward Black Rain. It is fast, dark, and unsuitable for heavy loads or unprotected memory vessels.

## Conflict and force

The Feast has no standing army. It has doors, boiling water, smoke flues, knowledge of every crawlspace, and many people capable of making an invader's route expensive. Violence here rapidly becomes a hostage and fire problem rather than a clean battle.

If attacked, households scatter cups and children into different routes, cut ration chains, flood the wash room, and call Garden keepers or sympathetic Wardens. A victorious party can seize weights, cups, and guides, but coercive consent will fail at the Chapel and every humane ending becomes harder. Register that cost without declaring the crawl unwinnable.

## Carry-forward states

Record the Feast broadly as one of these states, then note household exceptions.

- **Sheltered:** the hall remains a refuge; households are cautious but cooperative.
- **Compacted:** enough households and surface authorities have accepted specific obligations to support a replacement burden.
- **Divided:** households support incompatible outcomes and will contribute only separately.
- **Evacuating:** routes, food, and guides are committed to moving people upward or toward a prepared deep refuge.
- **Tollbroken:** memory loss, violence, fire, or betrayal has shattered common witness; individual households may still aid the party.

Also record food remaining, cups allocated, memories carried, inherited names invoked, compact weights promised, surface authorities contacted, and which households have consented to which finale architecture.

## Results

Leave the Feast with people, duties, and terms—not just information. It can provide a safe camp, guides, witnesses, household weights, black-water equipment, genealogy standing, rescue labor, and routes to the Chapel or Grave. It can also impose deadlines and expose the human cost of apparently functional machinery.

Low Choir endorsement never gates the Deep Bell. Bypass or alienate the Feast and lose witnesses, humane operators, evacuation capacity, and some chance that a replacement will differ from the old coercion.
