encounters.title: The Inverted Chapel
encounters.summary: An inverted sanctuary turns judgment into position, weight, and the right to withdraw.
encounters.opening_view: The chapel hangs roof-first beneath you. Pews, altar, witness rails, and iron candles wait fifty feet down on four strained chains. Merrit Dole hangs below the altar in penitent irons, conscious and very still. From a barricaded brake platform across the shaft, Elra Venn calls, “One more step.” Her hand settles on the release lever.
encounters.content:
## Situation

The Chapel hangs in a shaft wider than the chapterhouse above it. From the arrival balconies, the sanctuary lies fifty feet below and upside down: pews, altar, witness rails, and iron candles fixed to the present ceiling. Four pivot chains pass through the nave into separate brake houses; a fifth descends toward the Wells. Every claimant must occupy the physical position their argument assigns to someone else.

The old court rotated the chapel when Queen Avarra was sentenced. It needed one structure to serve as courtroom, execution platform, maintenance bridge, and burden-transfer frame while denying the condemned sovereign equal ground with her judges. Later operators kept it because no other station can recognize a new legal burden and pass it into the Wells.

The mechanism reads declared roles, witnessed consent, bounded terms, remedies, and physical balance. Force the forms and it will accept an unjust arrangement with visible instability. Offer a benevolent promise without authority, duration, or remedy and it refuses the load.

## What is happening now

The sanctuary rests in **Inverted Rest**, its usual sealed state. The Mourning Brake near the Feast is intact. The Breath Brake near the Reliquary is wet but operable. The Judgment Brake toward the Scriptorium is held by an Ember Company rigger. The Service Brake near the Menagerie crawl is fouled with feathers, chain grease, and one broken guardian wing.

**Merrit Dole**, a Low Choir mourning guide, hangs beneath the altar in the chapel's penitent chains. He entered after the second toll to recover an acceptance response and declared, in frustration, that he would carry Harrowgate's whole debt if no one above would name it. The old execution compulsion treated the statement as consent. He has survived on water lowered from the Feast and cannot free himself without a valid release, a careful rotation, or destruction of the bearer station.

**Rigger Elra Mott** controls the Judgment Brake from a barricaded platform. She followed Orren Saye's search party because he promised triple hazard pay and a share of the crown metal. Orren used her to turn the chapel, took the royal route when it opened, and left her with two dead companions when a chain-wing guardian struck. Elra has wired her brake to run free if anyone rushes the platform. She wants a safe route out, written protection from both the Ember Company and Harrowgate, and proof that Orren cannot later claim she sabotaged the expedition.

Neither Merrit nor Elra is required to operate the chapel. Each can make it safer, faster, and more human.

## The five chapel states

Moving between adjacent states requires control of two pivot brakes, or one pivot brake plus the Wells counterchain, a heavy external brace, or a dangerous manual traverse. A complete half-turn normally takes several minutes and produces a clear sequence of groans, moving shadows, and shifting debris. During a tremor or fight, resolve it in stages so characters can react.

### Inverted Rest

The sanctuary hangs upside down beneath the balconies. The Mourning and Breath approaches are easiest. The Scriptorium judgment chain reaches a side rail. The Wells door is sealed behind the altar floor. The chain-wing guardians are slow because their perches are inverted.

Crossing is possible by descending onto the undersides of pews, traversing chain handholds, or rigging a line across the shaft. Loose objects fall into the lower dark. Merrit hangs twenty feet below the nearest stable surface.

### Mourning Turn

The chapel rotates one quarter-turn toward the Feast. Pews become ladders and the mourning aisle becomes a vertical wall. The Feast stair, Reliquary ledge, and Scriptorium chain all connect through the nave. Cups placed in the mourning font can be cooled, witnessed, or passed safely toward the Iron Choir.

This is the best state for rescuing Merrit without accepting his declaration. It is also the state in which old grief records become audible through the iron candles. Prolonged exposure can impose borrowed mourning on anyone carrying an open memory cup.

### Upright Hearing

The sanctuary stands as a conventional chapel, though the shaft remains open around it. The Wells door, civic acceptance collar, four declaration stations, and lower route to the Iron Choir become accessible. This is the only stable state for consecrating the Common Measure or another replacement burden.

Upright Hearing shifts physical load onto the Counterweight Wells. If the Wells are unbalanced, one floor quadrant rises while another sinks. Operators can still work, but every declaration must be made while managing a visible material failure.

### Execution Turn

The chapel rotates one quarter-turn away from the Feast. The accused rail becomes a floor, the execution chute opens toward the Choir of Iron Tongues, and the Menagerie ceiling crawl connects to the Service Brake. The old royal return toward the King's Narrow Grave can be exposed from this state if the chained genealogy is present.

Execution compulsions are strongest here. Unassigned people are sorted into accuser, bearer, witness, and remedy roles by moving chains. The state is useful for forcing a royal burden through without full consent, breaking a hostile guardian formation, or making a rapid one-way descent. It is the most dangerous state in which to improvise.

### Dropped Nave

If two brakes run free, a pivot chain is severed, or the Wells counterchain fails during rotation, the chapel drops until one or more safety chains catch it. It becomes a steep broken bridge across the shaft. Some routes open permanently and others are crushed or lost.

A dropped chapel can still be crossed and may even create the shortest path to the Deep Bell approaches. It cannot perform a clean acceptance unless raised or extensively rebuilt. Cutting it loose entirely sends enormous mass toward the lower works, changing the Wells and Iron Choir state and risking a premature toll.

## Operating the pivots

Each brake house contains a handwheel, ratchet, speaking tube, and role plate. The plates name the operators as **Mourner**, **Breather**, **Judge**, and **Servant**. These are maintenance roles, not moral ranks.

To rotate safely:

1. inspect the intended stopping dogs and clear debris;
2. establish communication among at least two brakes;
3. take or provide counterweight through the Wells chain, rigging, water, or distributed personnel;
4. release adjacent brakes together;
5. arrest at the next state; and
6. set both dogs before moving people or heavy objects.

A failed operation should change position, route, injury, or machine state rather than merely consume time. Useful failures include:

- one side moves first, turning the nave into a steep slope;
- a brake heats and must be cooled with Reliquary water or ward-oil sacrificed as lubricant;
- a safety dog catches early, leaving a route open but the acceptance station unusable;
- a guardian seizes a loose chain and redirects the motion;
- Merrit's penitent chain takes load and begins to injure him; or
- the Wells counterchain lifts unexpected mass elsewhere in the dungeon.

The Ropeworks can provide synchronized line, Pell Varo can repair one brake, Warden crews can hold a station, Garden root fiber can replace a frayed signal cord, and burden-bearer statues or quiet beasts may supply controlled mass. None is mandatory.

## Traversal without rotation

A party may cross or descend without operating the whole chapel.

- **Underside traverse:** move across pew backs and candle chains in Inverted Rest. Fast climbers need only one anchor line; wounded people and heavy loads require a second.
- **Judgment chain:** the Scriptorium route reaches a narrow rail and can be tensioned into a bridge. Doing so temporarily disturbs one archive chain family.
- **Mourning net:** the Low Choir can rig cup lines and burial cloth into a broad catching net, permitting a slower group crossing.
- **Breath lift:** controlled Reliquary water fills copper bladders beneath one balcony, raising a temporary platform. A reversal can strand it.
- **Condemned chute:** Execution Turn opens a fast one-way descent to the Iron Choir approaches. It is difficult to reverse and marks users as condemned in the lesser mechanisms.
- **Wells counterchain:** a skilled climber can descend beside the fifth chain regardless of chapel state, but movement in the Wells may carry them unexpectedly.
- **Severed bridge:** cutting selected pew and aisle chains creates a rough bridge at the cost of future acceptance stability.

The chapel is therefore a route set piece, not a mandatory rotation puzzle. Operating it well preserves options and creates leverage; bypassing it trades those benefits for speed or damage.

## The execution compulsions

Four old legal roles are built into rails, chains, and speaking stations.

- **Authority:** who has standing to assign or recognize the burden?
- **Bearer:** who actually consents to carry it?
- **Witness:** who can independently attest to the consent and terms?
- **Remedy:** who or what acts when the burden is exceeded, breached, or revoked?

The chapel reacts when people make declarations near the stations, especially in Execution Turn. A person saying “I will bear it” may be chained as Bearer. Someone accusing another may be drawn to Authority. A silent observer may be fixed as Witness. A weapon or demolition charge can be classified as Remedy.

The compulsions can be handled in several ways:

- assign the roles deliberately before entering;
- answer the stations with bounded statements;
- carry a Warden duty tablet or Low Choir witness weight that clarifies standing;
- darken the Mourning Bough and move without speaking;
- jam or cut individual role chains;
- rotate out of Execution Turn; or
- accept a temporary role and complete a formal release.

The machinery does not detect lies in the abstract. It detects contradiction between declared role, recognized authority, witnessed consent, and later action. A clever false declaration can work briefly, then return as a chain seizure or failed transfer when the contradiction becomes material.

## Merrit Dole, the penitent

Merrit is exhausted, furious, and embarrassed by the sentence that caught him. He refuses to let anyone describe his outburst as noble consent. He will cooperate with a rescue that preserves the bearer station, but he accepts destruction of the station rather than indefinite captivity.

Ways to free him include:

- rotate to Mourning Turn and speak a witnessed release distinguishing compassion from consent;
- present Nara's testimony that Merrit lacked authority to bind the whole Low Choir;
- transfer his temporary bearer role to a willing, bounded carrier and release it immediately at Upright Hearing;
- counterweight the altar, slacken the chains, and pick or cut the cuffs;
- sever the bearer rail, damaging future acceptance; or
- drop the nave onto a prepared net and extract him during the impact.

Merrit knows the mourning responses, Feast route, and names of two Iron Tongues that can store transferred memory. He can serve as a witness but will not become the Common Measure's permanent bearer. Rescuing him gives Nara evidence that the Chapel can recognize revocation. Abandoning him leaves an unresolved coercive declaration in the machinery.

## Elra Mott and the Judgment Brake

Elra has food for one day, a cracked rib, and a spool of excellent rigging wire. She believes Captain Rook may protect her but does not know whether Rook survived. She has Orren's spoken order recorded in a memory sliver: turn the Chapel, open the royal return, and leave any Low Choir witness behind.

Elra's brake barricade is defensible but not impregnable. She bargains more readily than she fights.

She will release or coordinate the brake for any two of the following:

- a protected route to the Feast, Reliquary, or surface;
- written recognition that she acted under Orren's order and later prevented a drop;
- treatment for her injury or confirmation from Rhea Colm;
- credible news of Rook, Pell, Tavia, or other Company survivors;
- a share of ordinary salvage not including the crown; or
- help recovering her companions' bodies from a guardian perch.

Threats may gain immediate compliance, but Elra will run the brake at the first sign the party intends to abandon her. Killing or disabling her leaves the wired brake live until someone understands her rig.

If befriended, Elra can operate any pivot, repair the Wells signal clutch, and testify against Orren. She admits she joined a predatory contract and asks no stranger to absolve her.

## Chain-wing guardians

Three brass guardians called **appeal wings** patrol the shaft. Each resembles a narrow human torso folded inside two latticed chain wings. One is damaged at the Service Brake. They were built to prevent unsignaled rotation and to carry last appeals between stations.

They respond to imbalance, contradictory declarations, severed chains, and unassigned heavy movement. In conflict they do not simply claw intruders. They hook equipment, exchange people's positions, pin declared roles to stations, and arrest a moving pivot at the worst possible angle.

Ways to manage them include:

- signal the intended turn through two speaking tubes;
- present a valid appeal, Warden command, or Low Choir witness response;
- assign one guardian to carry Merrit's release or another bounded declaration;
- lure them with moving counterweight rather than living prey;
- darken the Deep or Mourning Bough to reduce their perception;
- repair the damaged wing and gain a temporary operator; or
- destroy them, leaving future rotations without automatic arrest.

A repaired appeal wing can accompany the party to the Wells or Iron Choir and carry one declaration or light load. It obeys procedure, not friendship.

## Accepting a replacement burden

The Chapel can recognize the Common Measure, a repaired Crown arrangement, a temporary emergency burden, or another designed frame. Recognition does not physically balance the Deep Bell. It creates a legible legal burden that the Wells and control chains can receive.

### Material preparation

A candidate burden needs:

- a frame capable of taking the mechanical interface, such as the Common Measure's copper acceptance collar;
- enough physical mass or a clear connection to distributed mass in the Wells;
- named maintainers or operators;
- marks or witnesses connecting each component to a declared obligation; and
- a route from the Chapel to the Wells and Deep Bell.

The Reliquary provides the Common Measure handweights, collar, trial crown segments, and Pilgrim's Yoke. Other materials can substitute if engineered and documented.

### The four declarations

At Upright Hearing, speakers occupy four stations.

1. **Authority:** name the person or coalition empowered to establish this burden and the limits of that power.
2. **Consent:** name every community or bearer contributing labor, memory, property, office, or risk, and show how each assented.
3. **Duration:** state the term, inspection interval, transfer rule, and conditions under which the burden must be reconsidered.
4. **Remedy:** state what happens when consent is withdrawn, limits are exceeded, maintenance fails, or authority is abused.

The same person may speak more than one declaration, but no declaration can supply its own independent witness. Unanimity across Harrowgate is not required. Specific consent from actual bearers is.

### Testing the frame

The Chapel loads the candidate in stages. Duty weights lift, the Pilgrim's Yoke transfers a fraction of the strain, and the Wells counterchain answers. Participants can revise a term, remove a weight, add a remedy, or stop the procedure before full recognition.

A successful acceptance produces a stable response in the four stations and opens the Wells transfer door. The frame becomes **consecrated to a named burden**, not sacred in a general sense.

A partial acceptance may still be useful. It can support emergency stabilization for one toll, recognize a route or operator, or prove that a coerced component is the source of instability.

### Forced acceptance

A royal seal, Warden command tablet, or sufficient physical force can drive a burden through in Execution Turn without complete consent. This opens routes and may stabilize the bell temporarily. It also marks the frame with an execution clause: when strain exceeds its declared limit, the machinery seeks a living bearer or condemned substitute.

Forced acceptance is a viable dark choice, not a secret failure screen. Telegraph the clause through tightening chains, missing witness responses, and Merrit's sentence.

## Chapel pressure scenes

### Rotation during a tremor

The shaft moves while one brake is released. The party must choose whether to arrest early, complete the turn, protect Merrit, secure Elra's platform, or preserve a route carrying rescued people.

### The appeal that cannot be proved

An appeal wing presents a memory fragment from Queen Avarra or a forgotten laborer. The statement is relevant but lacks an independent witness. The party can delay to find corroboration, accept it as repaired testimony, or reject it and preserve procedural certainty.

### A bearer withdraws

During acceptance, one household, Warden crew, surface authority, or player character revokes consent. The Chapel pauses rather than immediately failing. The party can reduce the burden, replace the contribution, renegotiate the term, force the declaration, or abandon the attempt.

### Orren's return line

Elra can open the same royal route Orren used. Doing so improves pursuit toward the King's Grave but moves the Chapel toward Execution Turn and gives royal seals priority in the next operation.

### The shortest route is the cruelest

Dropping the chapel creates a rapid bridge to the lower works while destroying the acceptance station and threatening Merrit, Elra, or household witnesses. The party may still choose it under clock pressure.

## Routes by state

| Route | Inverted Rest | Mourning Turn | Upright Hearing | Execution Turn | Dropped Nave |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Feast mourning stair | open to brake | broad access | open | difficult | variable |
| Reliquary ledge | open | open | open | partly blocked | flooded or crushed |
| Scriptorium judgment chain | narrow rail | open | open | broad access | severed or bridge |
| Menagerie ceiling crawl | blocked | difficult | high crawl | open | variable |
| Counterweight Wells | sealed | service slit | open transfer door | chain descent | exposed chain |
| Choir of Iron Tongues | deep traverse | cup line | lower stair | condemned chute | broken bridge |
| King's Grave return | hidden | hidden | sealed | open with genealogy | variable |

Use the table as a starting state. Rigging, excavation, water, allied labor, or deliberate damage can change any route.

## Carry-forward states

Record the Chapel as one of these states, plus brake and route details.

- **Inverted:** sealed but stable; acceptance unavailable.
- **Turned:** held at Mourning or Execution quarter-turn; several lateral routes improve while others worsen.
- **Upright:** Wells and acceptance stations available; physical load transferred downward.
- **Consecrated:** a named burden has been accepted, with declarations and witnesses recorded.
- **Dropped:** the nave is a damaged bridge; acceptance requires repair.
- **Severed:** the chapel has fallen or been dismantled, permanently changing lower load and routes.

Also record Merrit's condition, Elra's disposition, each brake, guardian status, declarations attempted, coercive clauses, accepted weights, and whether the Wells transfer door is open.

## Results

The Chapel can provide a safe deep route, a rescued witness, an Ember Company operator, an appeal-wing assistant, access to the Wells and Iron Choir, a royal pursuit route, and legal recognition for a replacement burden. It can also become a damaged shortcut or a weapon dropped into the lower machine.

The Chapel can be bypassed, damaged, or abandoned. Its unique gift is no moral permission; it makes consent, limits, and remedy legible to machinery built around coercion.

An accepted burden leaves the Chapel legible but still needs physical mass, path, and timing at the Wells.
The Chapel can recognize a bounded replacement burden but cannot make it physically sufficient.
The Chapel tests material preparation and the four declarations required for accepted transfer.

encounters.title: The Menagerie of Quiet Beasts
encounters.summary: Four purpose-bred beasts consume heat, vibration, loose memory, or panic until hunger widens the task.
encounters.opening_view: Three taps. A pause. Two taps. Hollis Fen keeps the rhythm with a spoon against the wicker cage above the gallery. “Walk,” they say. “Do not run.” Below, velvet hounds listen to each footfall, white moths gather around spoken names, and something translucent follows fear through the floor. The painted boundary lines are faded. Every creature still knows where its line lies.
encounters.content:
## Situation

The Menagerie is a maintenance arsenal bred instead of forged. The buried house produces excess heat, trapped vibration, severed memory, and contagious panic; its keepers answered with appetites. Each beast consumes one excess and ignores most others until the work ends and hunger widens the definition.

Every bronze cage stands open. The beasts remain inside territories painted around their thresholds: a soot-black lizard watches flame; velvet hounds follow footfalls without turning their heads; white moths gather around spoken names; a glass animal listens through the floor. Bars made frightened beasts fight their keepers. Marked territory, prepared appetite, and an obvious return trail let them choose the work and come back.

Ward-light once reinforced the boundaries. With the Ossuary Bough unstable, lines are fading. Nothing here is required for the Bell, but every borrowed advantage creates a handling duty.

## First contact

Quarry, Garden, Chapel, and Black Rain each enter beside a different appetite. Arrival triggers attention, not an automatic attack.

- Open flame causes the coalheart lizard to stand and taste the air.
- Heavy or repeated steps draw the velvet hounds to the edge of their painted floor.
- Spoken names make the white moths settle into letter-like shapes.
- Racing hearts wake the glass sleeper beneath its wool cover.

A brass keeper's gong hangs beside every entrance. Striking it once announces an operator. Striking it twice requests a beast. Striking it three times means uncontrolled excess and opens all return gates. The third signal was meant for a staffed emergency. With only one surviving handler, it is now an invitation to a regional disaster.

## Hollis Fen, surviving handler

**Hollis Fen**, an Ember Company animal handler and trap specialist, is suspended in a wicker work cage above the central floor. A snapped Chapel traverse dropped the cage and tore Hollis's left shoulder from its socket. They have kept the beasts calm for two days by tapping keeper rhythms with a spoon.

Hollis joined Orren's party because the contract promised hazard pay and because no one else in the company understood living maintenance tools. They refused to release the moths against Low Choir witnesses and were marooned when Orren's loyalists crossed toward the Grave. Hollis knows:

- Orren carried a royal sequence plate and intended to enter the Narrow Grave before returning to the Deep Bell;
- Captain Rook ordered every beast left contained unless a named operator accepted responsibility for its return;
- the black-water throat can be cooled by the coalheart or quieted by the velvet hounds, but not both at once without a second handler;
- one of the hounds followed an uncontrolled toll vibration into the wall and may emerge elsewhere after the next tremor; and
- the Menagerie records distinguish a beast's useful appetite from its starvation behavior.

Freeing Hollis requires raising the cage, crossing a keeper line, or lowering it into one enclosure. Hollis can direct that enclosure's beast while injured. Treatment, a sling, or a functioning appeal wing makes them a mobile operator. Hollis treats rescue as a debt of thanks, never a transfer of ownership.

## The handling law

Every release needs three things. The old keeper plates call them **appetite, boundary, and return**.

1. **Appetite:** identify the exact excess the beast is meant to consume and present enough of it to wake the trained behavior. “Protect us” is not an appetite. Heat from a pipe, resonance in a chain, spilled memory in a cup, or panic in a wounded crew is.
2. **Boundary:** mark where the work ends. Keeper chalk, ward-oil, salt line, running water, Warden command marks, or a continuously held sound can define a boundary. A vague instruction does not.
3. **Return:** provide a trail back to the enclosure or another prepared resting place. The return may be scent, heat, vibration, a spoken keeper name, or a carried wool pad. If the work ends without a return, the beast seeks the nearest related stimulus.

A handler may improvise any of the three if they understand the creature. On failure, widen the appetite, erase the boundary, or sever the return trail. The beast becomes a specific moving complication, not generically hostile.

A beast can be transported in a keeper harness, guided loose, or installed temporarily in a target region. Harnessed transport is safer but requires hands and limits climbing. Guided transport is faster but exposes every related stimulus along the route. Installation creates the strongest effect and the greatest risk of the beast claiming a new territory.

## The four principal beasts

### Cinderback, the coalheart lizard

Cinderback is long as a coffin, low to the ground, and armored in dull plates that brighten from within as it feeds. It consumes heat gradients: open flame, hot metal, fever, and the pressure heat carried by black water. It does not need to bite the source. It lies against stone or pipework and drinks warmth until its plates glow.

**Useful work:**

- cool the Black Rain Cistern enough to approach a valve or injured crew;
- extinguish a basin fire without spending water;
- draw heat out of a seized brake, chain, or Crown Drum fitting;
- preserve a body or salt tablet threatened by warm water; or
- create a cold route through a fire or steam hazard.

**Risk:** once the named heat is gone, Cinderback follows the nearest warmer thing. That may be a ward lamp, a living body, a Reliquary air bell, or the Garden's warm root bed. If allowed to feed without a boundary, it can extinguish an entire lamp bough and leave chilled survivors unable to move.

**Handling:** feed it a warmed copper tile, bound its work with two cold lines, and carry its basalt sleep-stone as the return. It dislikes running water and will not cross a Reliquary saint's active stream unless starving.

**Violence and salvage:** when threatened, it presses against metal armor or weapons and steals heat from the bearer, then lashes with its heavy tail. Killing it yields four heat-storing plates and a coalheart gland useful for one major cooling operation. The plates do not reproduce the creature's judgment; they absorb heat until they crack.

### The velvet hounds

Three narrow hounds occupy a floor covered in black felt. Their ears are sealed folds, and their paws never click. They consume patterned vibration: footsteps, machinery chatter, chain resonance, shouted cadence, and the repeated impacts that precede structural failure. They hunt a rhythm rather than a creature.

The hounds are **Murmur**, **Latch**, and **After**. Murmur follows the strongest vibration. Latch pins itself between source and structure, drinking the transmission. After remembers a rhythm and follows it later. The missing wall-hound is After; it entered a maintenance slot while pursuing the third toll.

**Useful work:**

- suppress one line of bell resonance while a chain is repaired;
- quiet an Iron Tongue row or prevent it from calling Wardens;
- mask a group's movement through a sound-sensitive region;
- stabilize a vibrating bridge or brake long enough for one operation; or
- draw a dangerous repetitive mechanism away from people.

**Risk:** when the named rhythm stops, the hounds seek a substitute pattern. Marching crews, heartbeats, spoken chants, and the Deep Bell's frame are all viable. Total silence does not calm them; it leaves them hungry and attentive to smaller living rhythms.

**Handling:** establish a target rhythm, draw a felt or oil boundary, and keep a return metronome tapping at the enclosure. A hound can be recalled by its individual cadence. Confusing their cadences makes them trade targets.

**Violence and salvage:** the hounds fight by interrupting balance, breath, and coordination. They shoulder a combatant at the instant of commitment, swallow shouted orders, and hold vibrating weapons between their jaws. A dead hound's felt organs can damp one route or device for a scene, but deteriorate after exposure to loud sound.

### The white name moths

The moth cloud rests around a dead keeper's mask. Each wing carries fragments of handwriting. The swarm consumes **unattached memory**: recollection spilled into light, water, metal, or air without a willing carrier or stable vessel. The moths were bred to clean failed transfers and prevent loose commands from haunting the machinery.

**Useful work:**

- remove an unstable memory cloud without forcing it into a person;
- strip Orren's command residue from a route, guardian, or Deep Rank order;
- clean a cracked cup or Iron Tongue before a deliberate transfer;
- separate one intrusive remembered command from a Warden shell; or
- make a short corridor safe from name bleed after a toll.

**Risk:** once loose memory is gone, the moths test spoken names, titles, promises, and recently recalled faces. They do not immediately devour identity. They first erase the connection between a word and the obligation it carries. A hungry swarm may leave someone remembering a loved face but not why it matters, or retaining a duty while forgetting who assigned it.

**Handling:** present the contaminated vessel, surround the work with witness cords or silver-root fiber, and keep the dead keeper's mask as the return focus. A stable voluntary memory cup repels them. A false name attracts them because its contradiction sheds loose associations.

**Violence and salvage:** flame scatters the swarm but risks feeding the lamp-memory channel. Water clumps the moths into readable sheets. Ward-oil traps them at a boundary. Killing the whole swarm yields mnemonic powder that can erase one command mark or blur one pursued trail, but destroys a humane way to clean failed transfers.

### Sable, the glass sleeper

Sable is a translucent, many-jointed animal curled beneath gray wool. Its organs brighten in time with nearby pulses. It consumes contagious alarm: shock, panic, pain rhythms, and the collective fear that makes a crew seize, stampede, or obey the loudest voice. It was designed to keep workers functional during a toll, not to make them docile forever.

**Useful work:**

- calm a panicking rescue group long enough to extract them;
- absorb the shock transferred through a replacement burden's first physical test;
- keep a wounded operator conscious through one major task;
- prevent a frightened beast or Warden shell from escalating; or
- distinguish deliberate refusal from fear-driven incapacity during a dangerous operation.

**Risk:** Sable does not understand healthy fear. If overfed, it leaves people calm enough to accept mortal danger, fail to flee, or agree without emotional comprehension. If starved after waking, it follows the strongest heartbeat and begins drinking bodily rhythm rather than alarm.

**Handling:** place the wool pad within a ring of slow voluntary pulses—tapped fingers, a drum, or measured breathing—name the group and duration, and end with the keeper's resting cadence. Consent matters because people should know that fear is being removed from their decision-making.

**Violence and salvage:** Sable moves through grapples and crowds rather than striking. Its contact slows reactions and can stop an exhausted heart. Cutting it releases stored panic in a wave. Its glass marrow can preserve one person's shock or pain for later treatment, but whoever opens the marrow experiences the stored fear.

## The sealed brood

A fifth enclosure is bricked shut and labeled **grave breath**. A white-furred burrowing brood inside consumes corpse gas, mold, and decomposition heat. Opening it can clear the King's Grave crack, a Garden contamination, or Black Rain deadwork. It also risks releasing creatures that nest in lungs and sealed cavities.

The brood is not necessary to use the Menagerie. Hollis advises leaving it sealed unless the party has a specific contaminated space and a prepared smoke return. The brickwork can also be salvaged as alchemical filter stone without opening the enclosure.

## Moving beasts through the dungeon

Record every region a beast crosses and what related excess waits there.

- **Quarry and Ropeworks:** vibration attracts the hounds; heat and lamp smoke attract Cinderback.
- **Garden:** silver-root memory attracts moths, while warm beds attract Cinderback. Garden keepers can prepare excellent boundaries.
- **Feast:** Sable can protect a toll shelter, but Low Choir households will demand explicit consent and limits.
- **Chapel:** the appeal wings recognize a properly handled beast as a maintenance instrument. An unbounded beast is classified as a condemned hazard.
- **Wells:** hounds can suppress resonance, Cinderback can cool a brake, and Sable can protect a crew. Every creature is at risk if a well drops.
- **Iron Choir:** moths can clean command residue; hounds can prevent a call; either can also destroy evidence or control capacity.
- **Black Rain:** every beast has a plausible use, which makes it the easiest place to overcommit them.

One trained handler can direct one released beast safely. Two beasts require a second handler, a prepared stationary installation, or a meaningful risk. Hollis, a repaired appeal wing, a knowledgeable Garden keeper, or a character who has studied the plates can fill that role.

## Pressure scenes

### The faded line

A tremor breaks one ward boundary while a beast is feeding. The party must preserve the appetite target, redraw the line, establish a new resting territory, or let the beast migrate.

### After returns

The missing velvet hound emerges from a wall following the third toll's remembered rhythm. It may appear in the Ropeworks, Wells, Iron Choir, or Deep Bell. Its return can be helpful if recognized or disastrous if mistaken for an attack.

### Orren's abandoned lure

A royal-sequence chime in the keeper gallery is still tapping. It was meant to draw the hounds away from Orren's route. Stopping it frees the hounds to notice new rhythms; following its chain reveals the Grave return line.

### The appetite is politically useful

A faction asks the party to use the moths to erase evidence, Sable to calm dissent, or Cinderback to extinguish another faction's protected route. The operation may be technically sound and ethically predatory.

### A beast chooses a new territory

After successful work, a creature finds a region rich in its appetite and refuses the return. The party can improve the new territory, offer a stronger trail, compel it, kill it, or accept a lasting ecological change.

## Carry-forward states

Record each beast separately as **contained, prepared, guided, installed, roaming, dead, or harvested**. Also record:

- its current appetite target;
- the boundary and who maintains it;
- its return object or cadence;
- the handler responsible;
- regions crossed;
- what danger it removed;
- what new danger it created; and
- any faction claim over its use or remains.

The Menagerie as a whole may remain **stable**, become **partially emptied**, be **stripped for salvage**, turn into a **new refuge**, or suffer a **general release**. A general release is not a random monster table. Each creature follows its defined appetite into the wider dungeon.

## Results

The Menagerie can provide Hollis Fen, a Black Rain shortcut, rare salvage, and living tools for heat, resonance, loose memory, or panic. It can also export specialized predators into rooms where those appetites are abundant.

Humane play may preserve, kill, bypass, or release these creatures. Ask what each living tool consumes, who owns the work, and where hunger goes after the task ends.

encounters.title: The Counterweight Wells
encounters.summary: Three Wells separate mass, path, and timing; every shortcut makes one loss permanent.
encounters.opening_view: Pera Quill laughs once when the Royal weight rises. It is not amusement. Chains answer through the chamber: one line bows toward Harrowgate, another shivers with voices belonging to the dead. Pera lies pinned beneath a fallen signal frame while Captain Rook and two delvers brace the platform between the Wells. Nothing has fallen. That is the trouble.
encounters.content:
## Situation

Three shafts fall beyond ordinary light, each crossed by a weight large enough to crush a house. The Royal Well carries Crown and cut-chain load; the Civic Well carries accepted public burdens and Harrowgate's ridge; the Funerary Well carries water, memory, and the dead built into the house.

Each mountain groan lifts the Royal weight a finger's width. Orren's cut left it light, forcing strain through the Chapel counterchain into the Civic and Funerary paths: the ridge bows while toll-memory drives toward the Low Choir.

Every plan must answer three questions:

1. **Mass:** what physical or magical load balances the system?
2. **Path:** which chains, drums, frames, and communities actually receive that load?
3. **Timing:** in what order are brakes, water, and weights moved so the bell does not take the difference all at once?

Solving only one question creates a short-term brace or a new casualty.

## Approaches

The Wells have five principal approaches.

- The **Ropeworks royal lift** reaches the Crown Brake above the Royal Well. It is fast if the Crown Drum still functions and treacherous if the royal line is loose.
- The **Barracks muster stair** reaches the Civic gallery and gives a Warden crew room to operate.
- The **Chapel transfer door** reaches the distribution frame where an accepted burden can be attached.
- The **Black Rain lower gallery** reaches piston feet and emergency drain valves.
- The **Iron Choir control walk** reaches timing chimes and remote brake commands.

Two approaches permit safe local work; three make full rebalancing much easier. Chain descent, a cut service wall, or a moving weight can substitute at greater risk.

## The surviving crews

**Engineer Pell Varo** may arrive from the Ropeworks if rescued or contacted. Without Pell, plates, experiments, Warden crews, Elra Mott, Hollis Fen, or player expertise still operate the Wells. Pell's advantage is coordination: he can conduct one major movement while others handle complications.

Three Deep Rank Wardens are already here under Orren's sealed order:

- **Istren Vale** guards the Royal Brake and believes restoring a crowned line is the fastest lawful solution.
- **Malk Salt-Under-Tongue** operates the timing chimes but has discovered that Orren's order omitted the Funerary load.
- **Pera Quill** is pinned beneath a fallen signal frame near the Civic Well and has heard the Low Choir's memory through the chains.

The three are not a unified enemy. Istren may enforce the sealed order. Malk will suspend it if shown contradictory command or physical evidence. Pera wants rescue before law. A recognized Warden commander can recall them, but old command pressure and immediate danger may still require conversation or force.

**Captain Maelin Rook** is also here if she survived the expedition's split. By default, she occupies a braced platform between the Civic and Funerary Wells with two exhausted company members, **Tomas Reed** and **Veyla Sorn**. Rook severed Orren's second demolition line and has held the platform through two tremors. She will cooperate with anyone prioritizing rescue and stabilization, but refuses to surrender her people to Lady Vey's retainers or Warden punishment before the crisis is contained.

If Rook is elsewhere, leave her field signs, cut lines, and written orders here; move the survivors accordingly. The Wells remain operable without her.

## Reading the Wells

Observable evidence lets the party learn the system without guessing.

- Plumb chains show the Royal weight rising, Civic weight descending, and Funerary weight oscillating.
- Chalk arcs left by Pell record how far each moved after the first three tolls.
- Water gauges show that the Funerary pistons take load from the Reliquary and Black Rain systems.
- Chapel response lamps identify whether a candidate replacement burden is recognized, partial, coercive, or absent.
- Iron timing chimes sound one beat before each safe brake window.
- Hairline cracks in the Civic gallery align with Harrowgate streets above.
- Names appearing in condensation on the Funerary chains identify memory and ancestral load being transferred.

A party can test a small movement with hand jacks, portable weights, water changes, or a beast. Safe experiments give clear results. Failed experiments move a component, injure a route, or advance the clock; they never hide the operating principle.

## The three wells

### The Royal Well

The Royal weight is a single red granite block bound in iron bands. A crown-shaped void runs through its center. Its chain bundle once connected directly to the Crown of Measure through the Crown Drum, Chapel royal return, and Deep Bell clapper cage.

Orren cut one royal chain and removed a sequence plate. The weight now rises, loading the bell frame and pulling the Crown toward an uncontrolled strike. Repairing the cut line requires a splice, royal sequence, or substitute coupling. The Grave contains the cleanest sequence and compatible royal metal. The Scriptorium, Ropeworks, and Wardens provide slower alternatives.

Possible Royal Well operations include:

- **splice the Queen's chain:** restore the old load path temporarily, preserving the crown's sentence unless a later extraction is prepared;
- **attach an accepted replacement:** connect the Chapel-recognized frame through the Civic distributor and gradually remove royal load;
- **install equivalent metal:** add crown-bars, reliquary segments, salvage, or other measured mass while preserving the current path;
- **brace the weight:** lock it against the shaft wall, buying time but disabling the royal lift and increasing frame strain;
- **cross-load another well:** move Royal load into Civic, Funerary, water, or surface systems with a named consequence; or
- **drop the Royal weight:** permanently sever the crown path, jerking the bell upward and making crown extraction easier but damaging the upper frame and royal routes.

The Royal Well reacts to recognized authority because its brakes were designed to prevent seizure. Authority can open the mechanism; it cannot make an unsafe load safe.

### The Civic Well

The Civic weight is not one block. It is a cage holding thousands of replaceable stones, each stamped with a district, guild, household, bridge, well, or public obligation. The cage allows distributed maintenance. It also makes hidden political choices visible: later custodians removed affluent surface weights and replaced them with unmarked Low Choir burdens.

The Civic Well is where the Common Measure attaches. Its distribution frame has six receiving arms corresponding to witness, passage, provision, maintenance, limit, and remedy. A complete compact need not use identical names, but every physical arm needs a declared source, maintainer, and failure response.

Possible Civic operations include:

- add or remove district stones to change who bears strain;
- install the Common Measure or another accepted frame;
- reconnect surface foundations through the Ropeworks and Chapterhouse;
- substitute treasury crown-bars, quarry stone, water mass, or suspended salvage;
- expose and remove the unmarked Low Choir weights;
- deliberately spread a short emergency load among consenting crews and institutions; or
- lock the cage as a temporary brace, preserving Harrowgate while preventing further redistribution.

Every new Civic load needs an accessible maintenance route. A brilliant burden sealed behind a collapsed Chapel is not a stable settlement.

### The Funerary Well

The Funerary weight is a lattice of copper coffins, memory vessels, water jackets, and bone-filled counterboxes. It receives pressure from the Reliquary, Garden, Iron Choir, and Black Rain. The original purpose was to let maintenance dead and voluntary memorial burdens continue supporting the system. Later custodians expanded it until involuntary Low Choir memory became ordinary operating mass.

The well oscillates because water and memory are arriving out of phase. A person standing near the chains hears remembered work songs, last instructions, and names the living have forgotten.

Possible Funerary operations include:

- synchronize Reliquary water and Iron Choir memory release;
- return stored memory, reducing mass and requiring replacement weight elsewhere;
- root selected memories in the Garden or transfer them to willing carriers;
- add voluntary Warden tablets or memorial vessels after explicit release;
- isolate the Funerary path, protecting memory while moving load into water or stone;
- brace the coffin lattice for one toll; or
- drop the Funerary weight, sealing many memories below and sending a pressure wave into Black Rain and the Mouth Below.

Destroying the vessels leaves the people represented in them bound. Returning memory, preserving evidence, accepting loss, and preventing immediate catastrophe may pull in different directions.

## The brake houses

Each well has a local brake and all three answer a central **Measure House**.

- The **Crown Brake** releases in seven unequal steps keyed to the royal sequence. A guessed sequence may work until the fourth or fifth step, where accumulated error becomes visible.
- The **Civic Brake** is operated by six levers. Any four can move the cage, but missing obligations determine where excess load goes.
- The **Mourning Brake** uses water pulses and voice chimes. It can be run manually by a crew, through the Iron Choir, or with a Reliquary saint connection.
- The **Measure House** compares plumb, water, and timing. It reveals which component takes the difference; it never chooses who ought to pay.

A single operator can hold one brake. Two trained operators can conduct a local transfer. A full three-well movement normally needs three crews or compensating tools: an appeal wing, Warden detail, quiet beast, prepared Ropeworks drum, hydraulic saint, or destructive one-way release.

## Replacement mass

The Wells measure equivalent load rather than noble blood. Compatible material matters because it must fit, endure, and transmit recognized authority, but the system will accept distributed stone, metal, water, memory, or living labor if properly coupled.

Useful sources include:

- the Common Measure handweights and acceptance collar;
- crown-bars and chain metal from the Narrow Grave;
- quarry stone committed by Harrowgate;
- water held in Reliquary saints or Black Rain pistons;
- Garden bone loam and root tension;
- Warden tablets voluntarily dedicated or dissolved;
- treasure, tools, armor, or structural metal carried by the party;
- temporary human crews using the Pilgrim's Yoke; and
- a quiet beast installed to consume heat, resonance, or panic during the transfer.

A source can supply mass without supplying legitimacy, or legitimacy without enough mass. The Measure House displays both separately.

## Standard operations

### Brace one well

Lock a weight to its shaft using wall dogs, chain wraps, water pressure, or a beast-assisted brake. Bracing buys time and creates a stable work platform. It disables at least one route or transfer and pushes slow strain into the frame.

### Exchange load between wells

Set the receiving brake, open the path, release the sending brake in timed steps, and confirm where the difference appears. A rushed exchange may save one region while damaging another. Name the receiving cost before the final release whenever the party has adequate gauges or expertise.

### Install an accepted burden

Bring the recognized frame through the Chapel door or an improvised route. Attach its material fittings to the Civic distributor. Load it gradually while the Royal path is reduced. Test every declaration arm. If one is partial, the corresponding excess appears as a route, labor, maintenance, consent, or remedy problem rather than generic instability.

### Remove the Crown load

This operation may free the crown, prepare a replacement, or make a controlled collapse possible. It requires a receiving mass or a deliberate drop. The party can reduce the Royal load before reaching the Deep Bell, making final extraction safer, but doing so changes routes and may alert Avarra's retained will.

### Conduct an emergency human hold

The Pilgrim's Yoke and maintenance harnesses let a crew bear a fraction of one well while a brake is reset. This is survivable for a short, witnessed interval with consent, relief rotation, and Sable or medical support. Without those protections, it becomes another coerced burden.

### Drop a well

A drop is a permanent one-way operation. Cut or release the final dogs, open a destination path, and let the weight fall into its sump. The falling mass absorbs a major strain event and buys immediate time. It also destroys routes, assets, and future options according to the well.

## Dropped-well outcomes

### Royal drop

- The crown path goes slack and the Crown becomes easier to remove.
- The Deep Bell jumps upward and damages its upper frame.
- The royal lift, Grave return, and some Scriptorium chains fail.
- Lady Vey loses the cleanest restoration option and may treat the act as destruction of inheritance.
- Harrowgate needs Civic, water, or collapse stabilization afterward.

### Civic drop

- The inhabited ridge is released from immediate load.
- The Common Measure distributor and many surface-foundation links are destroyed.
- The Wells maintenance bridge becomes a broken descent.
- A long-term distributed settlement becomes much harder.
- The town may survive the next toll while losing its buried infrastructure.

### Funerary drop

- Toll-memory stops reaching the Low Choir for a time.
- Stored memories, Warden releases, and memorial vessels are sealed or shattered below.
- Black Rain and Mouth pressure rise sharply.
- The lower bridge becomes flooded or buried.
- Iron Choir evidence may be preserved above, lost below, or violently released depending on timing.

A dropped well is not failure. It converts uncertain future risk into a named permanent loss. More than one well can be dropped, but each additional drop narrows the finale toward evacuation, collapse, or a Mouth Below settlement.

## Counterweight conflicts

### Orren's sealed order

Istren attempts to restore Royal priority while another operation is underway. The party can countermand, persuade, isolate the command line, prove omitted load, or fight over the Crown Brake.

### Rook's rescue line

Rook's platform begins to descend. Saving the crew requires Civic load, a quiet hound, Chapel chain, or abandoning another moving operation. Rook will cut her own platform loose if it prevents a mass casualty above.

### The chain chooses a memory

The Funerary weight catches a loose name or personal memory from someone nearby. Releasing it changes balance. Leaving it in place gives a small mechanical advantage at a human cost.

### A perfect mass in the wrong path

The party finds enough metal or stone, but the only open route would assign it to an unintended population or destroy a retreat. The challenge is not obtaining more weight but changing the coupling.

### The bell moves early

An Iron Choir command, tremor, or Deep Bell action advances the timing window. The party must complete a partial transfer, arrest all brakes, or deliberately spend one component.

## Failure without dead ends

On failed operations, choose a concrete state change:

- one weight moves farther than intended;
- a brake becomes hot, jammed, or one-way;
- a route opens while another closes;
- a crew is pinned or separated;
- load shifts to a named district, household, memory store, or water path;
- the tremor clock advances;
- a beast claims a new territory;
- a Warden order propagates; or
- a well becomes droppable but no longer finely controllable.

After a mistake, use new plumb marks, cracks, water levels, and voices to show exactly what moved.

## Carry-forward states

Record each well as **balanced, braced, redistributed, slipping, severed, or dropped**. Also record:

- actual or estimated mass;
- current load path;
- local brake condition;
- operators and crews;
- linked water and memory state;
- available routes;
- replacement fittings;
- named populations or structures bearing excess;
- timing windows or failed chimes; and
- whether another major operation remains possible.

The whole system may be **stable for one toll**, **prepared for crown extraction**, **prepared for replacement**, **prepared for distributed stabilization**, **prepared for controlled collapse**, or **in cascading failure**.

## Results

The Wells can rescue Rook's surviving company, recall or divide Deep Rank Wardens, attach a replacement burden, reduce the Crown load, establish a safe Deep Bell approach, or convert an imminent catastrophe into a permanent sacrifice.

The Wells decide neither justice nor Crown custody. They make every proposed answer pay its physical bill.

reference_links.context: Recognized Warden crews can hold stations and make load transfers accountable.
Rook refuses premature Vey custody of survivors, while a Royal drop would destroy Vey's cleanest restoration path.
Rook holds the Civic-Funerary platform, protects survivors, and can coordinate rescue without deciding their later judgment.
Varo's advantage is coordinating mass, path, and timing while others handle the Wells' complications.
Quoin's command can supply accountable Warden crews without deciding which load settlement is just.
Nara's compact supplies civic obligations only where each arm has a consenting bearer, maintainer, and failure response.
Rook's surviving crews can provide disciplined labor while resisting premature private custody.
The three Wells, brake houses, crews, operations, and permanent drops are encountered directly.
The Wells assign mass, path, and timing during Drawing Load and Crown Descent.
The Funerary and emergency paths can direct load toward or away from the Mouth without establishing a settlement.
The Royal Well shows the physical load coupled to the Crown and the receivers required before release.
The assembled Measure must be balanced through compatible mass, load path, and timing.

encounters.title: The King's Narrow Grave
encounters.summary: A narrowing royal tomb forces blood, maintenance, and surrender claims to divide its gold.
encounters.opening_view: “By which succession?” asks the coffin. Orren Saye has answered three times. Three sealed genealogies lie across the bier, each lawful, each granting the gold to someone else. The treasury walls press inward one knuckle at a time. Behind Orren, the wounded porter puts both hands against the gold as though shame might hold it back. The coffin asks again.
encounters.content:
## Situation

The Grave is Aldren Harrow's treasury, command crypt, and second coffin. Gold covers every surface; each claimant must call the metal inheritance, evidence, or weight keeping Harrowgate alive.

Aldren preserved three genealogies because each answers a different legal question—and because his successors could invoke whichever one favored them. The optional Grave offers the cleanest royal sequence, compatible counterweight metal, evidence against simple versions of Lady Vey's claim, and substantial wealth. Entering buys easier repairs, extractions, bargains, and betrayals at the cost of time and a decision about what counts as treasure.

## Entrances

- The **chained genealogy** from the Scriptorium opens a shoulder-width door behind the coffin wall.
- The **Reliquary royal niche** enters through a pressure-sealed kneeling passage beneath the Closed-Eyes Saint.
- The **Feast servants' way** reaches a floor hatch used by the people who maintained the tomb without being named in court records.
- The **Chapel royal return** opens during Execution Turn or through a valid genealogy response.
- The **Choir mortuary walk** reaches the command-voice chamber behind the king's head.
- A **grave-breath crack** leads toward Black Rain. It is clogged with mold, corpse gas, and gold leaf.

Each route enters a different part of the defense. A party can leave through another exit even if it does not open the coffin.

## Factor Orren Saye

By default, Orren has reached the Grave with two surviving loyalists, **Kael Dorn** and **Mira Sedge**, plus one wounded porter who no longer supports him. Orren has not opened the coffin. He has used Lady Vey's surface seal, the stolen royal sequence plate, and Elra's Chapel turn, but the Grave keeps asking which genealogy he invokes. He hoped the question would have one correct answer.

Orren is controlled, sleepless, and furious that the chain cut has become one man's madness in every public account. He indicts rather than shouts: which concealed injustice would still be hidden if he had obeyed? His reasoning is coherent and dangerous:

- Harrowgate's authorities concealed the Crown's existence and the Low Choir's burden.
- The Salt Wardens can delay any settlement by disputing authority.
- Lady Vey has money, public standing, and a real blood claim.
- Whoever physically holds the Crown can force negotiations that records alone cannot.
- The bell was already unjust; cutting the chain merely exposed a crisis others preferred to inherit quietly.

He accepted consequences he did not understand and abandoned people when the operation failed. He does not deny either fact. “I cut the chain,” he says. “They built the room in which cutting it was the first honest act anyone could imagine.” He still believes returning empty-handed would restore the old silence.

Orren wants the royal sequence, enough crown-metal to complete an extraction frame, and a route to the Deep Bell. He may bargain for shared custody, offer contract evidence, help operate the Grave, threaten the porter, race the party, or fight over the coffin. If shown the three claims and a credible replacement plan, he may shift from seizure to enforceable leverage. If humiliated or cornered, he uses the retained king's voice to command the crypt and escape toward the Choir.

Lady Vey's recovery trust is the expedition's lawful sponsor, and Lady Vey did not authorize the chain cut. Her written contract conditions recovery on stabilization and witnessed transfer. The contract case and complete sequence show Coss and Rhun adding a possession bonus, debt rider, and abridged sequence; Orren knew the accelerated terms and proceeded without the missing operations. Vey may repudiate their method, but her secrecy, money, and chosen agents created the opportunity. The documents divide culpability rather than absolving or condemning her whole claim.

## The succession vestibule

The grave's first ten feet contain three standing plates and one empty witness niche. Each plate accepts a different form of lineage.

- The **Golden Branch** recognizes descent from Aldren Harrow and opens custody mechanisms.
- The **Burden Chain** recognizes offices and communities that have actually maintained the bell and opens treasury and counterweight mechanisms.
- The **Ash Witness** recognizes Avarra's retained surrender conditions and opens Crown-release testimony.

Any one plate opens a route deeper. Two suppress most defenses. Three allow the king's retained voice to be cross-examined instead of merely obeyed. The empty niche requires a living or preserved witness willing to state what authority they claim and what they do not.

A false claim can activate a plate if supported by seal, memory, or command. The contradiction appears later as a defense assigned to the unsupported part of the claim.

## The three genealogies

### The Golden Branch: custody by blood

Gold wire runs from Aldren's coffin through generations of acknowledged children, collateral heirs, marriages, and adoptions. Lady Merrow Vey descends from Aldren's younger daughter through a line recognized in every surviving surface register. Her descent is genuine.

The Golden Branch grants a strong claim to **custody of Aldren's royal goods**, representation of his extinct house, and participation in any transfer of the Crown. It does not prove that Aldren owned Avarra's retained authority absolutely, that custody overrides the bell's maintenance obligations, or that one descendant may endanger Harrowgate to recover property.

The genealogy also records two disinherited branches. One entered the Low Choir through a marriage the court refused to acknowledge. Another became quarry freeholders and contributed land to the bell's vents. Lady Vey's line is the cleanest, not the only blood line.

### The Burden Chain: succession by maintained obligation

Lead links hidden behind the gold name every office, household, guild, Warden rank, and buried work crew that supplied labor, money, bodies, memory, or repair to keep the bell operating. The chain treats succession as an obligation attached to performance rather than blood.

Under this genealogy, Harrowgate's civic officers, the Salt Wardens, Low Choir households, quarry workers, and maintainers all inherit portions of authority. House Vey appears repeatedly when it paid, witnessed, or repaired; it disappears during generations when it claimed title without contributing.

The Burden Chain grants standing over **maintenance funds, operating decisions, and replacement duties**. It does not grant personal ownership of the Crown or allow inherited obligation to compel unwilling descendants forever. Its later links were manipulated to hide Low Choir contributions under generic “subterranean service.”

### The Ash Witness: Avarra's retained terms

The coffin lid's underside is blackened rather than gilded. Heat reveals a genealogy of witnesses to Avarra's surrender: prisoners, envoys, foster children, oath-bearers, and descendants entrusted with particular remembered terms. It grants no throne. It names the people authorized to testify about conditions the victorious court omitted from public law.

The retained terms include:

- the Crown remains Avarra's instrument until the mountain danger can be borne without her compelled will;
- no descendant of either crown may treat the surrender as personal chattel;
- the people maintaining the burden must receive safe passage, provision, and a hearing when conditions change;
- a lawful release requires witnesses representing victor, surrendered authority, maintainers, and those exposed to the danger; and
- if those witnesses cannot agree, the Crown may be secured but not privately alienated.

Several Ash Witness lines survive among Low Choir inherited names, one Salt Warden tablet family, and House Vey's own maternal ancestry. Nara's Narrow Line has standing, but not exclusive standing. Lady Vey can participate in the Ash claim if she accepts that it limits her custody claim.

### What the genealogies do not do

The three records divide authority; they do not converge on a secret rightful heir:

- blood supports custody and representation;
- maintained obligation supports operation and funds;
- witnessed surrender terms support release and limits.

A coherent Crown settlement may involve all three, a negotiated substitute, or a deliberate rejection with known consequences. Any faction presenting one genealogy as the whole law is omitting something real.

## The retained king's voice

Aldren's body is dead. The crypt preserves a command voice made from his final judgments, court formulas, and selected memories. It speaks through the gold walls in Aldren's measured cadence. It is not a complete ghost and cannot learn freely. It can compare claims, invoke defenses, open treasury compartments, and issue commands recognized by royal mechanisms.

The voice's central directive is: **keep the victory indivisible**. It interprets separation of Crown, bell, treasury, or royal claim as defeat unless shown that all three genealogies authorize the change. This is the old regime's bias, not an objective law of the dungeon.

The party can manage the voice by:

- answering through one genealogy and accepting limited access;
- presenting two claims to force it into consultation mode;
- filling the witness niche and cross-examining contradictions;
- using a white moth to remove one retained command without erasing the records;
- transferring the voice into an Iron Tongue for later testimony;
- drowning the mortuary chamber through the Reliquary niche;
- overriding it with Warden command or Chapel authority;
- severing gold speaking strips; or
- destroying the coffin and fighting the succession defenses at full strength.

The voice can reveal what Aldren knew, but it cannot prove that his account is true. It openly admits that he kept the genealogies separate to prevent any single successor from controlling both Crown and bell.

## Succession defenses

The crypt was designed to punish seizure, not ordinary visitation. Defenses escalate according to unsupported claims.

### The narrowing walls

Gold-sheet walls bow inward around anyone carrying royal metal or claiming sole inheritance. They stop when the claimant names another standing interest or deposits equivalent weight. Bracing, removing the metal, distributing it among several bearers, or advancing through the servants' way also works.

### The gilt mourners

Six flat royal figures peel from the walls. Each carries a ceremonial tool: key, scale, chain, cup, shovel, or sword. They attempt to assign intruders to genealogy plates and confiscate objects inconsistent with the declared claim. In combat they fold around limbs, pin people against gold, and pass seized items through the walls.

The mourners can be redirected by giving them a real custodial, maintenance, or witness task. Destroyed figures become compatible gold plates but remove one defense that could guard the treasury later.

### The indivisible command

If someone tries to take Crown sequence, treasury, and claim records under a single unsupported authority, the king's voice seals exits and orders every royal mechanism below to recognize that person as temporary sovereign. This sounds like success. It also assigns the sovereign every unresolved maintenance debt and makes later machinery seek their body when a burden fails.

A claimant can renounce part of the authority, divide custody, add witnesses, or carry the dangerous recognition deliberately.

### The coffin knight

Aldren's stone effigy rises only if the coffin is forced or the retained voice is destroyed while defenses remain active. It cannot leave the narrow crypt. It uses the corridor itself as armor, driving intruders toward plates, closing exits, and making every blow risk the gold records.

The fight's objective may be to hold a plate, open the coffin, extract a person, preserve a genealogy, or reach the voice chamber. Reducing the effigy to rubble is possible but not the only resolution.

## The royal treasury

The treasury was endowed to maintain the bell in perpetuity. Later kings treated it as a dynastic reserve; later councils borrowed against it without entering the grave. Its contents therefore have several simultaneous claims.

### Six crown-bars

Six rectangular bars of royal gold and meteoric iron fit the Civic distributor or can be forged into a Crown coupling. Each bar supplies one substantial unit of compatible mass. Together they can replace much of the missing Royal load, complete a Common Measure frame, or finance an emergency evacuation and rebuilding effort.

Removing bars triggers the narrowing walls unless equivalent mass or recognized obligation is entered. The Wells do not care whether the replacement is financially valuable; the treasury defenses do.

### The chain sequence coffer

A lead coffer inside the coffin contains the complete seven-step Royal Brake sequence, measurements for the clapper cage, and three compatible splice links. These make repair or controlled Crown extraction much safer. A Scriptorium reconstruction or experimental Wells sequence can substitute.

### The maintenance trust

Sealed coin, civic bonds, quarry rights, and repair contracts could fund:

- rapid surface evacuation;
- long-term Common Measure maintenance;
- compensation and resettlement for Low Choir households;
- rebuilding quarry vents and wells;
- a professional Warden and civic operator corps; or
- Lady Vey's restoration of the royal estate.

The value is large enough to make political choices concrete but not infinite. Spending it below as counterweight or losing it in collapse removes those future possibilities.

### Personal and ceremonial goods

Aldren's sword, seal crown, victory cups, mourning cloth, and jeweled armor are valuable and symbolically charged but not essential to the bell. Marr's public commission treats them as disputed royal goods, not ordinary salvage. Lady Vey claims them. Low Choir households may claim the cups as stolen witness vessels. Orren may trade them to retainers.

### Records of debt

A hidden drawer contains Councilor Rhun's rider, generations of loans against the maintenance trust, and evidence that surface elites reduced their Civic weights while preserving profit from the treasury. Publishing the records may fracture Harrowgate during evacuation. Suppressing them preserves coordination at the cost of future accountability.

## Treasure extraction

Getting treasure out is a dungeon operation.

- The Scriptorium route favors records and small bars.
- The Reliquary niche can float heavy loads but exposes them to water and pallbearer claims.
- The Feast passage lets Low Choir porters move goods if a division is negotiated.
- The Chapel royal return is rapid in Execution Turn and marks the carrier as a claimant.
- The Choir walk allows command transfer and pursuit toward the Deep Bell.
- The Black Rain crack can move unrecorded salvage at severe contamination risk.

Every crown-bar or chest occupies carrying capacity, rigging, routes, and time. A Warden or civic seal can authorize transport. Quiet removal is possible but changes later reactions.

Leave treasure secured, move it to the Chapterhouse, install it in the Wells, divide it, or abandon it. Call it recovered only after it has been physically moved and politically assigned.

## Orren outcomes

### Bargained leverage

Orren shares the sequence and contract evidence in exchange for a witnessed Crown settlement, a share of ordinary salvage, and protection from immediate execution. He may become a difficult ally in the Wells or Deep Bell.

### Divided expedition

His wounded porter or loyalists defect after the genealogies expose the concealed debt rider. Orren retreats through the Choir with sequence or bars, creating a pursuit rather than a final fight.

### Royal claimant

Orren accepts temporary sovereign recognition to command the defenses. He gains dangerous access and becomes personally liable to the machinery. The party can exploit, rescue, negotiate with, or oppose him.

### Defeat and custody

Orren is captured, killed, or driven off. His contract, sequence plate, and testimony remain useful. His removal does not settle Lady Vey's claim or repair the damage.

### Escape with treasure

Orren takes bars, records, or ceremonial goods rather than the Crown. This may weaken a replacement or future settlement while leaving the immediate finale open.

## Pressure scenes

### Lady Vey arrives by proxy

A speaking seal or retainer reaches the crypt with new surface orders. Vey may demand custody, authorize a coalition, repudiate Orren, or prioritize evacuation after another tremor.

### The treasury must become weight

The cleanest available repair consumes wealth promised for Low Choir resettlement or surface rebuilding. The party can seek other mass, accept the trade, or use a temporary brace.

### A genealogy is damaged

Combat, water, moths, or a narrowing wall threatens one record. Saving it costs position, treasure, or escape time. A damaged genealogy remains evidence but becomes easier to contest.

### The king grants too much

The retained voice recognizes a character as sovereign, custodian, or witness beyond what they intended. The authority opens routes and assigns obligations. Renunciation is possible but must be witnessed and may close an exit.

### The fourth toll reaches the gold

The walls ring like thin bells. Each genealogy speaks through living descendants and bearers elsewhere in the dungeon. The party can protect records, use the resonance to contact claimants, or flee before the sheets peel loose.

## Carry-forward states

Record the Grave as **sealed, opened under one claim, opened under divided claims, stripped, defended, flooded, or collapsed**. Also record:

- which genealogies were read, copied, damaged, suppressed, or carried;
- who filled the witness niche and the limits of their claim;
- the retained king's voice: active, constrained, transferred, altered, or destroyed;
- Orren, his loyalists, and the wounded porter;
- crown-bars removed, installed, promised, or lost;
- chain sequence and splice links;
- maintenance funds and records;
- ceremonial treasure and custody;
- exits opened or sealed; and
- any temporary sovereign recognition or inherited debt.

## Results

The Narrow Grave can provide a clean Royal Brake sequence, compatible replacement metal, major funding, contract evidence, Orren's confrontation, a route to the Choir or Black Rain, and a principled division of royal claims.

It reveals no secretly correct sovereign. Its sharpest treasure is proof that custody, maintenance, and release were always separate—and that every generation profited by pretending otherwise.

The complete sponsor chain separates Coss's unauthorized escalation from Vey's genuine but compromised claim.

The unacknowledged blood line, maintenance claims, and debt records complicate every attempt to make the Crown exclusively royal.
The three chained genealogies open the Grave while preserving distinct jurisdictions rather than one ownership claim.
The genealogies, retained voice, succession defenses, Orren, and treasury are encountered directly.
