Three genealogies and the treasury divide descent, maintenance, and surrender claims around the Crown.
Crown-bars, trial segments, maintenance funds, and Ash Witness limits can support a bounded replacement.

encounters.title: The Choir of Iron Tongues
encounters.summary: An iron choir stores severed voices and obeys only commands with source, address, and limit.
encounters.opening_view: “Name the source.” Iron answers through seven galleries. “Name the address.” Chains draw tight in distant rooms. “Name the limit.” No limit comes. A copyist hangs in the upper tuning cage, lending the Choir his breath, while three royal tongues speak in one woman’s voice and dispute what she surrendered. The unfinished command waits for its next word.
encounters.content:
## Situation

The Iron Choir descends in seven galleries around the Deep Bell’s upper throat. Hundreds of tongues hang above a conductor’s dais: shields, knives, keys, tools, and memorial plates remade as instruments. They swing without bells. Their voices travel through chain, water, and bone, carrying names and commands farther than any speaker can see the consequence.

Every lesser mechanism in the buried house can be addressed here. The lamp boughs, Reliquary saints, Garden shutters, Warden musters, Chapel pivots, Wells brakes, Black Rain gates, and the Deep Bell's preparatory catches all have phrases in the Choir. The system was meant to let several custodians coordinate during a toll. Later operators discovered that a command carries farther when spoken through a remembered human voice. They fed the Choir copied recollections. When volunteers became scarce, they routed involuntary memory from the Low Choir through the Lantern Cistern and into the iron.

The Choir is both control room and stolen civic archive. Silence ends immediate commands and traps the memories. A general recital restores nothing; it calls active mechanisms into contradictory motion.

## Cast

- **The Iron Cantor** is an articulated frame of tuning forks, chain fingers, and a faceless bronze hood. It sorts voices, completes familiar commands, and treats missing limits as damage to be repaired. When it cannot identify a lawful conductor, it preserves continuity by making every mechanism finish the sentence it began.
- **Hara-of-Three-Refrains** is a Low Choir memory keeper who entered through the condemned Chapel chute. One refrain is her childhood, one her dead aunt’s, and one a maintenance sequence she accepted for a season. She marks each change of voice by touching a different finger. The Choir has begun answering all three as one person.
- **Lieutenant Olt Venn** leads three Deep Rank Wardens sent before the Barracks command crisis was settled. He has an intact shell, a damaged tablet, and an order to preserve royal operation until relieved by recognized authority. He will obey a valid muster, but he interprets uncertainty as sabotage.
- **Jori Pell**, an Ember Company copyist, hangs inside the upper tuning cage with iron wire through his coat and pack. He tried to record the command lexicon. The Cantor now uses his breath to test phrases.
- **Queen Avarra** is present only in retained faculties distributed among three royal tongues. The chamber can speak with her measures, her refusal, or her witness. It cannot initially assemble a complete ghost.

## Immediate pressures

The next toll is entering its preparatory phase. The Iron Cantor is issuing a **general continuity recital**: lamp boughs brighten, Wardens receive muster calls, water gates seek their old positions, and the Funerary Well begins taking memory load. Each subsystem answers according to its current damage. The result is not restoration but synchronized strain.

Hara is trying to isolate the Low Choir register before another generation of memories is drawn upward. Olt Venn is trying to reach the conductor's dais and complete the recital. Jori Pell will lose his voice if the upper cage makes three more test strokes. Three royal tongues have begun speaking over one another in Avarra's voice.

Ignoring the recital leaves the upper control walk open, but the party reaches the Bell amid a command cascade, with fewer controls, more defenders, and another packet of Low Choir memory loaded for sacrifice.

## The chamber

### The name galleries

The upper three galleries carry personal and household memory. Each tongue is marked with a salt name, a Low Choir cup sign, a Warden tablet notch, or a blank acquisition number. Touching one produces a sensory fragment rather than an explanation: a kitchen at dawn, a quarry blast, a child's fever, a face no living bearer can presently recall.

The galleries are crossed by narrow chain bridges. A voice released without an identified recipient passes into adjacent tongues, combining memories that were never lived together. White name moths, if released from the Menagerie, can consume such unattached fragments before they spread, but they cannot determine rightful ownership.

### The command galleries

The middle three galleries carry operating phrases. Their tongues are grouped by mechanism rather than location:

1. **Light and passage** — lamp boughs, route latches, warning shutters, and Warden doors.
2. **Water and breath** — Reliquary saints, separator gates, Garden filters, and Black Rain spillways.
3. **Burden and timing** — Ropeworks drums, Chapel brakes, Wells catches, and Deep Bell preparatory locks.

A gallery can be isolated by setting two chain dampers and one memory brake. Isolation prevents remote operation of its mechanisms until the dampers are released, but it also stops contradictory commands and lets operators work locally.

### The royal register

The lowest gallery contains nine tongues cast from conquered royal instruments. Six hold old legal forms. Three retain Queen Avarra's will:

- **Measure** can compare loads, promises, and physical consequences. It recognizes disproportion and can help fit or test a burden. Choosing the bearer remains a living judgment.
- **Refusal** preserves Avarra's capacity to reject commands made through her Crown. It can break a coerced acceptance or deny a claimant, but it cannot operate the machine by itself.
- **Witness** remembers the terms of surrender, the first contact with the Mouth Below, and the distinction between what Avarra yielded and what later custodians invented. Its memories are incomplete wherever records were deliberately removed.

The three faculties answer separately until the party brings them into one cadence through evidence, living recognition, or the Crown itself. Even then, the result is a retained will under constraint—not an omniscient queen returned from death.

### The conductor's dais

The dais has three sockets and a circular speaking rail. A command is reliably accepted only when it supplies:

- a **source** the system can recognize: a Warden muster, Chapel acceptance, royal faculty, recorded custodian, or present operator taking responsibility;
- an **address** identifying the mechanism, person, or register acted upon; and
- a **limit** stating duration, stopping condition, or permitted cost.

Commands lacking a source are repeated as questions. Commands lacking an address spread to every similar mechanism. Commands lacking a limit continue until interrupted by damage, a stronger command, or the next toll. The old custodians often omitted limits when directing involuntary memory transfers.

## Entering and moving through the Choir

The chamber can be reached from five directions:

- the Chapel's lower stair opens onto the name galleries;
- the King's Narrow Grave mortuary walk enters beside the royal register;
- a service climb from the Counterweight Wells reaches the burden gallery;
- the Black Rain speaking shaft rises behind the water tongues; and
- the Deep Bell upper control walk begins beyond the conductor's dais.

No route requires the party to master the whole Choir. They can traverse hanging tongues, crawl along damping chains, use a Quiet Beast to suppress one kind of excess, accept Olt Venn's guarded escort, or break through the rear lattice. Every bypass leaves more of the chamber uncontrolled during the finale.

## Common operations

### Identify a voice

Identify a fragment through a living witness, marked cup, Warden tablet, Scriptorium record, or distinctive repeated fact. Some have no surviving claimant. Preserve, release, archive, or spend them as anonymous operating force.

### Restore a memory

Restoration requires three things: an identified memory, a receiving person or vessel, and recognition by someone who knows the memory belongs there. A memory cup can hold the fragment during transfer. The Lantern network can carry it. The Returning Breath saint can stabilize a damaged recipient. The Iron Cantor can perform the joining, but it cannot supply consent or recognition.

Restoration is imperfect when the recipient has built a life around the absence. Give the player or GM a choice of how the memory returns: vivid and disruptive, partial but integrated, or stored nearby until the person chooses to receive it. A restored recollection does not erase years of adaptation.

### Issue a lesser command

Once the party understands source, address, and limit, it can remotely prepare or operate one linked mechanism. Major operations still require local capacity. The Choir can set a Garden shutter to ready; it cannot evacuate the Garden. It can command a Reliquary saint to kneel; it cannot create air in a flooded chamber. It can call Wardens; it cannot make disputed authority legitimate.

Useful commands include:

- isolate or relight a lamp bough;
- hold a Reliquary saint in a chosen position;
- prepare a root shutter or Black Rain spillway;
- set a Wells catch for a known brake window;
- open a route latch;
- call or stand down Wardens under a recognized muster; and
- delay one phase of the next toll.

### Separate the royal faculties

The party may remove or damp one of Avarra's three tongues. This protects that faculty from destruction and prevents others from using it, but weakens any later reconstruction. A claimant may especially want Measure without Refusal, or Witness without the limits preserved by the other two.

### Reconstruct Avarra's retained will

Bringing Measure, Refusal, and Witness into one cadence requires at least two independent anchors among the Ash Witness genealogy, Avarra's Crown, an original Scriptorium surrender plate, a living witness carrying inherited terms, or a Chapel declaration that recognizes her as a wronged bearer rather than a reigning sovereign.

The reconstructed will remembers making contact with the Mouth Below during a siege. She tried to force the phenomenon to consume an enemy army's engines and instead taught it to answer royal cadence. After defeat, she surrendered the Crown's command over the Mouth for the limited purpose of stabilizing the fault. She did not consent to indefinite imprisonment, hereditary ownership of her retained voice, or the diversion of memory cost onto the Low Choir.

Avarra wants the sentence ended. She also knows that an abrupt release can kill Harrowgate. She will aid a replacement, distributed settlement, controlled collapse, or bounded emergency continuance if no one is coerced into taking her place. She refuses to certify that justice consists of handing her Crown to a descendant and repeating her authority.

## Conflict in the Choir

The Iron Cantor treats unresolved voices as dangerous material. If opposed, it uses the room rather than fighting as a single creature:

- chain fingers seize a speaker and carry them toward the register they most resemble;
- command tongues strike mechanisms elsewhere, changing light, water, or route state;
- name tongues speak intimate memories aloud, creating confusion and leverage;
- the upper cage steals breath to complete an unfinished command; and
- a royal tongue can force anyone carrying recognized royal metal to repeat a phrase.

Olt Venn and the Deep Rank Wardens fight to control stations, close dampers, and finish a valid command. They can be defeated, persuaded, mustered, relieved, or shown that their order lacks a lawful limit. Hara fights only to prevent another involuntary draw. Jori will help whoever first frees him, then demand that the copied memories not be treated as treasure.

Fight for the dais, Jori, dangerous registers, and the fate of the general recital. Every destroyed tongue may erase an irreplaceable memory, command, or witness.

## Failure states

Use named failures so the consequences remain legible.

- **General Muster:** every active Warden receives a royal continuity order and moves toward the deep chambers.
- **Name Rain:** unattached memories fall through the dungeon, causing temporary identity confusion and feeding the Mouth.
- **False Silence:** command transmission stops, but stored pressure and memory continue accumulating without warning.
- **Royal Recital:** one Avarra faculty dominates the other two. Measure produces cold optimization, Refusal breaks needed operations, or Witness traps the chamber in accusation without action.
- **Cantor fracture:** the control frame breaks into autonomous forks that continue familiar commands in nearby regions.

None blocks the finale. Each changes who or what must be handled there.

## Treasure and salvage

The Choir contains six removable command tongues, coils of silver memory wire, Warden muster forks, and private civic records. Removing a command tongue grants portable authority over one narrow mechanism if the user can still supply source and limit. Removing memory wire makes later restoration and distributed stabilization harder. The royal tongues are not ordinary salvage: carrying one means carrying a faculty of Avarra's retained will and exposing it to anyone who can make it speak.

## Carry-forward states

Record:

- which command galleries remain active, isolated, or broken;
- who controls the conductor's dais;
- whether Jori Pell and Hara are alive, free, and allied;
- Olt Venn's order and disposition;
- memories restored, preserved, released, or lost;
- whether the general recital completed;
- which lesser mechanisms are prepared remotely;
- the condition and location of Measure, Refusal, and Witness; and
- whether Avarra's retained will has been reconstructed and what it has agreed to do.

A controlled Choir grants coordination and truth. Silence grants privacy and local autonomy. Break it, and every final operation depends on runners, timing, and whatever memories survived elsewhere.

Measure, Refusal, and Witness remain divided among three royal tongues and may be reconstructed without restoring a throne.
Maintenance concordances from Odran's archive identify voice sources, command limits, and later alterations.
Extracted Low Choir voices and names remain evidence and possible persons, not merely command material.
Maintenance concordances connect written source, spoken command, address, and limit across the Iron Choir.
Royal voice and genealogy affect which command sources the Iron Choir recognizes and which limits remain audible.
Commands from the Iron Choir can address Wells mechanisms only when source, station, and limit are valid.

Repeated command cadence and separated royal faculties can become source material for a bounded deep exchange.
Avarra's retained faculties can pass between the Crown and the royal command register without becoming one complete sovereign.

encounters.title: The Black Rain Cistern
encounters.summary: Upward rain gives every spared strain an address in body, street, root, or machine.
encounters.opening_view: The first drop strikes your chin from below. Black rain rises from a lake with no visible surface, clears against the ribbed ceiling, and runs into four great gutters. Surveyor Kesh Arden has written a Harrowgate street beside every gauge mark. Sister Pell tastes the water, closes her eyes, and refuses to name its owner. Every gutter is already somebody’s address.
encounters.content:
## Situation

The Black Rain Cistern makes mountain strain visible. A bottomless lake hangs below; black drops rise, strike the ribbed ceiling, turn clear, and enter four great gutters. The water changes color. The force passes into stone, roots, counterweights, foundations, and the Deep Bell.

The builders could route pressure, never erase it. Every clean-looking solution sends force toward quarry vents, the Reliquary, the Mouth Below, or Harrowgate's foundations. Later custodians hid the recipient by calling the cistern a drain.

The Ember Company opened the royal spillway while the quarry mouths were still sealed. The next surge tore one gutter from its frame and filled the chamber with upward rain. The Iron Choir is now calling the gates toward their old automatic sequence. That sequence assumes intact roots, staffed pumps, and an evacuated lower cloister. None of those assumptions is presently true.

## Cast

- **Surveyor Kesh Arden**, a Harrowgate quarry apprentice, was pulled through a cracked vent while measuring the third toll. He has survived on a shelf above the Foundation Weir, scratching street names beside each pressure mark. He speaks quickly until asked who lives above a vent; then he gives every household he knows.
- **Sister Pell-of-the-Last-Dry-Step** is a Low Choir pressure reader. Black rain has replaced pieces of her recent memory with sensations from the fault. She predicts surges in images—iron under the tongue, a stair bending west—and always adds, “Mine or the mountain’s; use it, but do not call it mine yet.”
- **The Rain Wardens** are four ceramic diving forms stored in wall alcoves. They enter black water, carry gate chains, and return coated in mineral glass. Two answer old Warden command. One answers the Iron Choir. One answers any person who has been struck by black rain and survived.
- **The Upward Drowned** are pressure bodies shaped from water, grit, and borrowed posture. They resemble people climbing through deep water in reverse. Breaking one releases force into the nearest open path.

## Immediate pressures

The cistern begins at **High Working Level** unless prior water operations changed it. The torn royal gutter is shedding clear water toward the foundations. The quarry gutter is sealed by surface rubble. The Reliquary return is partly open. The Mouth sluice is breathing in pulses.

At the next pressure rise, one of four things will happen unless the party intervenes:

- the Foundation Weir lifts and cracks Harrowgate's inhabited ridge;
- the Reliquary return floods the copper saints and any lower rescue route;
- the Mouth sluice opens without terms and teaches the underlying phenomenon a new path upward; or
- the torn gutter fails, dropping a section of the Bell's lower bridge.

Kesh can identify the surface consequences. Pell can identify the sequence. Neither can operate all stations alone.

## The four routes of strain

### Quarry vent manifold

Six bronze throats lead toward the quarry and abandoned lower cloister. Three surface mouths are known. Two have been built over. One opens into a forgotten lime pit. Venting here converts water pressure into rockfall, steam, and violent air movement.

A safe staged vent requires:

- at least two surface mouths opened or one mouth and a sacrificial collapse zone;
- Garden root shutters prepared so the pressure does not tear through food beds and inhabited ways;
- people cleared from the quarry and affected streets; and
- the manifold opened in rising order rather than all at once.

Opening the manifold without those preparations still relieves the Bell. It spends buildings, routes, and lives instead of preparation.

### Reliquary return

This broad copper channel sends water through the six saints, where breath, heat, and suspended grit can be separated. It is the most controllable route while the Reliquary remains intact. It also carries black-water memory into a chamber already holding the dead and the injured.

At low and middle Reliquary levels, the return can absorb one major surge. At high level, it threatens Rhea Colm's former station, the royal niche, and the lower culvert. A cooperative pallbearer or prepared saints can distribute the surge. An uncontrolled return animates drowned load ghosts and may overwrite restored memory.

### Mouth sluice

A vertical throat descends beneath the lake. When opened, it sends vibration and black water directly into the Mouth Below. This buys immediate pressure relief and can create a descent route. It also constitutes an offering before the party has stated any boundary. Repeated use teaches the Mouth that Harrowgate answers strain by feeding it memory-laden water.

The sluice can be opened narrowly for sound, halfway for a negotiable flow, or fully as an emergency sacrifice. Closing it after a full opening may require the Deep Bell's Refusal faculty, a Funerary Well release, or a bargain made below.

### Foundation Weir

The final gutter leads upward through Harrowgate's ridge. It was designed as a last resort: distribute strain across empty terraces, let walls crack, and preserve the deep system. Those terraces are no longer empty. The chapterhouse, poor streets, old quarry housing, and part of Lady Vey's estate now stand above them.

The weir can spread one surge broadly, focus it into a chosen collapse zone, or be blocked. Blocking it does not remove the load. It forces the next surge toward another route. Using it without evacuation protects the machine by spending the town.

## Cistern levels

Track five broad states.

1. **Low:** the lake hangs far below; the lower bridge and Mouth throat are exposed. Pressure is accumulating elsewhere.
2. **Working:** upward rain is steady; any one prepared route can carry the next surge.
3. **High:** rain fills the chamber; travel requires anchored lines, Rain Warden assistance, or movement through dry gutter ribs.
4. **Crown:** black water reaches the royal gauge. The next major change begins the Deep Bell's Crown Descent phase immediately.
5. **Ruptured:** the chamber has chosen a new permanent path through broken stone. Mark which population, region, or landscape receives it.

A level change means nothing without a destination; low water may still conceal high total strain.

## Moving through upward rain

Ordinary falling becomes unreliable. Loose objects rise until they strike the ceiling gutters. A person who loses contact with a line may be carried upward, pinned beneath a channel, and swept laterally into another route. Clear water falls normally once separated, producing intersecting curtains.

Useful methods include:

- Rain Warden carries;
- Counterweight Wells tension lines;
- a Menagerie velvet hound consuming patterned vibration along one crossing;
- Cinderback drawing heat from a gate housing;
- Reliquary saint breath sent through the return;
- Garden roots grown or rigged across the ribs; and
- deliberate release of a small surge to create a brief dry interval.

Build combat around anchors, gates, rescue, and route choice. Killing an Upward Drowned without controlling where its pressure goes can be worse than letting it pass.

## Pressure readings

Three instruments make the chamber legible.

- The **water crown** shows which route will receive the next uncontrolled surge.
- The **fault harp** sounds the total pressure irrespective of visible level.
- The **foundation pins** correspond to districts above and show where accumulated strain has already entered Harrowgate.

Together they show pressure routed, delayed, divided, or converted—never erased. Anyone claiming disposal has failed to name the sacrifice.

## Common operations

### Stage a quarry vent

Open surface mouths, prepare Garden shutters, clear exposed areas, and sequence the six manifold throats from smallest to largest. A fully prepared vent lowers Black Rain by two states and creates a safe controlled-collapse path. A partial preparation lowers it by one state and assigns a specific local disaster. An unprepared full release lowers it immediately and devastates the quarry district.

### Load the Reliquary return

Set the six saints, establish an air and memory path, and open the copper channel during a Wells brake window. Success moves one surge into manageable water and heat. Failure raises the Reliquary level, activates drowned load ghosts, or washes memory into the wrong recipients.

### Feed the Mouth sluice

Choose the width and duration of the opening and identify what accompanies the water: anonymous vibration, named memory, royal cadence, black-water minerals, or a deliberate message from the Iron Choir. This operation can begin a settlement or create a predatory expectation.

### Focus the Foundation Weir

Use the foundation pins and Harrowgate surveys to choose a collapse line. Surface evacuation and shoring determine casualties. This can save the Deep Bell or create time for another operation, but it makes the party responsible for where the town breaks.

### Repair the torn royal gutter

Compatible royal metal, three splice links, silver-root fiber, or a living Quiet Beast can hold the gutter. Repair preserves the lower bridge and clean Crown extraction. A brace may last one toll. A full repair restores the route but increases the Bell's ability to continue the old arrangement.

## The Rain Wardens

The four ceramic forms can dive into black water without losing their names because each carries a blank tablet that records only present duty. They are strong gate operators and dangerous literalists.

A Rain Warden accepts a command identifying route, limit, and return. Without a return condition it remains in the lake. Without a limit it keeps opening a gate. Without a route it follows the loudest pressure. A recognized Barracks commander, Iron Choir source, or person marked by black rain can direct one.

If the party destroys a Rain Warden, its blank tablet fills with the nearest person's last fear. That fear may later speak through the Iron Choir or Mouth.

## Queen Avarra and Black Rain

Witness fragments reveal that Avarra first encountered upward rain during the siege that ended her reign. She believed the fault could be commanded because it answered cadence. In truth, it learned recurrence. The more consistently royal orders fed it strain, the more it shaped itself around royal sound.

The Black Rain Cistern was built after her surrender to make that dangerous relationship measurable. The Crown did not create the fault. It made a repeated bargain look like machinery.

## Failure states

- **Foundation lift:** Harrowgate's ridge rises and drops unevenly, destroying buildings and surface routes.
- **Reliquary wash:** black-water memory floods the saints and anyone linked to them.
- **Mouth learning:** the lower sluice opens without terms and the phenomenon begins answering Harrowgate's uncontrolled distress.
- **Bridge shear:** the torn gutter takes part of the lower approach to the Deep Bell.
- **Mineral birth:** an Upward Drowned reaches clear water and hardens into a glass pressure figure that continues toward the surface.

## Treasure and salvage

Black-water pearls form in dead eddies. Each holds compressed vibration and can power a single command, shatter stone, or serve as an offering below. Mineral glass from the Rain Wardens is valuable and useful for pressure gauges. The fault harp can be dismantled, but doing so blinds every later attempt to distinguish low water from low total strain.

## Carry-forward states

Record:

- cistern level and total pressure reading;
- which of the four routes is open, prepared, damaged, or permanently chosen;
- surface vent mouths and evacuation zones;
- Garden shutter preparation;
- Reliquary capacity and contamination;
- Mouth sluice width, duration, and what was sent through it;
- Foundation Weir districts exposed;
- Kesh Arden and Pell-of-the-Last-Dry-Step's condition;
- Rain Warden survival and command; and
- whether the royal gutter and lower bridge are intact.

The cistern makes the ending honest: choose where force goes, name who prepares, and never call it gone.

Witness fragments show Avarra mistook the fault's recurring response for royal obedience.
Rhea's mnemonic training can distinguish black-water contamination from ordinary confusion and identify dangerous return pulses.
Black Rain routes stolen and returned memory through occupied districts and inherited addresses.
Black Rain receives or redirects pressure displaced by Wells operations and dropped loads.
Black Rain receives displaced pressure and memory through routes that can be repaired, focused, or ruptured.
The Mouth sluice carries pressure, matter, and memory into the fault's learned routes.

encounters.title: The Deep Bell
encounters.summary: Four moving approaches converge on the Bell, where the Crown cannot leave its load behind.
encounters.opening_view: The bridge moves sideways beneath your first step. Across the void, three other approaches answer in different directions. Only then does the Deep Bell emerge from the dark: a bronze horizon patched with royal plate, Warden bronze, quarry clamps, and mourning wire. The Crown burns in the clapper cage. The speaking rail clicks once. There is no floor to receive what comes next.
encounters.content:
## Situation

The Deep Bell hangs over the Mouth Below between four load systems. Its skin is patched with royal metal, Warden bronze, quarry clamps, and Low Choir memorial wire; every patch records who was available to spend when an earlier repair failed. This operation will add another record.

There is no safe floor. Four approaches reach different parts of the mechanism:

- the **upper control walk** from the Choir reaches the preparatory catches and speaking rail;
- the **maintenance bridge** from the Counterweight Wells reaches the load yokes and chain splices;
- the **lower bridge** from Black Rain reaches the clapper cage, water brakes, and collapse charges;
- the **mortuary walk** from the King's Narrow Grave reaches the Crown cradle and royal release locks.

No approach suffices alone. Cross by climbing the bell skin, traversing moving chains, using appeal wings or Quiet Beasts, throwing lines through the cage, or rotating the Bell. Every crossing is exposed when the cycle advances.

Inside the clapper cage hangs the Crown of Measure: six gold-black arches around a measuring tongue, with the cut royal chain trailing like a severed tendon. Measure, Refusal, and Witness move between Crown and Choir according to the current system state.

## The four phases of a toll

Track the toll in four phases. Advance after a major failed operation, prolonged conflict, or unopposed command cascade. Prepared systems can delay, repeat, or skip a phase.

### 1. Taking Breath

The Lantern and Reliquary networks draw air, heat, and memory toward the deep works. Lamps brighten or fail. People carrying loose memories hear them speak. The upper control walk is stable.

Actions suited to this phase include issuing Choir commands, establishing witnesses, setting water routes, evacuating exposed people, and moving a replacement burden into position.

### 2. Drawing Load

The Ropeworks and three Wells take weight. Bridges tilt. The maintenance yokes become accessible. Anyone holding a voluntary or coerced burden feels the machine trying to classify it.

This is the safest phase for splicing chains, fitting mass, shifting Wells paths, or arranging a distributed stabilization. It is the most dangerous phase for people trapped on unbalanced bridges.

### 3. Crown Descent

The Crown drops toward the bell skin. Black Rain rises. The royal and mortuary locks align. Avarra's faculties become loud enough to speak through metal carried by the party.

This is the only clean phase for removing the Crown, transferring its load, or placing a recognized replacement. A forced extraction is possible at other times but tears mass through an uncontrolled path.

### 4. Sounding

The measuring tongue strikes. Force passes into whichever water, memory, and counterweight routes remain open. Everyone in the shaft must anchor, yield, or ride the motion. The town above receives whatever the party did not route elsewhere.

A controlled sounding can complete a repair or test a replacement. An uncontrolled sounding advances the catastrophe, destroys one vulnerable approach, and creates memory bleed throughout the dungeon.

After Sounding, the cycle returns to Taking Breath if the Bell survives.

## Immediate pressures

Begin in Taking Breath unless prior failures accelerated the sequence. Select or infer three active pressures:

- a Wells load is slipping;
- Black Rain is at High or Crown level;
- the Iron Choir is issuing an automatic continuity command;
- the royal gutter or lower bridge is failing;
- Deep Rank Wardens are securing the Crown for continuance;
- Orren, Lady Vey's agents, or another claimant is attempting the mortuary locks;
- Low Choir memory is being drawn into the Funerary path;
- the fourth toll is already damaging Harrowgate; or
- the Mouth Below is answering a prior uncontrolled offering.

Begin with enough information for a plan. The difficulty lies in executing linked operations under pressure, never in hiding the relevant lever.

## Queen Avarra's retained will

Avarra may arrive divided among Crown, Choir, records, or portable tongues. Bring Measure, Refusal, and Witness into cadence and she can speak in short intervals.

She remembers the siege, constrained surrender, and first Bell design; later history reaches her only through memories fed to the machine. She compares burdens, refuses royal commands through her Crown, and identifies the Low Choir transfer and hereditary sentence as later additions.

Her wishes are clear but bounded:

- end the use of her Crown as an involuntary clapper;
- do not place another unwilling person or people into the same sentence;
- preserve Harrowgate if doing so does not require pretending the old arrangement is just; and
- leave future duty visible, transferable, and answerable to those who bear it.

She is capable of compromise. If immediate release would kill thousands and no prepared alternative exists, she will accept a bounded emergency continuance with a stated end, living witnesses, and enforceable remedy. She will not declare a descendant absolute, certify a coerced Common Measure, or promise that the Mouth Below can be mastered.

A claimant may operate the Crown through isolated Measure while suppressing Refusal. A destroyer may break the Bell through Refusal without hearing Witness. Make the mutilation and its advantage visible.

## The Bell's defenses

Build opposition from unresolved earlier states, not one final monster.

### Burden echoes

As Drawing Load begins, the Bell extrudes figures from soot, mineral water, and memory wire. Each resembles someone currently carrying an obligation: a Warden commander, a Low Choir witness, a claimant, a rescued delver, or a party member. An echo repeats the obligation without its limit. A promise to protect becomes refusal to move. A claim to the Crown becomes possession at any cost. A rescue duty becomes dragging everyone toward one route.

An echo can be fought, named, given a limit, discharged through a fulfilled act, or redirected into a prepared burden. Destroying it releases its load into the nearest chain.

### Chain saints

Four enormous jointed forms climb the suspension chains. They were built from decommissioned Reliquary saints and royal armor. Each protects one approach and can transfer itself between chains during Sounding. They obey valid Choir command, recognized Warden muster, or the old continuity recital.

Their combat purpose is to separate teams, close access to timing windows, and carry materials to the wrong load path. They can be disabled locally, reassigned, deceived with a legitimate narrow command, or given a safer maintenance duty.

### Claimant conflict

Any faction still pursuing exclusive control arrives through its available route. This may be Orren with contract survivors, Lady Vey's retainers, Deep Rank Wardens, a Low Choir release party, or surface authorities attempting to prevent collapse. Keep their goals intelligible. They may bargain during the operation, defect when costs become visible, or fight over the Crown cage while the Bell continues moving.

## Core operations

### Hold the cycle

The party can delay one phase through a prepared Choir command, a correctly timed Wells catch, a Reliquary breath reserve, a velvet hound consuming the phase's vibration, or people physically holding a brake. Every method has a local limit. Repeating it without relief causes injury, beast migration, mechanism damage, or lost memory.

### Repair the royal chain

A durable repair requires compatible metal, a splice path, and a safe Drawing Load window. Royal splice links and crown-bars are ideal. Salt bronze, silver root, or beast tissue can make bounded repairs. The repaired chain restores controlled continuance and clean future Crown transfer. It also restores the old machine's capacity to keep operating.

### Transfer the Crown's load

The Crown cannot be removed cleanly while it remains the recognized and physical burden. The party must either:

- fit an accepted replacement with sufficient mass and a viable Wells path;
- distribute the load among water, counterweights, roots, and ongoing civic operations;
- drop or spend a Well to take the shock;
- route the load into a controlled collapse; or
- negotiate a new destination through the Mouth Below.

Cutting the Crown free without a destination is still a choice. The load goes to the nearest open path, usually Harrowgate's foundations, the Funerary memory route, or the person holding the Crown.

### Fit the Common Measure or another replacement

A replacement needs Chapel recognition, actual material, named maintainers, and consent that remains valid at Crown Descent. At Drawing Load, move the frame through the Wells yoke. At Crown Descent, bring Crown and replacement into parallel measure. Measure can test the transfer. Refusal can reject coercion. Witness can record the terms.

A partial replacement may carry some functions while water and civic labor carry the rest. A frame accepted under coercion works briefly but produces burden echoes, Chapel execution claims, and future political crisis.

### Free the Crown

The six release locks on the mortuary walk answer the Golden Branch, Burden Chain, and Ash Witness in pairs. Any one genealogy can open two. Two compatible jurisdictions can open four. All six open cleanly when custody, operating authority, and surrender limits are acknowledged.

Force, royal command, or Crown Descent alignment can bypass missing locks. The Crown then comes free with damage or an attached claim. Whoever carries it can invoke Avarra's retained authority over old mechanisms and the Mouth's learned royal cadence. That power is real, limited, and politically explosive.

### Break the Bell

The Bell can be destroyed by severing suspension chains, detonating quarry charges on the lower bridge, dropping a Well, inducing a Black Rain surge, or turning its own Sounding against a prepared fracture line. Destruction without venting and evacuation sends the shaft collapse into Harrowgate. Controlled collapse requires choosing a route for water, stone, and people.

## Finale architectures

Use these as operating architectures, not scripts. Combine them when preparation supports a hybrid.

### Controlled continuance

**Purpose:** keep the Bell operating while ending the immediate uncontrolled tolls.

**Requirements:** a repaired or securely braced royal chain; balanced Wells and Ropeworks; one lawful water route; operators; and a decision about ongoing memory cost.

**Procedure:** stabilize during Drawing Load, restore the Crown path at Crown Descent, issue a bounded continuity command, and survive one controlled Sounding as a test.

**Costs and variants:** the old system survives. The Low Choir burden may be reduced, voluntarily compensated, transferred, or shamefully continued. Avarra accepts only an emergency term with a real end and remedy. This ending buys time and creates a campaign about reform, maintenance, and whether promises made under crisis are kept.

### Replacement burden

**Purpose:** free the Crown while preserving a centralized pressure-release mechanism.

**Requirements:** an accepted frame, sufficient mass, compatible fittings, Wells path, maintainers, and continuing consent.

**Procedure:** bring replacement and Crown into parallel measure during Crown Descent, transfer physical and recognized load, open the release locks, then complete a test Sounding.

**Costs and variants:** a well-designed Common Measure distributes obligation and makes future transfer possible. A dynastic, Warden, or coerced replacement may work but recreate the injustice in another form. Partial acceptance produces a hybrid with water and civic labor.

### Distributed stabilization

**Purpose:** silence the Bell as a central sovereign machine and divide its work among visible systems.

**Requirements:** Crown release; controlled Black Rain routes; functioning Wells or substitutes; Garden and quarry pressure capacity; ongoing Harrowgate labor and funding; settled Low Choir and Warden roles.

**Procedure:** during Drawing Load, unload the Crown into several prepared paths. At Crown Descent, lock the clapper away from the bell skin. At Sounding, let each system take a bounded share and verify that no hidden Funerary draw occurs.

**Costs and variants:** Harrowgate must maintain pumps, vents, roots, brakes, and evacuation plans permanently. The solution is less elegant, more expensive, and harder to hide. It is also harder for one claimant to own. Failure in later years becomes political and administrative rather than mythical.

### Controlled collapse

**Purpose:** destroy the Bell and allow the mountain to settle through prepared sacrificial routes.

**Requirements:** surface evacuation; quarry vents or another collapse zone; Garden shutters prepared or replaced; Black Rain sequence known; severance or demolition access.

**Procedure:** lower Black Rain into the chosen route, open vents in staged order, isolate memory and water systems where possible, then break the Bell during Sounding so its force follows the prepared fracture.

**Costs and variants:** the deep complex is partly or wholly lost. Harrowgate loses districts, wealth, and perhaps access to rescued history. A well-prepared collapse preserves most lives. A rushed one still may be preferable to cascading failure. The Crown can be removed first, buried, destroyed, or lost below.

### Crown release and royal claim

**Purpose:** prioritize possession or liberation of the Crown even without a complete replacement.

**Requirements:** release-lock access or force; a way to take the load, however costly; an extraction route.

**Procedure:** unload through a Well drop, Foundation Weir, temporary human hold, or Mouth path; free the Crown at Crown Descent; then stabilize or flee before Sounding.

**Costs and variants:** giving the Crown to Lady Vey, another claimant, a Warden trust, the Low Choir, Harrowgate, Avarra's retained will, or no one creates different campaigns. Exclusive royal use can command old mechanisms and influence the Mouth, but Refusal may oppose it. Pure liberation without a custody plan invites theft and renewed conflict.

### Mouth Below settlement

**Purpose:** replace the Bell's repeated mechanical bargain with an explicit relationship to the underlying phenomenon.

**Requirements:** safe descent, an offering, stated boundary and return, an exit plan, and acceptance of uncertainty.

**Procedure:** hold or redirect the cycle while representatives descend; negotiate below; return with a pattern the Bell, Choir, or Black Rain gates can enact; then test it at Sounding or silence the Bell under the new arrangement.

**Costs and variants:** the Mouth may accept periodic vibration, opened landscape, named memory, royal cadence, or another recurring exchange. No settlement makes it human. The result can restore memories, reduce pressure, or end royal control, but it creates a new duty and a new kind of risk.

### Cascading survival

**Purpose:** determine what can still be saved after the prepared architectures fail.

When Sounding begins uncontrolled, ask each active team to save one category:

- people on an approach;
- Harrowgate above;
- Low Choir memory;
- the Crown and Avarra's faculties;
- a future operating system; or
- access to the Mouth Below.

Every saved category assigns force to another unless someone accepts an extraordinary sacrifice. A cascading ending should still answer who survived, where the pressure went, who carries authority, and what remains possible next.

## Partial successes

Use partial outcomes instead of treating the finale as binary.

- **Bell stabilized for one season:** enough time for evacuation or political settlement, but another descent will be required.
- **Crown freed, load unresolved:** the party escapes with the Crown while Harrowgate enters an emergency campaign.
- **Low Choir memory released, identities mixed:** involuntary extraction ends, but restoration becomes long communal work.
- **Town saved, deep community displaced:** the machine or collapse preserves Harrowgate while the Low Choir must relocate.
- **Machine destroyed, Mouth awakened:** the old injustice ends and a new phenomenon begins shaping the region.
- **Replacement works, consent disputed:** physical victory produces legal and moral instability.
- **Avarra witnessed but not freed:** her testimony changes every claim even though the Crown remains.
- **Crown lost below:** no faction controls it, but the Mouth now has royal cadence.

## After the operation

State four things plainly after the operation:

1. what happened to Harrowgate's people, districts, water, and future safety;
2. what happened to the Low Choir's memory, homes, and political standing;
3. who controls, carries, destroys, or loses the Crown and Avarra's retained faculties; and
4. what duty remains, who accepted it, and what remedy exists when they fail.

Then resolve surviving factions and rescues. Orren's contract, Lady Vey's claim, Warden command, Low Choir compacts, treasure custody, and Ember Company responsibility do not disappear because the engineering succeeded.

## Carry-forward states

Record:

- final phase reached and whether a controlled Sounding occurred;
- surviving approaches and chain saints;
- Bell frame, clapper, and royal chain condition;
- Crown location, carrier, and recognized custody;
- Measure, Refusal, and Witness condition;
- chosen architecture and any hybrid elements;
- load destinations and permanent sacrifices;
- Harrowgate and Low Choir casualties, evacuations, and resources;
- factions present, agreements made, and authority recognized;
- recovered treasure and extraction route; and
- explicit future duties, limits, and remedies.

At the Bell, every earlier choice becomes physical. Reward preparation, permit costly improvisation, and leave a result whose bearers and casualties can be named.

reference_links.context: Warden command, labor, and consent shape whether the Bell is continued, replaced, distributed, or ended.
Vey may contribute resources or pursue Crown custody, but the final operation cannot make her claim exclusive.
Varo's brake windows and burden-system knowledge can coordinate the Bell's moving approaches without deciding its settlement.
Avarra's retained faculties can compare, refuse, and testify during the final operation without choosing Harrowgate's justice.
Orren may reach the mortuary locks with claimants or contract survivors, bringing leverage without settling the Bell's operation.
Quoin may issue bounded emergency orders and convene a later muster, but cannot turn crisis command into a permanent sentence.
Nara's settlement standard requires a bounded transition, named operators, and a remedy that survives the emergency.
Company engineers, riggers, rescuers, and claimants may support several final operations without deciding their legitimacy.
Every final architecture must name what happens to the community's mnemonic burden, authority, and continuing work.
Any durable finale needs named maintainers, affected witnesses, and household commitments that the Feast can help assemble.
Crown-bars, brake sequences, custody claims, and surrender limits can support several finale architectures without selecting one.
The Wells take parallel load during Drawing Load and Crown Descent in several finale architectures.
The four phases, defenses, core operations, and finale architectures are encountered directly.
A Mouth settlement is one finale architecture for replacing the Bell's inherited mechanical bargain.
The Crown hangs in the clapper cage carrying command, memory cadence, and load that must be transferred or spent.
The Measure can take Crown load during a replacement or hybrid finale only under its accepted limits.

encounters.title: The Mouth Below
encounters.summary: A listening fault learns repeated exchanges and turns every bargain into a future pattern.
encounters.opening_view: At the basalt lips, everyone becomes conscious of repetition. A heartbeat. A drip. The scrape of a boot, corrected too late. The Mouth waits for one of them to happen again. Beyond the threshold, the chamber will take the shape of the first pattern offered. Repeat it, and the shape begins to become law. It asks nothing. It listens for an answer you may already have given.
encounters.content:
## Situation

The Mouth Below is the old records’ name for a place where fault, resonant cavity, and intelligence cannot be separated. It consumes patterned vibration and returns altered pressure, matter, and memory. It learns recurrence more readily than intention. A promise spoken once means little here; an exchange repeated twice has already begun to become law.

The Bell can be resolved without entering. Descent trades operating certainty for a chance to change the relationship beneath the entire machine: release from the old bargain, restored memories, a safer pressure path, the Crown's freedom, or power over the fault. The Mouth promises nothing in human terms; it answers patterns enacted clearly enough to recur.

Avarra mistook response for obedience. Later engineers mistook recurrence for machinery. The deepest choice is whether to repeat either error.

## Reaching the Mouth

There are three practical descents:

- the Deep Bell clapper line lowers directly through the sounding shaft during Crown Descent or after the Bell is secured;
- the Black Rain sluice opens a wet route through pressure ribs and mineral glass;
- the Garden's Last Teeth roots reach a dry fissure if they were not burned, flooded, or spent in collapse.

A party may force another route through broken Bell masonry or a dropped Well. Such entries are unstable and may close behind them.

Useful preparations include an anchored return line, controlled sound, a named memory vessel, black-water pearls, a Quiet Beast, Avarra's Witness or Refusal, and someone above able to interrupt the Bell. Each defines one part of the exchange before the Mouth chooses it.

## The threshold

The shaft narrows into two ridges of warm basalt like closed lips. Beyond them is no visible chamber until a sound is offered. A spoken name produces a corridor lined with moments from that person's memory. A hammer stroke produces an angular cavern of repeating impacts. Silence produces depth without distance, where the party can feel other heartbeats but not locate them.

Crossing the threshold requires making a pattern. The first pattern becomes the Mouth's provisional understanding of why the party has come.

Examples:

- a Warden cadence suggests command and return to station;
- a Low Choir memory cup suggests exchange of remembered lives;
- Crown metal suggests royal recurrence and Avarra's old bargain;
- black-water rhythm suggests pressure relief;
- a quiet-beast handling call suggests appetite, boundary, and return;
- a personal song suggests relationship with the singer rather than Harrowgate as a whole.

The party can correct an unfortunate first pattern, but every repetition teaches it more deeply.

## What lives here

### The Unsaid Brood

Small pale forms move at the edge of any created chamber. They have no mouths and wear impressions of faces that were almost remembered. They feed on abandoned clauses, interrupted names, and promises whose limits were never spoken.

When threatened, the Brood removes the final term from an action: a rope is tied but not to anything; a warning names danger but not whom it threatens; a command opens a gate but loses its stopping condition. Protect language and intent as carefully as bodies. Complete unfinished statements, feed the Brood harmless discarded patterns, contain it in memory cups, or destroy it and release its stolen omissions into the chamber.

### The Long Listener

Far below any temporary floor lies a shape assembled from black water and fault glass. It mirrors the posture of whoever speaks most regularly. The shape is only the form the phenomenon uses to maintain a conversation.

The Long Listener learns through recurrence. If attacked repeatedly, it learns combat as the exchange. If offered names repeatedly, it learns names as food. If given bounded pressure pulses and a consistent return, it can learn a civic venting pattern. Its apparent emotions reflect the pattern offered to it and should not be trusted as proof of human motives.

### Returned things

The Mouth sometimes gives back objects or memories altered toward stability:

- a cracked memory returns without pain but missing the face that caused it;
- a black-water pearl returns as clear glass holding one future tremor;
- a broken chain returns flexible and alive, seeking a recurring load;
- a dead person's voice returns able to answer only repeated questions;
- a lost name returns attached to the wrong duty; or
- a Crown command returns stripped of genealogy and usable by anyone who repeats its cost.

Each return shows what the Mouth understood the offering to mean.

## The grammar of settlement

A stable settlement requires three enacted terms.

### Offering

What will recur from Harrowgate to the Mouth? Possible offerings include:

- bounded vibration from civic machinery;
- pressure pulses routed through an opened quarry throat;
- chosen memories copied rather than removed;
- royal cadence without Crown ownership;
- black-water minerals or heat;
- seasonal music, labor, or public witness; or
- the destruction of a structure whose breaking teaches a new path.

An offering must be physically possible and politically maintainable. A promise to send what no one controls is only noise.

### Boundary

What may the Mouth take, affect, or follow? Boundaries can be marked through Refusal, Chapel acceptance, root growth, salt tablets, repeated silence, mapped geography, or a person willing to become the first living limit.

A vague boundary such as “harm no one” is not legible. A workable boundary names places, kinds of memory, durations, thresholds, and stopping conditions. The Mouth obeys patterns better than abstractions.

### Return

What does Harrowgate receive, and what happens when either side fails? Returns may include:

- reduced fault pressure;
- restoration or release of stored memory;
- closure of the royal command path;
- predictable tremor warnings;
- safe black-water minerals;
- a new vent landscape; or
- the Crown freed from acting as clapper.

The return must recur. A single gift may solve the crisis; it establishes no settlement.

Witness is not a fourth mechanical term, but without witnesses no human institution can know whether the exchange remains what was accepted.

## Possible settlements

### The open throat

The party teaches the Mouth to release pressure through a permanently opened quarry and uninhabited ravine. Harrowgate loses land and gains a strange steaming valley. The Bell can be silenced or reduced to warning duty. This requires geography, evacuation, and continuing maintenance of the boundary.

### The civic cadence

Harrowgate sends regular bounded vibration from mills, pumps, bells, or public works. The Mouth returns predictable pressure relief and warning patterns. This makes everyday civic labor part of the settlement and prevents one crown from owning it. Failure to maintain the cadence causes tremors rather than moral judgment.

### The memory exchange

Volunteers copy chosen memories into cups or Iron Tongues and offer those copies. The Mouth returns stolen Low Choir fragments or releases them from the fault. This can repair generations of loss, but copied memory remains a real intimacy and can become exploitation under another name.

### The royal unbinding

Avarra's Witness repeats the original limited surrender while Refusal denies all later additions. The Crown's cadence is offered once, then broken into a nonhereditary public pattern. The Mouth releases its learned expectation of royal command. The Crown becomes materially powerful but loses exclusive control over the fault.

### The deep lease

A person, faction, Quiet Beast, or constructed burden remains as a recurring interpreter. The Mouth gains a stable partner; Harrowgate gains adaptable relief. This is the closest settlement to the old Bell and the most likely to become another sentence. Consent, duration, relief, and return must be especially explicit.

### The severance

The party uses collapse, Refusal, and a massive nonrecurring offering to break every learned pattern between Harrowgate and the Mouth. Pressure returns to natural fault behavior. The region experiences earthquakes and long geological change without a directing intelligence. This may be liberation, catastrophe, or both.

## Negotiating through action

Negotiate through repeated demonstrations, never propositions.

1. The party enacts an offering in miniature.
2. The Mouth returns an interpretation.
3. The party accepts, rejects, or corrects it through a changed pattern.
4. The Mouth tests the proposed boundary.
5. The party demonstrates the return and failure condition.

The Iron Choir can translate complex sequences. The Deep Bell can amplify them. A Quiet Beast can consume one unwanted component. Avarra's faculties can compare, refuse, and witness. Low Choir memory keepers can identify when an offered memory has been altered beyond recognition.

Three clear exchanges may establish a provisional settlement. More exchanges improve precision but deepen the Mouth's expectation that the participants themselves will continue.

## Conflict below

Violence is possible and sometimes rational. The Unsaid Brood may strip limits from the party's terms. A rival claimant may try to teach the Mouth exclusive royal obedience. Deep Rank Wardens may attempt to seal the threshold. The Long Listener may reproduce a prior uncontrolled attack until someone changes the pattern.

Combat changes the negotiation:

- repeated weapon rhythms become an offering of conflict;
- collapsing terrain can mark a boundary;
- a protected retreat line demonstrates return;
- sacrificing a black-water pearl can interrupt learned cadence;
- Refusal can deny one repeated pattern; and
- Sable can consume contagious panic before the Mouth learns it as Harrowgate's voice.

Manifestations can be wounded and local structures destroyed. The fault survives; violence only makes future contact difficult, dangerous, or differently shaped.

## Queen Avarra below

The Long Listener recognizes royal cadence before it recognizes Avarra as a person. If the retained will is reconstructed, Witness can show the distinction between her original error, her later surrender, and the machine built afterward. Refusal can end the assumption that every Crown bearer speaks for her. Measure can compare proposed returns without deciding that efficiency equals justice.

Avarra may offer her retained royal cadence for unbinding. Doing so ends her ability to command the Mouth and weakens the Crown's old authority. She regards this as freedom if the decision is hers and as execution if imposed by a claimant suppressing Refusal.

If only part of her will is present, the settlement reflects that mutilation. Measure alone creates an efficient but indifferent exchange. Refusal alone can sever the old path without building another. Witness alone may recover truth and memory while leaving pressure unresolved.

## Failure states

- **Unbounded appetite:** the Mouth learns to take a class of memory, sound, or pressure without a stopping condition.
- **Walking cadence:** the learned pattern attaches to a person or carried Crown and follows them away from Harrowgate.
- **False return:** the Mouth gives an apparent benefit whose cost appears elsewhere or later.
- **Borrowed face:** the Long Listener stabilizes around a speaker and begins being treated as that person.
- **Deep closure:** the threshold collapses, trapping the party or sealing the Mouth after an incomplete exchange.
- **Royal recurrence:** a claimant establishes exclusive Crown cadence and revives the possibility of sovereign fault command.

Failure creates a campaign problem with a known origin and pattern; annihilation is unnecessary.

## Treasure and salvage

The Mouth can yield fault glass, living chain, returned memories, future-tremor pearls, and altered command metal. Each treasure embodies a term of exchange. Removing it without understanding that term may continue the settlement through the carrier.

The greatest treasure is a changed relation between Harrowgate and the fault. It cannot be sold without also transferring duty.

## Returning upward

A settlement is not complete until it is enacted through the Deep Bell, Black Rain gates, Iron Choir, civic infrastructure, or landscape. The party must return, communicate the terms, and survive the final transfer. If the route closes, allies above may need to interpret the last demonstrated pattern without explanation.

The Mouth may provide a return path shaped by the agreement: a clear-water column, a living chain, a corridor of restored memories, or a fault opening in the quarry. A failed or predatory exchange may return the party somewhere the Mouth considers equivalent rather than where they intended.

## Carry-forward states

Record:

- entry route and whether it remains open;
- first pattern offered and how it was corrected;
- Unsaid Brood and Long Listener behavior;
- offering, boundary, return, witnesses, and failure condition;
- memories, pressure, Crown cadence, or people committed;
- Avarra faculty involvement and any royal unbinding;
- provisional tests and the Mouth's interpretations;
- treasure removed and recurring duty attached to it;
- who remains below, if anyone; and
- how the settlement is enacted above.

Keep the Mouth stranger than a person and more responsive than a natural hazard. It offers no escape from responsibility; it makes the bargain visible.

revelations.title: Every petition has a toll
revelations.description: The Hall of Bent Knees can be entered through the processional stair, quarry inspection ledge, or an internal Warden route by declaring a burden the old mechanism recognizes.

revelations.title: The Ropeworks has no single door
revelations.description: The central machinery hub has approaches from the petition hall, quarry-side galleries, Scriptorium, and lower Warden works; no single blocked lift seals it.

revelations.title: The chains are the map
revelations.description: The Chain Scriptorium can be found by following officer galleries, maintenance concordances, muster records, ration chains, or the old chapterhouse plan.

revelations.title: Four boughs feed the buried lights
revelations.description: Oil and warm black water meet in a service basin reachable from the quarry, petition hall, Ropeworks ladders, or Garden conduits.

revelations.title: The saints breathe the Reliquary open
revelations.description: The Reliquary Under Water has a lift, archive register, chapel ledge, and cistern valve route that become usable at different water levels.

revelations.title: The Barracks keeps the inner gate
revelations.description: The Warden garrison can be reached by prisoner stair, anchor bridge, muster record, or ossuary door, providing a durable route toward the deep works.

revelations.title: Roots keep a dry road
revelations.description: The Garden of Teeth is crossed by quarry cracks, lamp conduits, petition drains, and Low Choir root ways that remain above most flood states.

revelations.title: The Low Choir keeps the Feast
revelations.description: Ration records, ossuary guides, Warden service doors, and mourning stairs all point toward the inhabited Feast of Empty Chairs.

revelations.title: The Chapel hangs beneath the nave
revelations.description: The suspended sanctuary can be reached from the archive, flooded reliquary, Low Choir mourning stair, menagerie ceiling crawl, or royal grave's execution return.

revelations.title: The Menagerie lies behind the cages
revelations.description: An optional maintenance gallery of purpose-bred beasts lies behind quarry cages, ossuary transfers, Warden handling doors, and the chapel ceiling crawl.

revelations.title: The Wells do not need the royal lift
revelations.description: The deep weight shafts have approaches from the Ropeworks, Barracks, Inverted Chapel, and Black Rain gallery, so a failed lift does not make repair impossible.

revelations.title: Three lineages lead to the narrow grave
revelations.description: The optional royal tomb can be located through the archive's three lineages, Reliquary niche, Low Choir servants' route, or mortuary walk from the Iron Choir.

revelations.title: The Iron Choir commands the lesser works
revelations.description: The Choir of Iron Tongues can be approached from the Wells, Chapel, royal grave, or Warden command route and controls warnings, valves, brakes, and stored toll-memory.

revelations.title: Black Rain reaches the fault
revelations.description: The lowest reservoir can be reached by lamp conduit, Reliquary culvert, Menagerie throat, Counterweight gallery, or a crack behind the royal grave.

revelations.title: Four roads reach the Bell
revelations.description: The final chamber is accessible from the Iron Choir, Counterweight Wells, Black Rain lower bridge, and royal mortuary walk, but every route depends on the bell's current tension.

revelations.title: The last chamber opens into the Mouth
revelations.description: The optional super-depth can be entered from Black Rain, the Deep Bell, a Menagerie maintenance throat, or the Iron Choir's lowest sounding chamber.

revelations.title: Water, light, and burden govern the house
revelations.description: Every major mechanism transfers one of three loads: black water and pressure, ward-light and stored memory, or physical and legal burden. Operating one system changes at least one other.

revelations.title: The Bell releases pressure
revelations.description: The Deep Bell was built to discharge mountain strain into controlled water and counterweight movement. Its current ringing is dangerous because the chain and sluice sequence is broken.

revelations.title: Orren cut the chain; Maelin split the Company
revelations.description: Factor Orren Saye used an abridged extraction schedule and a concealed possession rider to order the loaded Crown chain cut; Captain Maelin Rook recognized the missing safety sequence and resisted, dividing the expedition during the first failure.

revelations.title: The Wardens divide over continuance and release
revelations.description: The preserved garrison is divided between controlled continuance, lawful release from the old sentence, and literal obedience to orders whose authors are dead.

revelations.title: Every toll takes from the Low Choir
revelations.description: Later custodians routed the bell's mnemonic cost into the labor community below. The Iron Tongues store names and memories lost whenever the bell sounds.

revelations.title: A new burden need not renew Avarra’s sentence
revelations.description: A new burden accepted through the Chapel and fitted at the Wells can make the machine legible without chaining Queen Avarra's crown back into the clapper.

revelations.title: A controlled collapse begins at the quarry vents
revelations.description: Destroying or abandoning the bell need not kill the town, but only if the quarry vents, root sluices, and black-water channels are opened before the main load drops.

revelations.title: The Bell admits several endings
revelations.description: The dungeon supports several coherent finales. Their costs depend on rescued operators, controlled systems, faction bargains, replacement burdens, and evacuation preparations rather than a hidden correct answer.

revelations.title: Ward-light fences and carries memory
revelations.description: Lit branches suppress wick-eaters and make routes legible, but their silver wicks carry future toll-memory toward the Choir of Iron Tongues. Darkening a branch releases what it already holds and changes where the creatures migrate.

revelations.title: The copper saints share breath and water
revelations.description: The six statues share an air-and-water manifold. Their bells, valves, and counterweights can create trapped-air routes, rescue a sealed survivor, or stabilize the chamber locally without draining all its pressure into Black Rain.

revelations.title: A civic burden must be voluntary and accepted
revelations.description: The Common Measure can replace the Crown only if voluntary public obligations are assembled in its acceptance collar, recognized at the Inverted Chapel, balanced in the Counterweight Wells, and assigned to living maintainers.

revelations.title: A Warden survives in shell, tablet, and witness
revelations.description: Salt Warden identity is distributed among a preserved body, a memory-and-duty tablet, and witnesses who recognize their continuity. Damage, transfer, repair, and release therefore require choices about consent and uncertainty rather than simple replacement of a component.

revelations.title: Command requires claim, muster, and duty
revelations.description: The Barracks command chair recognizes three independent forms: a command claim embodied in a tablet, witnessed assent from the ranks, and a defined duty the buried house can test. Emergency or joint commands are possible without unanimous agreement.

revelations.title: The Garden feeds on death and feeds the living
revelations.description: The ossuary beds are simultaneously a food source, black-water filter, mnemonic catch, and route network. Burning, flooding, harvesting, or preserving the Garden changes Low Choir survival and the state of neighboring regions.

revelations.title: The root sluices save the town by spending the Garden
revelations.description: Three Garden shutters can vent fault pressure toward prepared quarry cracks. Modest venting costs routes or memory; opening Last Teeth enables the safest controlled collapse but destroys most food beds, ancestral remains, and filtration.

revelations.title: Memory cups need a willing bearer
revelations.description: A cup can preserve, lend, return, or redirect a witnessed memory. Stable carrying requires consent and temporarily displaces one of the carrier’s own vivid memories.

revelations.title: An inherited name carries chosen duties
revelations.description: The Low Choir uses inherited names to preserve standing, kinship, testimony, and selected obligations after a toll. The bearer explicitly accepts or refuses each duty.

revelations.title: The compact needs six weights
revelations.description: Six concrete obligations can become Common Measure weights. They distribute continuing work and give affected bearers a real response when authority or maintenance fails.

revelations.title: Four brakes and one counterchain turn the Chapel
revelations.description: Two coordinated brakes, or one brake plus an external counterweight, can rotate the sanctuary among inverted, mourning, upright, execution, and dropped states with different routes and hazards.

revelations.title: Acceptance needs authority, consent, term, and remedy
revelations.description: At Upright Hearing, a replacement burden becomes legible only when bounded authority, specific bearer consent, a term and transfer rule, and an enforceable remedy are independently witnessed.

revelations.title: A quiet beast needs appetite, boundary, and return
revelations.description: A Menagerie creature works safely only when an operator names the exact excess it should consume, marks where the work ends, and provides a trail or object that leads it back to a prepared resting place.

revelations.title: Every appetite outlives its task
revelations.description: The Menagerie creatures can consume heat, vibration, loose memory, or contagious alarm, but after the named excess is gone each appetite widens toward nearby lamps, hearts, identities, structures, or decisions.

revelations.title: Three lineages divide royal power
revelations.description: Lady Vey’s blood descent supports royal custody, the Burden Chain distributes operating authority among actual maintainers, and the Ash Witness preserves limits on Avarra’s surrender; none answers every Crown question alone.

revelations.title: The treasury is the Bell’s trust
revelations.description: The Grave’s crown-bars, coin, rights, and contracts can become replacement mass, evacuation funds, Low Choir remedy, or dynastic wealth, so extracting treasure assigns future costs rather than producing free salvage.

revelations.title: The Wells separate mass, path, and timing
revelations.description: A safe counterweight operation needs enough equivalent load, a deliberate chain or community to receive it, and a timed sequence of brakes and water; solving only one of those problems moves the casualty elsewhere.

revelations.title: A dropped Well makes one loss permanent
revelations.description: A Royal, Civic, or Funerary drop can absorb an imminent strain event, but permanently destroys distinct routes, settlement options, resources, or memories; it is a controlled sacrifice rather than a reset.

revelations.title: A command needs source, address, and limit
revelations.description: The Choir reliably accepts a command only when it identifies recognized authority or responsibility, the mechanism or person acted upon, and a duration or stopping condition.

revelations.title: A memory needs identity, recipient, and recognition
revelations.description: The Iron Choir can join a memory only when the fragment is identified, a person or vessel receives it, and a living witness or durable record recognizes where it belongs.

revelations.title: Avarra survives as Measure, Refusal, and Witness
revelations.description: Queen Avarra is not a whole ghost in the Crown. Her capacity to compare burdens, refuse coercion, and remember the surrender survives in separable faculties that can be reconstructed or misused apart.

revelations.title: Pressure moves; it does not vanish
revelations.description: Every Cistern operation sends strain toward the quarry, Reliquary, Mouth Below, Harrowgate foundations, or another prepared load path. A supposed drain merely conceals its recipient.

revelations.title: Safe venting needs mouths, roots, and sequence
revelations.description: Controlled venting requires surface outlets, Garden shutter preparation, evacuation, and an ordered release; skipping a component buys relief by assigning a specific local disaster.

revelations.title: A toll has four phases
revelations.description: The toll has four operational phases. Different repairs, transfers, rescues, and extractions are safest in different windows, and prepared systems can delay or reshape the cycle.

revelations.title: The Crown cannot leave its load behind
revelations.description: The Crown is both authority and physical burden. Clean removal requires a replacement, distributed paths, a permanent sacrifice, controlled collapse, or a Mouth settlement; otherwise the load strikes the nearest open route.

revelations.title: A Mouth bargain needs offering, boundary, and return
revelations.description: The Mouth learns repeated exchanges rather than human intent. A durable settlement must enact what recurs, what the phenomenon may affect, and what Harrowgate receives when the pattern is kept.

clues.discovery: Share a meal, inspect the ration ledgers, or ask which Garden route supplied the current food and water.

clues.discovery: Follow the gardener cuts and whispered names through the roots toward The Feast of Empty Chairs.

clues.title: The Feast of Empty Chairs on the muster chain

clues.discovery: Read the drowned salvage notches on the saint associated with The Inverted Chapel.

clues.title: Low Choir place record: Inverted Chapel
clues.description: Mourning guides mark the safe stair to the Chapel’s Mourning Brake and record which sanctuary states preserve the route.
clues.discovery: Ask Merrit’s household how food and water reach him or inspect the mourning-response board.

clues.discovery: Match the keeper’s return tag to the handling passage marked for The Inverted Chapel.

clues.discovery: Follow the numbered rungs, cut hoist marks, and Company chalk toward The Menagerie of Quiet Beasts.

clues.discovery: Read the route table, inspect the lower stations, or rotate far enough to expose both approaches.
