clues.title: Petition plate: The dungeon is governed by water, light, and burden
clues.description: The petition wall states that water carries weight, light remembers the way, and the chain decides who pays.
clues.discovery: Read the burden symbols beneath the statues or test an alternate declaration at the scale.

clues.title: Ropeworks load tally: The dungeon is governed by water, light, and burden
clues.description: The three drums visibly transfer hydraulic, mnemonic, and physical loads whenever one brake moves.
clues.discovery: Inspect the drum labels, bridge anchors, or Pell Varo's surviving control notes.

clues.title: Hanging concordance: The dungeon is governed by water, light, and burden
clues.description: Maintenance concordances classify every plate under water, light, or burden and cross-reference changes between them.
clues.discovery: State the relevant duty at the reading post and follow the chain family it presents.

clues.title: Lamplighter service line: The dungeon is governed by water, light, and burden
clues.description: The lamp-tree brightens only when water pressure and a weighted oil float remain within paired limits.
clues.discovery: Trace oil pipes, wick labels, and maintenance arrows beneath the cistern lip.

clues.title: Chapterhouse survey: The toll is a pressure release, not a summons
clues.description: Tarrow's survey shows ridge strain dropping immediately after each toll, then rebuilding as the damaged machinery slips.
clues.discovery: Compare Tarrow's stakes, the floor crack, and the returned expedition notes.

clues.title: Quarry service marks: The toll is a pressure release, not a summons
clues.description: The breathing shelf exhales in the same phase as buried strain releases, while fresh cracks close slightly after a toll.
clues.discovery: Examine the old rung numbers, snapped hoist, or Ember Company route chalk.

clues.title: Well balance inscription: The toll is a pressure release, not a summons
clues.description: Balance inscriptions describe the great sounding as the final step in transferring accumulated mountain load.
clues.discovery: Compare hanging weights, chain angles, and the maintenance bridge numbers.

clues.title: Faultkeeper gauge: The toll is a pressure release, not a summons
clues.description: Faultkeeper gauges mark each lawful toll as a controlled rise in black water and fall in stone pressure.
clues.discovery: Read pressure vanes, upward rain, and the marked lower galleries.

clues.title: The old exhaust bruises beneath the sounding rail
clues.description: Each lawful impact scar aligns with a drop in the Crown gauge and a surge into the water and counterweight lines. The Bell was built to discharge strain, not to call anything upward.
clues.discovery: Inspect the frame between phases and compare the bruises with the surviving pressure marks.

clues.title: Quarry service marks: The Ember Company cut the Queen's chain and split itself
clues.description: Jessa Noll names Orren's order, Captain Rook's refusal, and Orren's claim that the outer chain was only a release restraint; she also identifies the party that left for the royal grave after the cut.
clues.discovery: Examine the old rung numbers, snapped hoist, or Ember Company route chalk.

clues.title: Ropeworks load tally: The Ember Company cut the Queen's chain and split itself
clues.description: The severed link, two opposed sets of boot marks, Pell Varo's account, and the complete three-drum sequence show that Orren ordered a loaded chain cut from a copy missing its unload and synchronization lines.
clues.discovery: Inspect the drum labels, bridge anchors, or Pell Varo's surviving control notes.

clues.title: Hanging concordance: The Ember Company cut the Queen's chain and split itself
clues.description: Orren's copied schedule preserves the Crown release command but omits the Crown unload, Water-forward, and Memory-brake prerequisites; his removed contract plate shows he was racing public notice.
clues.discovery: State the relevant duty at the reading post and follow the chain family it presents.

clues.title: Royal mortuary seal: The Ember Company cut the Queen's chain and split itself
clues.description: Royal-seal scratches, Rhun's accelerated-possession rider, and abandoned Ember Company tools show Orren's faction continued toward the coffin after the split rather than returning to repair the loaded chain.
clues.discovery: Open or examine the coffin fittings, succession defenses, or hammered-gold wall text.

clues.title: Petition plate: The Salt Wardens disagree whether duty requires repair or release
clues.description: Vesra openly describes Continuance, Release, and literal-obedience positions before granting passage.
clues.discovery: Read the burden symbols beneath the statues or test an alternate declaration at the scale.

clues.title: Warden muster route: The Salt Wardens disagree whether duty requires repair or release
clues.description: The empty command chair stands between two opposed duty boards, while sealed orders still direct a third group.
clues.discovery: Consult a salt tablet, command board, or the inner-gate duty roster.

clues.title: Root-way memory: The Salt Wardens disagree whether duty requires repair or release
clues.description: Missing salt tablets contain erased votes from Wardens who tried to end the old sentence decades earlier.
clues.discovery: Follow gardener cuts, whispered names, or black-water flow through the bone beds.

clues.title: Iron-tongue command: The Salt Wardens disagree whether duty requires repair or release
clues.description: Separate command tongues carry Vesra's repair order, Dalca's release petition, and the dead king's unrevoked prohibition.
clues.discovery: Touch or sound the tongue carrying the relevant maintenance memory.

clues.title: Hanging concordance: Every toll steals memory from the Low Choir
clues.description: Later maintenance plates reroute mnemonic discharge from civic witnesses to the labor galleries beneath the Feast hall.
clues.discovery: State the relevant duty at the reading post and follow the chain family it presents.

clues.title: Low Choir place record: Every toll steals memory from the Low Choir
clues.description: Each newly empty place links a recorded toll to a living person who lost the name, relationship, or sensory anchor preserved in its cup.
clues.discovery: Sit at an empty place, listen to its cup, or compare third-toll losses across several households.

clues.title: Iron-tongue command: Every toll steals memory from the Low Choir
clues.description: Sounding the lesser tongues releases voices identical to memories current Low Choir members have lost.
clues.discovery: Touch or sound the tongue carrying the relevant maintenance memory.

clues.title: Lamplighter service line: Every toll steals memory from the Low Choir
clues.description: Silver wicks brighten with remembered names during each strain pulse and carry them down the Memory lines.
clues.discovery: Trace oil pipes, wick labels, and maintenance arrows beneath the cistern lip.

clues.title: Reliquary salvage mark: The crown can be replaced without restoring Avarra's sentence
clues.description: A copper reliquary contains a rejected design for a civic burden assembled from many voluntary weights rather than one royal captive.
clues.discovery: Search the copper saints, air manifold, or submerged service inscriptions.

clues.title: Chapel execution line: The crown can be replaced without restoring Avarra's sentence
clues.description: The civic acceptance station can recognize a named frame, distributed obligations, and living maintainers without identifying any person or crown as the condemned bearer.
clues.discovery: Bring the acceptance collar to Upright Hearing or compare the civic station with the royal execution rail.

clues.title: Well balance inscription: The crown can be replaced without restoring Avarra's sentence
clues.description: The clapper fittings can receive a different balanced mass if its authority mark is recognized by the control chains.
clues.discovery: Compare hanging weights, chain angles, and the maintenance bridge numbers.

clues.title: Hanging concordance: The crown can be replaced without restoring Avarra's sentence
clues.description: Odran produces three historical replacement proposals and explains why politics, not engineering, prevented their use.
clues.discovery: State the relevant duty at the reading post and follow the chain family it presents.

clues.title: The empty chair kept for the burden
clues.description: The Low Choir compact assigns six transferable duties to an unoccupied place and expressly forbids making any living or dead bearer the property of the office.
clues.discovery: Compare the six-weight board with the empty chair and the inherited-name refusal clauses.

clues.title: The second acceptance collar beside the Crown cage
clues.description: A later collar has six civic sockets, trial-crown fittings, and no dimensions for a human head. Its builders expected the Bell to carry an accepted burden without reinstalling Avarra as its captive clapper.
clues.discovery: Compare the unused collar with the Crown cage, the Common Measure design, or the trial segments.

clues.title: Chapterhouse survey: Harrowgate can survive a controlled collapse only if the quarry vents open
clues.description: Tarrow's surface model shows a survivable load path through the eastern quarry only if streets above the old vents are cleared.
clues.discovery: Compare Tarrow's stakes, the floor crack, and the returned expedition notes.

clues.title: Root-way memory: Harrowgate can survive a controlled collapse only if the quarry vents open
clues.description: The root sluices lead toward sealed quarry vents and can spread a sudden pressure wave through expendable bone beds.
clues.discovery: Follow gardener cuts, whispered names, or black-water flow through the bone beds.

clues.title: Faultkeeper gauge: Harrowgate can survive a controlled collapse only if the quarry vents open
clues.description: Fault gauges specify the sequence: open quarry vents, lower black water, then drop the civic weight before the royal frame.
clues.discovery: Read pressure vanes, upward rain, and the marked lower galleries.

clues.title: Quarry service marks: Harrowgate can survive a controlled collapse only if the quarry vents open
clues.description: Fresh fractures reveal that the cleft already acts as a partial vent and could be widened deliberately after evacuation.
clues.discovery: Examine the old rung numbers, snapped hoist, or Ember Company route chalk.

clues.title: Ropeworks load tally: The bell can be stabilized, silenced, claimed, or destroyed
clues.description: Pell Varo distinguishes temporary stabilization, replacement operation, controlled severance, and total frame demolition as different jobs.
clues.discovery: Inspect the drum labels, bridge anchors, or Pell Varo's surviving control notes.

clues.title: Low Choir place record: The bell can be stabilized, silenced, claimed, or destroyed
clues.description: The four household positions name distinct prices for temporary continuance, replacement, evacuation and collapse, royal disposition, or permanent silence.
clues.discovery: Ask each household what outcome it can support and what resource or obligation that support requires.

clues.title: Bell-frame witness mark: The bell can be stabilized, silenced, claimed, or destroyed
clues.description: The chamber's four approach stations correspond to repair, replacement, royal claim, and controlled drop procedures.
clues.discovery: Inspect the approach brackets, clapper cage, or names cut into the surviving chains.

clues.title: Returned echo: The bell can be stabilized, silenced, claimed, or destroyed
clues.description: Returned echoes suggest the underlying phenomenon can be bargained with or fed directly, creating a fifth dangerous alternative.
clues.discovery: Listen from the lowest sounding ledge and compare the echo with a known route or name.

clues.title: Six mutually exclusive closure writs
clues.description: The archive preserves separate lawful forms for continuance, replacement, divided maintenance, controlled collapse, Crown release, and a settlement below. Each saves a different interest and voids a different protection.
clues.discovery: Open the chained closure case and sort its writs by consequence rather than date.

clues.title: The ring of six dispositions beneath the judgment rail
clues.description: The Chapel can recognize continuance, replacement, distribution, release, sacrificial collapse, or referral to the deep settlement. No inscription names one disposition as the final or pure judgment.
clues.discovery: Bring the Chapel to Upright Hearing and read the underside of the judgment rail.

clues.title: The manifold’s consequence ledger
clues.description: The four gutters and two sealed returns are indexed to distinct end states: continued service, a replacement load, distributed strain, controlled ruin, royal release, or a bounded exchange with the Mouth.
clues.discovery: Read the gutter collars while shifting one small test pulse through the manifold.

clues.title: Senn’s silver-wick ledger
clues.description: Senn’s branch ledger records both creature suppression and the names carried away through each silver line, showing that protection and mnemonic extraction are the same operation.
clues.discovery: Earn Senn’s cooperation, inspect the ceramic comb, or release one branch’s stored memories.

clues.title: Condemnation of the first lamplighters
clues.description: A condemned plate orders lamplighters to conceal that the ward network transmits memory as well as light and warns that full darkness releases the wick-eaters into adjoining routes.
clues.discovery: Follow the Memory chain family or lower the plates filed under concealed operating costs.

clues.title: Wick-eater migration scars
clues.description: Pale feeding scars cluster exactly where the Ossuary lamps end, while whispered names gather in the silver root mesh beneath the lit beds.
clues.discovery: Examine the boundary between living roots and dark bone beds or question a gardener who remembers the last outage.

clues.title: Iron Tongue lamp intake
clues.description: The lesser bells receive a distinct mnemonic line from every lamp bough and fall silent whenever that branch is extinguished.
clues.discovery: Trace the silver cords behind a speaking tongue or compare stored voices against the lamp intake register.

clues.title: Mourning-bough bell line
clues.description: The Mourning feed includes a bellows line marked with six saint symbols, each paired to an air return and a local water gate.
clues.discovery: Trace the darkened Mourning Bough beneath the basin lip or have Senn name its six terminal stations.

clues.title: Water Drum saint-manifold tally
clues.description: Pell’s surviving tally distinguishes the Reliquary’s local saint valves from the main Water Drum, proving the room can be stabilized without a full lower drain.
clues.discovery: Inspect the water-load labels or ask Pell how the trapped salvage team could still be breathing.

clues.title: The six-saint manifold
clues.description: Air moves from one copper mouth to the next as water shifts between hollow bodies, and the Kneeling Saint’s position changes the level without opening the main culvert.
clues.discovery: Speak with Rhea, operate two saints together, or inspect the gridded floor beneath the central pair.

clues.title: Liturgy of the breathing saints
clues.description: The Breath Brake liturgy names all six Reliquary saints as local pressure stations and records how their shared breath protected workers during reversals.
clues.discovery: Read the copper response lines, operate the hydraulic clutch, or ask Merrit to recite the mourning response.

clues.title: The Common Measure design
clues.description: Design plates beside Rhea show seventy-two voluntary civic weights fitted into one copper acceptance collar, then recognized at the Chapel and balanced at the Wells.
clues.discovery: Open the Saint of Returning Breath, recover the folded collar, or assemble the rack in the Saint of Many Hands.

clues.title: Judgment rejecting the Common Measure
clues.description: The rejection judgment admits that the civic design balanced correctly but refuses to treat distributed consent as equal to royal authority.
clues.discovery: Search the replacement-burden chain family or ask Odran for alternatives the kings refused rather than alternatives that failed.

clues.title: Low Choir household weights
clues.description: Households keep small duty weights under the empty chairs and record the living people who voluntarily maintain each obligation.
clues.discovery: Inspect the six compact weight families, witness a household decision, or ask Nara who may consent for each weight.

clues.title: Chapel station for an accepted frame
clues.description: The civic station fits the Common Measure collar and refuses to pass its load until the actual contributors’ consent, term, and remedy have been witnessed.
clues.discovery: Raise the Chapel to Upright Hearing and test the collar with one voluntary weight.

clues.title: The threefold continuity demonstration
clues.description: Heth Brine demonstrates that a shell retains reflex, a brined tablet retains record, and neither receives recognized standing until witnesses rejoin them.
clues.discovery: Observe a repair in the salt room, question Heth, or examine the disputed relief shells.

clues.title: Tablet transfer precedents
clues.description: Maintenance plates record successful and failed Warden transfers, repeatedly distinguishing body continuity, tablet record, and witnessed identity.
clues.discovery: Lower the personhood precedents, compare relief-shell serials, or ask Odran why some transferred names remained disputed.

clues.title: Tablets speaking without shells
clues.description: Quoin, Ora, and Maston can speak from rooted tablets, yet the Garden and Barracks mechanisms treat their words as testimony rather than embodied command.
clues.discovery: Cool the Bitter Bed, draw one tablet into clean brine, or listen through the silver roots.

clues.title: A pallbearer’s recognition record
clues.description: A copper saint record accepts a transferred Warden only after two workers identify the person and the Warden repeats a chosen duty in the new shell.
clues.discovery: Inspect the Pallbearer’s service marks, compare acceptance collars, or ask Rhea about preserved operators she treated.

clues.title: The command chair’s three recognitions
clues.description: The empty chair has separate fittings for a command tablet, rank-witness cords, and a duty plumb that tests whether an order has defined limits.
clues.discovery: Examine the chair, attempt a claim, or have a faction leader explain why no single token now commands the room.

clues.title: Petition for an emergency marshal
clues.description: A surviving petition form allows a living guest to accept a narrow command duty when two Warden ranks witness the appointment.
clues.discovery: Balance the military petitions, search rejected emergency forms, or ask the Hall what authority follows a declared burden.

clues.title: Muster load lines
clues.description: Three color-coded tension lines show that lower Warden controls respond separately to command claim, crew assent, and the physical duty assigned.
clues.discovery: Trace the muster lines from the royal drum, compare Pell’s diagrams, or operate a Barracks lift under conflicting orders.

clues.title: Quoin’s incomplete release-clause testimony
clues.description: Quoin’s damaged tablet remembers that command could pass through a witnessed emergency duty and that accepted replacement would trigger a final muster, though the deciding vote is missing.
clues.discovery: Read Quoin in cool brine, repair one crack, or follow command phrases through the Quiet Loam.

clues.title: The three-bed working
clues.description: The Jaw Catch removes physical waste, the Silver Root catches names and duties, and the Quiet Loam cools water while growing food.
clues.discovery: Work beside Edda, follow one water pulse through all three beds, or inspect the filter cuts and harvest marks.

clues.title: Lantern filter-return account
clues.description: Senn’s basin accounts distinguish unfiltered black water, Garden-gray water, and memory-laden return flow, proving the Garden protects both lamps and drinking supplies.
clues.discovery: Compare separator samples, read the Ossuary return marks, or ask Senn what happens when the Garden inlet is isolated.

clues.title: Toothcap ration ledger
clues.description: The Warm Table counts Garden harvest in household-days of food and clean-water batches and shows exactly what rescue, rest, or evacuation will consume.
clues.discovery: Share the last bowl, inspect the oven ledger, or ask Bera what is lost when a Garden bed is harvested or burned.

clues.title: Gray-water service mark
clues.description: A saint manifold labels Garden-filtered gray water as suitable for air bells and surgery, while untreated fault water is barred from both.
clues.discovery: Read the Returning Breath manifold, compare water samples with Rhea, or trace the service conduit toward the ossuary.

clues.title: The three root pressure shutters
clues.description: Upper Jaw, Widow’s Run, and Last Teeth vent progressively more pressure while sacrificing quarry space, stored memory, or the Garden itself.
clues.discovery: Reach the upper roots, inspect Edda’s shutter slate, or test the paired handles with a crew or harness.

clues.title: Survey of sacrificial quarry vents
clues.description: Tarrow’s survey and fresh cracks show three Garden outlets reaching expendable galleries, lower streets, and the ridge face at sharply different human costs.
clues.discovery: Compare surface stakes with the exposed root pipes, question a quarry worker, or climb to the blocked vent mouths.

clues.title: The root stage in the collapse sequence
clues.description: Fault-release diagrams require the Garden shutters to accept the first pressure wave before the quarry vents and Black Rain spillway can carry the rest.
clues.discovery: Read the collapse sequence, inspect lower shutter linkages, or compare fault pulses with Garden-root timing.

clues.title: The Last Teeth control line
clues.description: A severed emergency line once let the Ropeworks open the Garden’s final pressure shutter after stores and people had been evacuated.
clues.discovery: Trace the green-black emergency cable, repair its drum connection, or ask Pell which distant load it was meant to release.

clues.title: Cupkeeper’s willing exchange
clues.description: A cupkeeper listens, witnesses, carries, and returns a route memory while naming the personal recollection set aside during the transfer.
clues.discovery: Ask how a cup is used, volunteer to carry a harmless memory, or help return one to its owner.

clues.title: Lamp-basin memory decanting marks
clues.description: Marks beside the lamp basins distinguish listening, voluntary carrying, vessel return, and the dangerous scatter produced by a broken cup.
clues.discovery: Inspect the memory separators, question Senn, or release one stored fragment deliberately.

clues.title: Copper relief of a cup transfer
clues.description: A saint-station relief shows a volunteer drinking a memory while another recollection is held in the Returning Breath until the borrowed memory comes back.
clues.discovery: Drain the Open Palm station, compare the relief with a memory vessel, or ask Rhea about mnemonic displacement.

clues.title: Silver-root nest for returned memories
clues.description: The Silver Root holds cracked cups beside named witness cords and rejects memories poured from unwilling or incoherent carriers.
clues.discovery: Work with Edda, inspect the cup roots, or attempt to stabilize a recovered memory.

clues.title: Nara’s seven-name recital
clues.description: Nara states the duty attached to each inherited name and explicitly refuses the punishment, property, or identity claims that she did not accept.
clues.discovery: Ask Nara what her title means or witness a household inheritance.

clues.title: Inheritance limitation plate
clues.description: A chained amendment says a carried name preserves standing only for duties and testimony named before witnesses; it does not transfer the former bearer’s whole sentence.
clues.discovery: Read the condemned-name chain family or ask Odran for later Low Choir amendments.

clues.title: Warden record of a witnessed duty-name
clues.description: A muster tablet recognizes a Low Choir duty-name for route testimony while denying that the bearer inherits the dead worker’s rank or punishment.
clues.discovery: Inspect route-witness tablets, question Vesra or Dalca, or conduct a command muster involving a Low Choir witness.

clues.title: Name-brine return choice
clues.description: Garden keepers return a caught name by asking which relationship or obligation the recipient chooses to restore rather than imposing every trace at once.
clues.discovery: Recover a name from the Silver Root or help restore a relationship taken by the Garden.

clues.title: Board of six compact weights
clues.description: The Feast displays six labeled weight families and records which households will contribute to each obligation under which conditions.
clues.discovery: Negotiate with the household positions, inspect the weights under the chairs, or ask what a surface promise must contain.

clues.title: Gaps in the public commission
clues.description: Marr’s commission can cover rescue, temporary passage, records, and immediate maintenance, but permanent provision, limits, and remedy require additional public commitments.
clues.discovery: Compare the commission with Low Choir demands or ask Marr exactly which obligations he can bind.

clues.title: Six obligation sockets in the Common Measure
clues.description: The Common Measure collar has six independent weight sockets, each linked to a separate maintenance and release notation rather than one undifferentiated civic promise.
clues.discovery: Recover and assemble the Common Measure components or compare the collar with the Pilgrim’s Yoke.

clues.title: Command duty with a revocation remedy
clues.description: Quoin’s release clause treats witness, maintenance limits, and a defined remedy as distinct conditions of lawful continued service.
clues.discovery: Restore Quoin, inspect the empty chair records, or ask Dalca why an accepted duty must include release.

clues.title: Five-state pivot diagram
clues.description: The brake plates diagram Inverted Rest, Mourning Turn, Upright Hearing, Execution Turn, and Dropped Nave, with route and load changes at each arrest point.
clues.discovery: Inspect two brake houses, question Elra, or rotate the sanctuary far enough to expose the state marks.

clues.title: Chapel synchronizing line
clues.description: A four-colored line bundle once let the Ropeworks synchronize adjacent Chapel brakes and substitute a drum load for the Wells counterchain.
clues.discovery: Trace the chapel lines, repair the speaking line, or ask Pell which distant pivot the bundle controlled.

clues.title: Concordance of Chapel brake roles
clues.description: A route family links Mourner, Breather, Judge, and Servant brake houses to the fifth counterchain descending into the Wells.
clues.discovery: Read the Chapel maintenance chain family or ask Odran how the sanctuary was turned without royal authority.

clues.title: Water clutch for the Breath Brake
clues.description: The Chapel ledge contains a hydraulic clutch that can act as one pivot brake or provide temporary counterweight when the Reliquary is held at middle water.
clues.discovery: Operate the Breathing Saint, expose the Chapel ledge, or follow the copper pressure line.

clues.title: Four declaration stations
clues.description: At Upright Hearing, the stations separately demand bounded authority, named bearer consent, duration and transfer terms, and an enforceable remedy.
clues.discovery: Raise the Chapel upright, study the civic station, or conduct even a partial acceptance test.

clues.title: Four response marks on the Pilgrim’s Yoke
clues.description: The transfer yoke records four separate Chapel responses and warns that a missing remedy converts excess strain into a search for a living substitute.
clues.discovery: Examine the Pilgrim’s Yoke, fit it to the acceptance collar, or ask Rhea to read its mnemonic warning.

clues.title: Warden precedent for bounded duty
clues.description: A lawful emergency command names its issuing authority, assenting ranks, term, and release condition—the same four-part form the Chapel uses for civic burdens.
clues.discovery: Resolve a command claim, inspect Quoin’s release clause, or compare guest-marshal limits with Chapel records.

clues.title: Low Choir acceptance rehearsal
clues.description: Household witnesses rehearse four answers and stop whenever a speaker substitutes broad goodwill for specific consent, term, or remedy.
clues.discovery: Ask the Kept Chain to prepare the Common Measure or observe a household deciding whether to contribute a weight.

clues.title: A burden accepted without an ending clause
clues.description: A brass case records a petition with valid authority and witnessed assent but no term, transfer rule, or remedy. The scale accepted the burden and kept the petitioner kneeling until her heirs supplied all three omissions.
clues.discovery: Lift the third rejected petition plate and compare its paired verdict tabs.

clues.title: Menagerie three part keeper plates
clues.description: Three keeper plates repeat the same release sequence: present a named appetite, close the work inside a visible boundary, and maintain a return trail to a prepared resting place.
clues.discovery: Read the brass operating plates beside the central gong or have Hollis Fen explain why the cages stand open.

clues.title: Garden beast transfer lines
clues.description: Garden transfer rings combine food or waste lures, silver-root boundary cords, and keeper scent pads, showing that even useful maintenance creatures need a defined end and way home.
clues.discovery: Inspect the Menagerie refuse tunnel or ask Edda how Garden keepers once borrowed living tools.

clues.title: Chapel maintenance instrument appeal
clues.description: An appeal-wing procedure recognizes a living maintenance instrument only when its appetite, operating bounds, and responsible return keeper are declared separately.
clues.discovery: Present a beast route to an appeal wing, read the maintenance appeal strip, or inspect the ceiling-crawl threshold.

clues.title: Quarry hunter lure and retreat pattern
clues.description: Old quarry chalk around the lamp hunter’s route pairs a heat lure with cold boundary marks and a dark retreat slot, preserving the same three-part handling logic outside the formal Menagerie.
clues.discovery: Compare Tarrow’s marks with the cage tunnel signs or reconstruct the hunter’s repeated route.

clues.title: Menagerie starvation behavior ledger
clues.description: The keeper ledger distinguishes each creature’s trained appetite from starvation behavior: heat turns toward bodies, vibration toward hearts, loose memory toward names, and alarm toward bodily pulse.
clues.discovery: Recover Hollis’s ledger, read the cage inscriptions, or observe a beast after its named target is exhausted.

clues.title: Lantern cinderback ward warning
clues.description: A lamp-service warning says heat-eaters can save a burning basin but will consume the nearest ward branch unless two cold boundaries remain after the fire dies.
clues.discovery: Read Senn’s restricted-creature plate or ask why the Menagerie conduit has two shutoffs.

clues.title: Feast sable consent account
clues.description: A Low Choir account praises a glass sleeper for preventing a toll panic and condemns the keeper who left workers calm enough to accept an unsafe second shift.
clues.discovery: Listen to the Open Cup testimony or find the gray-wool memory cup kept behind the Narrow Table.

clues.title: Scriptorium living tool liability chain
clues.description: A maintenance chain assigns liability for what a beast consumes after its declared work ends, proving that useful appetite was always expected to create a secondary hazard.
clues.discovery: Follow the Menagerie liability family or ask Odran Greve to translate the keeper clauses.

clues.title: Grave three genealogy plates
clues.description: The Golden Branch, Burden Chain, and Ash Witness open different mechanisms and explicitly label their jurisdictions as custody, maintained obligation, and surrender limits.
clues.discovery: Enter the succession vestibule and activate, copy, or compare the three standing plates.

clues.title: Scriptorium genealogy concordance
clues.description: The chained genealogy index sends royal goods to the Golden Branch, operating authority to the lead Burden Chain, and Crown-release testimony to the hidden Ash Witness.
clues.discovery: Complete the genealogy chain family or compare its three material indexes.

clues.title: Feast narrow line three standings
clues.description: Illa Crownless distinguishes a descendant’s right to speak for royal goods, a maintainer’s right to govern the machine, and a witness line’s right to limit Avarra’s release.
clues.discovery: Earn the Narrow Line’s genealogy recital or ask why Nara refuses to name one rightful heir.

clues.title: Barracks three claim jurisdictions
clues.description: A Warden succession precedent says blood can establish custody, completed duty can establish operating command, and preserved testimony can restrict both without merging them.
clues.discovery: Read the royal-custody muster tablet or obtain Quoin, Vesra, or Dalca’s legal interpretation.

clues.title: Grave maintenance trust inventory
clues.description: The treasury inventory divides crown-bars, evacuation coin, quarry rights, resettlement obligations, and ceremonial goods, with each withdrawal assigned to a future maintenance account.
clues.discovery: Open the maintenance trust compartment or audit the records of debt behind Aldren’s coffin.

clues.title: Chapterhouse buried trust debt
clues.description: Marr’s emergency books show Harrowgate borrowing for decades against a buried royal maintenance trust while budgeting no accessible reserve for the bell or Low Choir.
clues.discovery: Compare town debt books, Lady Vey’s recovery trust, and Tarrow’s unfunded repair estimates.

clues.title: Wells crown bar dual use scales
clues.description: The Civic distributor measures each Grave crown-bar as both compatible counterweight mass and a marked maintenance contribution that can no longer fund surface work once installed.
clues.discovery: Test a crown-bar or read the distributor’s financial and load markings.

clues.title: Feast resettlement fund claim
clues.description: Low Choir compact drafts identify the buried trust as a possible source for passage, provision, and remedy rather than treating all royal gold as a claimant’s private inheritance.
clues.discovery: Review Nara’s compact weights or Bera’s costed resettlement and food transition plan.

clues.title: Wells three measure house gauges
clues.description: The Measure House displays physical mass, receiving path, and brake timing on separate gauges; a green reading on one does not conceal a dangerous reading on another.
clues.discovery: Operate the Measure House, conduct a small test, or have Pell, Elra, or a Warden crew interpret the gauges.

clues.title: Ropeworks load path before weight
clues.description: The three Ropeworks drums can hold equal loads while sending strain into different routes, and their timing marks show that a correct weight released on the wrong beat still shocks the bell.
clues.discovery: Compare drum plumbs, line colors, and brake windows during any transfer.

clues.title: Chapel recognition without balance
clues.description: A successful Chapel acceptance opens the Wells transfer door but leaves physical load and timing tests unresolved, proving that recognized authority supplies a path rather than sufficient mass or safe sequence.
clues.discovery: Complete or inspect an acceptance test and follow the counterchain response into the Wells.

clues.title: Reliquary water mass out of phase
clues.description: The copper saints can supply enough water mass to steady a well, but their manifold warns that out-of-phase delivery drives the same load into the Funerary chain and Black Rain.
clues.discovery: Read the Many Hands manifold or test a saint-assisted counterweight pulse.

clues.title: Wells three drop consequence plates
clues.description: Separate emergency plates show a Royal drop destroying crown routes, a Civic drop destroying distributed-settlement machinery, and a Funerary drop sealing memory while raising lower pressure.
clues.discovery: Open the final-dog housings or read the red emergency plates at each well.

clues.title: Garden last teeth and well drop sequence
clues.description: The Garden collapse sequence pairs Last Teeth with exactly one well drop and warns that the chosen shaft determines whether the permanent loss is royal access, civic infrastructure, or stored memory.
clues.discovery: Recover the root-shutter sequence or compare Quoin’s damaged tablet with the pressure plates.

clues.title: Scriptorium no rehoisting covenant
clues.description: A chain covenant states that a released final counterweight cannot be rehoisted from its sump; later builders must replace the whole route rather than pretend the sacrifice was temporary.
clues.discovery: Follow the emergency descent records or ask Odran about the black-sealed one-way chains.

clues.title: Hall final-weight sacrifice ruling
clues.description: A petition ruling permits a final counterweight release only after naming the route, public work, or memorial record that can never be restored once the weight enters its sump.
clues.discovery: Pay the Hall’s engineering toll, inspect the lower-load precedents, or ask a Warden examiner to interpret the black-sealed ruling.

clues.title: Three empty sockets on the conductor’s dais
clues.description: The speaking rail labels its three sockets SOURCE, ADDRESS, and END in successive historical scripts.
clues.discovery: Examine the dais while the Cantor attempts to complete a malformed command.

clues.title: Limited-command precedents
clues.description: A chain of emergency rulings voids commands that lack a recognized issuer, named mechanism, or stopping condition.
clues.discovery: Follow marginal links among Warden, water, and royal command plates.

clues.title: An order that never named relief
clues.description: A damaged Deep Rank tablet still obeys a centuries-old continuity order because no relief condition was engraved.
clues.discovery: Compare Olt Venn’s order pattern with the Barracks command-chair requirements.

clues.title: The Chapel’s command parallel
clues.description: A brake inscription equates authority with source, burden with address, and remedy or duration with limit.
clues.discovery: Read the underside inscription while the Chapel is in Upright Hearing or Execution Turn.

clues.title: The order that reached every petitioner
clues.description: An emergency order bears a lawful Warden seal and a six-hour limit but names no office or mechanism. The Hall therefore imposed it on every person kneeling before the scale.
clues.discovery: Read the surviving edge of the order and the identical command notches beneath each petition station.

clues.title: Instructions on the joining rail
clues.description: The restoration rail has separate fittings for a named fragment, receiving vessel, and recognizing witness.
clues.discovery: Free Hara or Jori and inspect the memory-work station.

clues.title: A three-person restoration at the Feast
clues.description: A Low Choir household restores a cup only after one person names the memory, one receives it, and one testifies that it belongs.
clues.discovery: Observe or assist a voluntary memory-cup return.

clues.title: Unclaimed memory drifting between lamps
clues.description: Released recollections without a marked recipient migrate into adjacent cups and begin combining.
clues.discovery: Darken a bough or release stored memory without first assigning vessels.

clues.title: The Returning Breath recognition protocol
clues.description: The saint stabilizes a recipient only when another person or record confirms the returning memory’s identity.
clues.discovery: Operate Returning Breath with Rhea Colm or read its drowned instructions.

clues.title: Three royal tongues speaking one divided queen
clues.description: Separate tongues compare burdens, reject commands, and recite surrender terms in Avarra’s voice.
clues.discovery: Reach the royal register and isolate the overlapping voices.

clues.title: The Ash Witness names three retained faculties
clues.description: The genealogy denies that the Crown contains Avarra entire and lists Measure, Refusal, and Witness as separately preserved capacities.
clues.discovery: Read the Ash Witness with a living claimant or copied royal sequence.

clues.title: The order dividing Avarra’s retained will
clues.description: A censored plate records that later custodians separated royal judgment, refusal, and testimony to make the Bell easier to command.
clues.discovery: Rehang the cut royal plates in burden order and read the removed middle links.

clues.title: Three resonances inside the Crown cage
clues.description: The Crown answers the same question with a calculation, a denial, and a remembered scene rather than one unified reply.
clues.discovery: Address Avarra during Crown Descent or sound the three royal fittings separately.

clues.title: Three answers to Avarra’s cadence
clues.description: The same royal cadence returns three unlike answers: a comparison of burdens, a denial of command, and a remembered surrender. The Mouth never returns them as one whole voice.
clues.discovery: Repeat Avarra’s cadence three times with distinct boundaries and compare the replies.

clues.title: The four strain gutters
clues.description: The fault harp remains loud no matter which visible water route is opened; only the recipient changes.
clues.discovery: Compare the water crown and fault harp while operating a spillway.

clues.title: The Reliquary’s black-return cost
clues.description: The saints can separate one surge, but its heat, grit, and memory must enter bodies, storage, or another outlet.
clues.discovery: Trace the lower copper manifold and its six exhaust paths.

clues.title: Pressure sleeping in the roots
clues.description: Closed root shutters preserve the Garden by sending strain onward; opening them spends beds and paths to absorb it.
clues.discovery: Read Edda’s root gauges before and after preparing a shutter.

clues.title: A Wells load change with no water change
clues.description: Moving mass alters the fault harp even when the Cistern level is unchanged, proving visible water is not total pressure.
clues.discovery: Compare the Measure House gauges during a controlled weight transfer.

clues.title: The scar that crosses all three drums
clues.description: One strain mark leaves the Crown Drum, crosses the Water Drum, and ends in the Memory Drum. Setting any one brake still makes the same mark advance across the other two.
clues.discovery: Chalk the three drums and operate one safe catch during a stationary window.

clues.title: The four receivers beneath the clapper
clues.description: Every catch beneath the clapper leads onward—to the Wells, Black Rain, Garden roots, or Harrowgate’s foundations. The frame contains no empty receiver and no route marked away.
clues.discovery: Trace the receiver chains while the cycle is held between Drawing Load and Crown Descent.

clues.title: The pressure knot that returns by another wall
clues.description: A bounded pulse offered through black water returns as heat, stone movement, or borrowed memory. Changing the pattern changes the recipient and form, never the fact of return.
clues.discovery: Enact a small bounded test at the threshold and mark where its answer enters the chamber.

clues.title: The quarry manifold staging plate
clues.description: The six throats are numbered by rising capacity and cross-marked with root shutters and surface clearances.
clues.discovery: Reach the manifold or ask Kesh Arden to reconstruct the sequence.

clues.title: Buried mouths in the quarry survey
clues.description: Old vent ribs continue behind two built-over shelves and one forgotten lime pit.
clues.discovery: Compare the maintenance cleft, loose stone, and old quarry pegs.

clues.title: The Garden’s vent map
clues.description: Root-keeper marks show which beds tear when each quarry throat opens and which shutters must be prepared first.
clues.discovery: Read the root tags at Upper Jaw, Widow’s Run, and Last Teeth.

clues.title: Harrowgate’s evacuation lines over the vents
clues.description: Tarrow’s stakes place houses, streets, and the chapterhouse above the old manifold and identify viable sacrificial zones.
clues.discovery: Overlay the floor crack, quarry plan, and current town map.

clues.title: The condemned venting order
clues.description: A charred order opened the fault sluice before the surface mouths and root shutters were prepared. Later annotators name the buried crews and preserve the corrected order: mouths, roots, evacuation, then rising release.
clues.discovery: Compare the burned order with the red-ink revision chained behind it.

clues.title: The four-phase speaking rail
clues.description: Four notches on the upper rail align with intake, Wells draw, royal lock, and impact.
clues.discovery: Reach the upper control walk and watch one phase begin.

clues.title: The Ropeworks quarter-cycle tally
clues.description: The three drums mark Breath, Load, Descent, and Sounding with different safe transfer operations.
clues.discovery: Reconstruct the tally from drum teeth and the trapped crew’s observations.

clues.title: The Choir’s preparatory recital
clues.description: The continuity sequence issues four sets of commands in a fixed order before every toll.
clues.discovery: Listen across the light, burden, royal, and impact registers.

clues.title: Four brake windows at the Wells
clues.description: Pell Varo’s gauge notes distinguish the safest moments to fit mass, move paths, open royal locks, and survive impact.
clues.discovery: Operate the Measure House or recover Pell’s marked brake sequence.

clues.title: Four changes in the lamp boughs
clues.description: The Processional, Ossuary, Mourning, and Deep boughs change in a fixed sequence: intake brightens them, load bows their flames, Crown Descent draws memory along the silver wicks, and Sounding releases or extinguishes what remains.
clues.discovery: Watch all four boughs through one shortened cycle or compare Senn’s phase notches.

clues.title: Four breath cuts on the saints’ manifold
clues.description: The shared manifold is cut with four ordinal instructions: draw breath, accept weight, receive the Crown line, release. Different saints open at each cut, preserving the Bell’s operating sequence in water and air.
clues.discovery: Pump the Returning Breath line and compare the four cuts across the six saint valves.

clues.title: The Crown cage’s empty-load warning
clues.description: A release inscription states that an unreceived burden falls to foundation, funerary path, or bearer.
clues.discovery: Inspect the six release locks during Crown Descent.

clues.title: The Grave counts the Crown as maintenance mass
clues.description: Treasury ledgers value the Crown both as sovereignty and as the fixed weight anchoring the Royal Well.
clues.discovery: Compare the maintenance trust, crown-bars, and release sequence.

clues.title: The Royal Well’s Crown deficit gauge
clues.description: The gauge shows exactly which other path takes the shock when Crown mass is removed.
clues.discovery: Set the mass, path, and timing gauges for a simulated extraction.

clues.title: Recognition without mass
clues.description: The Chapel can accept a new burden that the Wells still judge physically insufficient, separating lawful transfer from actual load.
clues.discovery: Consecrate a partial frame or read the acceptance warning beneath the altar.

clues.title: The Crown Drum’s displaced-load countermark
clues.description: The Crown tally falls after the outer chain is cut while the Water and Memory tallies rise by the same combined measure. The missing burden moved into the other drums before the first toll.
clues.discovery: Align the before-and-after tally plates with Maelin Rook’s chalk marks.

clues.title: Refusal rejects an unassigned release
clues.description: Avarra’s Refusal tongue will accept “free the Crown” only after the command names where its physical and civic burden goes. Without a recipient, the phrase returns as an accusation rather than an operation.
clues.discovery: Isolate Refusal and test a bounded extraction command without naming a load path.

clues.title: The Crown cadence returns carrying weight
clues.description: A royal rhythm offered without a recipient returns with pressure attached and seizes the nearest open chain. Only a repeated pattern that names another bearer separates Crown from load.
clues.discovery: Offer a safe fragment of the Crown cadence through a tethered token and observe what follows it back.

clues.title: The Mouth’s three-part return pattern
clues.description: The Long Listener stabilizes only after the party repeats what is given, what is excluded, and what comes back.
clues.discovery: Complete or observe three negotiation exchanges below the threshold.

clues.title: The handling law’s deeper analogy
clues.description: Hollis notes that appetite, boundary, and return were copied from older fault-handling instructions, though the Mouth is not a beast.
clues.discovery: Compare the oldest cage plate with the later handler rules.

clues.title: The unbounded Mouth sluice
clues.description: Old warnings say that sending water below without naming duration and return teaches the fault to expect every future surge.
clues.discovery: Read the sluice ribs or witness the result of an uncontrolled opening.

clues.title: The first Mouth cadence record
clues.description: Avarra’s Witness remembers an offering of siege vibration, a failed royal boundary, and a return mistaken for obedience.
clues.discovery: Reconstruct Witness or isolate the oldest royal cadence.
